...how much more that heavenly *Adam*, whom the only-begotten Son of God possesses in himself, ought to have been such.

Therefore, the heavenly, eternal, fundamental, and cornerstone *Jesus Christ* (just as the *Philosophical Stone* has been described in the same way) is and remains of a marvelous generation and origin according to both natures, and is of an inscrutable nature and property. For according to his divine nature, he is from eternity, from the sole divine essence of his heavenly and eternal Father—true God, indeed the Son of God, whose going forth (as the Scripture speaks of this matter) has been from the beginning and from eternity: (*Micah 5, Psalm 2, Matthew 16, Colossians 1*). According to his humanity, however, in the fullness of time he was born without sin or defect (*Isaiah 53, John 8, as Scripture testifies*), a true and perfect man with body and soul together (*Matthew 26*), so that now he has become an indissoluble, personal, and <term>Theandric essence</term> <note>original: *theandricæ essentiæ*; a term from the Greek words for God (*theos*) and man (*aner*), referring to the union of divine and human natures in one person</note>; that is, true God and true man, in one single person, indissoluble for all eternity, and in this way he remains to be acknowledged and worshiped as Almighty God.

It were to be wished here that the eyes of the greater part of the so-called <note>original: *putaticiorum*; meaning "supposed" or "reputed," used here dismissively toward academic theologians</note> doctors were better opened, and their dark spectacles or sophisticated masks were pulled away, so that they might become seeing (*Luke 10*). Especially indeed all the *Aristotelians* <note>Followers of Aristotle’s logic, whom the author views as too literal or rationalistic for spiritual mysteries</note>, and those sophists blind in divine works, among whom so many various disputes are stirred up even to this day in divine matters in a less than Christian manner; there is no end at all to the many kinds of distinctions, divisions, and mixtures concerning that difficult, well-founded, and most venerable article in Holy Scripture (*2 Timothy 3*) regarding the union of Natures and the <term>Communication of Attributes</term> <note>original: *communicatione Idiomatum*; the theological doctrine that the properties of both the divine and human natures belong to the single person of Christ</note> in Christ. But if they are now unwilling to believe God, or his divine word, then they should at least learn from the conjunction and union of the two waters—namely <term>Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, the "volatile" or spirit-like principle</note> and <term>the Sun</term> <note>original: *Solis*; referring to gold, the "fixed" or bodily principle</note>—performed in the often-mentioned <term>Chemical work</term> <note>original: *Chymici operis*; the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note> (as we have mentioned above)...

# EPILOGUE.

You have now, therefore, friend and benevolent Reader, a brief and simple demonstration and declaration, and also an infallible Type and allegorical comparison of the earthly chemist's [stone] and the true heavenly stone of Jesus Christ <note>original: "lapidis Jesu Christi"</note>, through which you will be able to arrive at certain blessedness and perfection, not only here in this earthly way, but also in the eternal one. Although both sides of the matter could have been treated somewhat more correctly and abundantly in the preceding theological work, you must nevertheless know that I am not a Professor of Scripture, nor an <term>Aristotelian-Theologian</term> <note>original: "Aristotelico-Theologum"; this refers to the Scholastic style of theology prevalent in universities that relied heavily on the logic and philosophy of Aristotle</note> after the fashion of today's world, but I am a citizen and a private person. For I attained that knowledge granted to me by God not through studies in any famous Academy, but I learned it in the universal <term>School of Nature</term> <note>original: "Schola naturae"; a concept suggesting that God reveals divine truths through the observation of the natural world</note> (Job 12) and from the great book of miracles (in which all those taught by God have exercised themselves for many centuries before us).

For this reason, I have directed this description of mine not toward elegant and "foot-and-a-half-long" letters <note>original: "sesquipedalemque literam"; a reference to the Roman poet Horace’s phrase for overly long, pretentious words</note>, but, as has been said, toward simplicity. Just as it is not my duty to establish a more fertile and copious treatment of theological matters here, whatever I have done was intended, for my part, to prescribe some brief sketch for those who perhaps have not yet made such great progress, so that they may be able to investigate the Matter <note>The "Matter" refers both to the chemical substance and the spiritual truth of Christ.</note> more deeply. For it seems fitting for every lover of truth by no means to pass over the miracles of God with a "dry foot" <note>original: "sicco pede"; a Latin idiom meaning to pass over something quickly or without paying attention</note>, nor to involve them in perpetual silence, but to celebrate, amplify, and glorify them.

At the same time, I also wished to make a public testimony of my confession, and what I think and believe regarding the articles of the Christian religion. For, alas, it is now so arranged that many pious Christians (Psalm 116) are proclaimed heretics behind their backs and held in suspicion through the untimely judgments of most lying slanderers (unless one is willing to "sing their song" <note>An idiom meaning to agree with their specific sectarian dogmas.</note>). May these impious blasphemies of the world and rash judgments not at all offend the true Christian who is torn apart by such slanders:

Therefore, this point must be considered well; one must not pant after this highest art so greedily and inconsiderately as many are accustomed to do (since often a person who is not at all fit or suitable for that art, nor practiced in the slightest in the aforementioned recognition, will attempt it), unless they desire to experience a shameful end to the matter. For as the beginning is, so usually is the end, as—alas— the reality itself speaks in the case of many. This, however, is to be uniquely imputed to immature intention and ignorance.

Thus may we rightly and well begin the supreme work <note>original: "summum opus"; the "Great Work" of alchemy.</note> which is to be performed by us here, proceed constantly in its labor, and finally complete it in a state of grace, enjoying it with eternal joy. We ask this through that heavenly and eternally established miraculous <term>Cornerstone</term> <note>The author explicitly links the alchemical stone to Jesus Christ, using the biblical metaphor of the "stone the builders rejected."</note>, Jesus Christ, who with you, O God the Father, together with the Holy Spirit—the true God in one indissoluble divine essence—commands and reigns, the <term>Triune God</term> <note>original: "triunicus"; a specific theological term emphasizing the three-in-one nature of the Trinity.</note>, most highly praised for everlasting ages. Amen.

# EPIGRAM

**Gold**; it is a cheap thing to prepare from metals in a furnace.
Sometimes there is someone who is powerful and creates by art.
Why is he not rich? The reason is that one thing is lacking,
Which lies hidden in the art; anxious care weighs down many.
Namely, this gold which is not <term>fixed</term> <note>original: "fix"; in alchemy, "fixing" refers to making a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat so it does not evaporate.</note> when it is tested,
But suddenly, being swift, it flees and perishes.
But he who knows this, and how it may remain <term>fixed</term> and constant 
at all times, so that nothing of the whole is lost:
He is the possessor of the true Art; he is called
A **Philosopher**, a **Chemist**, and a good **Practitioner**.

## ANOTHER

<term>Divine Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Theiosophia"; a term combining the Greek words for God (Theos) and Wisdom (Sophia).</note> flourishes thus when <term>Chemistry</term> <note>original: "Chymia."</note> comes together with her,
No differently than a noble body needs a right hand.
The present image graphically teaches and demonstrates this,
Surely it should be noted by signifying what it shows.
First, look upon the helmet, and the helmet with two wings,
Through which the love of the art is required.
And they denote favor towards <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Sophia."</note> with a hastening step,
Who shines like <term>Phoebus</term> <note>The Greek sun god Apollo; used here to represent the brilliance of the sun or the "solar" nature of the Stone.</note> in the citadel of the sky—
That she is naked of body signifies that she is loved zealously,
For the sake of the soul, before all the riches of the whole world.
He who once sees her, especially with a naked body,
It is difficult for anyone to restrain himself from the Goddess.

# NATURE.

**O** immortal God, how saddened I am when I consider the human race, which God created in His own image and as a perfect work—which, above all other creatures, without the right use of time and reason, recedes so far from me (Nature). I speak here with you as if with a dull <term>Philosophaster</term> <note>original: "Philosophastro" — a disparaging term for a false philosopher or a pretender to scientific knowledge</note>, while you name yourself a <term>Practical Chemist</term> <note>original: "Chimicum Practicum" — one who performs the physical laboratory work of alchemy</note> and a good Philosopher, and yet you are entirely destitute of art, the right matter, theory, knowledge, and recognition of me. Stupid ass, you break glass vessels and burn coals until your head goes mad from the vapors; you cook alum, salt, <term>orpiment</term> <note>original: "auripigmentum" — a deep yellow arsenic sulfide mineral once thought to be a key ingredient for making gold</note>, blackness, and you melt metals; you make small and large furnaces and use many types of vessels. Nonetheless, I am ashamed of your folly, and what is more, you distress me with your foul sulfurous smoke. 

Through your most intense fire you attempt to fix <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum" — mercury. "Fixing" it refers to the alchemical goal of turning liquid mercury into a solid, non-volatile substance</note>, when yet it will only be common and volatile, and not that from which I myself make metals; and thus by this path, unless you walk another, you achieve nothing at all. For you do not use my ways correctly, nor do you understand my craftsmanship. It would be better for you to take care of your own affairs than to dissolve so many frivolous things, distill them, and then congeal them through <term>alembics</term> <note>original: "alembicos" — the "cap" or lid of a still used to collect vapors</note>, <term>cucurbits</term> <note>original: "cucurbitas" — gourd-shaped glass vessels used in distillation</note>, <term>stills</term> <note>original: "distillatoria"</note>, and <term>pelicans</term> <note>original: "pelecanos" — a specialized vessel with two "arms" that feed condensed liquid back into the body, allowing for continuous circulation</note>. You will never make congealed <term>quicksilver</term> in this way. 

For your "vivification" <note>the process of giving "life" or metallic activity to a substance</note> you use a <term>reverberatory furnace</term> <note>original: "reverberatorio" — a furnace that reflects or "reverberates" heat from the roof onto the material being heated</note>, and you keep it so hot until everything flows; in such a manner you complete your work, yet in the end, you destroy both yourself and others with you. You will never find anything in this way unless you enter my smithy, in which I tirelessly forge metals in the interior bowels of the earth; in that place, you will indeed find the matter with which I labor, and the very specimen of my labor.

->### The Demonstration of Nature.<-

Do not think that I will reveal my mystery to you unless you seek the growing grain of metals, animals, and vegetables: all of which are in my power and are preserved in the earth: one as far as generation is concerned, the other as far as nutrition belongs.

Metals merely **EXIST**, vegetables **LIVE** and **GROW**, but animals truly have **SENSORY PERCEPTION**, which is more than merely growing. I create metals, stones, and <term>vitriols</term> <note>original: "attramenta" — literally 'inky substances,' but in alchemical texts this usually refers to metallic sulfates or vitriols used in making pigments and acids</note> from the elements, which I bring into a certain mixture and composition; and you have no need to seek them in any other places than in the womb of the earth. Vegetables preserve their seed and their species within that place. In a similar way, animals also bestow their seed, from which a being similar to themselves is generated. And, briefly, everything satisfies its duty without deception: And you, wicked man, who attempts to perform my office, recede from me, *Nature*, more than all other creatures.

Metals have no life, nor any single nourishment for growing, becoming green, or increasing, since they are made destitute of a birthing seed; for which reason they also do not generate anything like themselves. The first [comes] from the substance of the four elements in nine days: the Moon travels through the twelve celestial signs in twenty-nine and a half days.

Through the different course just mentioned, summer and winter arise, as well as the changes of the elements and the generations of things on the earth: and nothing, whether it be perceptible, visible, or invisible, can exist or subsist without me, without God, and the Heavens. Thus the heavens work all things which are contained under the Moon, and they bestow their influence upon virtue and matter: which, no differently than a woman desires to conceive from a man, desires to receive form. To all the stars, which are innumerable, matters are subject in various numbers, and some of them are bright, while others are dark: this is a miraculous thing. They thus work different things insofar as they have a peculiar course. First above in heaven, and afterwards below, according to their virtue, in the elements, and from there species and individuals are made.

Know therefore, that such manifold influences do not flow down into the element of earth in vain, although it happens in an invisible way, and,

-># *The Demonstration of Nature.*<-

...before they descend into the earth, they are so tightly enclosed within themselves that they even enter one another violently, and in that way break into the center, in such a diverse manner that they produce different generations of minerals through peculiar impressions; and the lower things follow the upper things without error or a straying path. And thus the earth is surrounded and adorned by the heavens, and from them it obtains influence and its most excellent substance. For this reason, any given Sphere is ready to communicate its truth and to permeate its center. 

Through this kind of motion and heat, the vapors rising in the earth—which are the first substances—are generated. Vapor is cold and moist, so that by this logic it may descend downward again and be preserved in the earth; but if it should be turned about in some cloudy cloud, then it can be moist and hot at the same time. That part of it which remains earthly and shut up in the earth, I reduce, in the length of time, into sulfurous matter, which is the **active agent**, and into <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum" — mercury</note>, which is the **passive patient**. Indeed, I repeat this so often for your sake, lest perhaps you err, or begin the practice itself too prematurely in a completely backwards way.

After <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: "putrefactionem" — the stage of decay or breaking down where matter turns black</note> the generation itself occurs, and that through an internal, incombustible heat used to warm the coldness of the quicksilver, which indeed endures so much that it is finally united with its sulfur. ->## *The Demonstration of Nature.*<-

...cold becomes hot, and dry becomes moist and oily. You must note, however, that the moist cannot exist without its dry part, nor the dry without its moist part. For one is preserved by the other in its first essence, which in the elemental essence is the spirit and the <term>quintessence</term> <note>original: "quinta essentia" — the "fifth element" or the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance</note>, from which our "child" <note>An alchemical metaphor for the Philosopher's Stone or the successful result of the work.</note> obtains its birth. Fire gives birth to it and nourishes it in the air, yet beforehand it rots in the virginal earth; then water flows forth, which we must seek out; this is the <term>prime matter</term> <note>original: "prima materia" — the original, formless substance from which all things are created</note> from which I begin my mineral work. For a thing violently resists its opposite, and in such a state it strengthens itself, lest it perhaps be taken away by the worker; and then the "patient" <note>The substance being acted upon in a chemical or alchemical reaction.</note> is transformed and stripped of its form through the "desire" of matter, which unceasingly attracts a new form.

Through my Wisdom I rule the <term>First Moveable</term> <note>original: "primum mobile" — in the traditional geocentric model, the outermost sphere that moves all the inner celestial spheres</note>; my hands are the Eighth Sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars.</note>, just as my father ordained. The matter from which I make my works—such as stones, metals, trees, herbs, rational and irrational animals, and indeed all things in general that are under heaven—I take from the four elements alone. Chaos, or **Hyle** <note>original Greek: "ὕλη" — fundamental, unformed matter</note>, is the first matter. She is the mistress who sustains the King, the Queen, and the entire royal household <note>These are common alchemical personifications for gold (King), silver (Queen), and the accompanying chemicals or processes.</note>. The Knight stands ready at all times to perform services for her, and the Chambermaid performs her duty at her command. The more excellent the form is, the more excellently I represent myself within it. Know, moreover, that I have the power to grant every essence its own being, to preserve them steadily, and to awaken form within matter.

Furthermore, observe closely the three parts into which **GOD** distributed the first matter from the beginning. From the first and purest part, He created the Cherubim, Seraphim, Archangels, and all the other Angels. From the second, not quite as pure part, He created the heavens and their enclosure. But from the third and impure part, He created the elements with their properties. And first indeed he created fire, which excels the rest in power, which he placed on high, just below the moon. I will not lie to you. Consider how the most excellent **gold** receives its remarkable appearance from the heavens and its good substance from the earth. Regarding the form, the heavens inform the quality which is already contained within the element; through this, over a long period and through purification, the form becomes noble. 

However, this is perfected through me alone. I am the **Architect** <note>original: "Architecta," personifying Nature as a master builder.</note>, and no other human knows the way of life. For unless a "smart-aleck" <note>original: "nasutulus," referring to someone who thinks they are clever or has a "keen nose" for things but lacks true wisdom.</note> knows what to do—how to assign proportion to the elements, how much of fire, air, water, and earth to take and from where, and by what reasoning to correctly mix contrary things so they attract nothing more than their own substances, and how he ought to give influence to these essences—then he will certainly be unable to make not only iron or lead, but even anything of lesser value. How, then, is he to make gold unless he steals my treasure from me? It is not situated in the grasp of his hands or his skill, but he must know my art, which is natural and cannot be carried out by the hands of men.

But truly, even if **gold** is held by the whole world as the most excellent metal (which indeed it is), it nevertheless cures or heals neither diseases nor the impurity of metals; for it transmutes neither into pure gold. In a similar way, it cannot even soften glass <note>A reference to "flexible glass" (vitrum flexile), a legendary lost invention that allowed glass to be hammered like metal without breaking.</note> so that it allows itself to be forged, which otherwise the **Philosopher’s Stone** <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>The legendary alchemical substance capable of turning base metals into gold and acting as an elixir of life.</note> is able to do. Gold alone is the best and most perfect of all metals.

Do you really think you can pour anything of value into your work? Do you also think that your distilling, dissolving, and congealing of your matter in your vessel, or drawing out water from oil, is the right way to follow me? Not in the least, my son; you err greatly here. For even if you spend your time with various mixtures and dissolutions of the elements—of your oil, water, and earth—nonetheless, you have still accomplished nothing except to wander in error.

Do you wish to know the cause? Your matter cannot endure the heat of fire for even half an hour, but everything will vanish in smoke or be consumed in the fire. But that matter in which I labor will be found suitable and upright in every trial, no matter how great the fire may be. Indeed, it becomes even better in the fire. This water comes from a certain dry root; it does not moisten what it touches <note>This "dry water" is a classic alchemical paradox referring to Mercury or the "Philosophical Solvent" which behaves like a liquid but does not wet the hands.</note>. It does not vanish, nor does it fall back, and its oil is not consumed by fire. So perfect are my elements! It is quite different with yours; just as it is not your duty to perform my craft or my office.

By way of epilogue, I tell you that through your artificial fire, you cannot infuse celestial heat. Therefore, from your water, oil, and earth, you will never be able to acquire any matter capable of conceiving the influence that grants it a true substance. It is a gift of God to grant this from the heavenly elements—and indeed more to one than to another—and it is preserved in a simple essence. No one besides me has knowledge of this, except for the one who has been entrusted to me and is a true *Philosopher* <note>In this context, a "Philosopher" specifically means an Alchemist who understands the deep laws of Nature.</note>. My son, I will mention one more true saying <note>original: *veriverbium*</note> to you: namely, that the whole work comes from one single, simple thing, joined with itself...

...matter, should be prepared in a single, well-sealed vessel and a single alembic <term>alembic: a distilling apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube, used here as a metaphor for the womb</term>. I alone form a body so subtle that neither Plato nor even Aristotle himself knew the slightest thing about it. I make hard bones and teeth for chewing, the liver, and soft flesh; I create cold nerves, a moist brain, and the heart—into which God pours life—which is warm; I fill all the veins with red blood.

So it is now compared with your alchemical work. For he who knows how to choose the right matter, and prepares it well in some well-closed vessel, and sets everything correctly in the alembic, has no need to delay the work further. For you and I complete it together, provided you apply the fire as required by Philosophy. For you should know for certain that everything depends on that. 

Therefore, you must see clearly here. Think upon the fire, which they call *boiling*, *digestion*, *ripening*, and *roasting* <note>originals: *epsefin*, *pepsin*, *pepansin*, and *aptesin*—Greek terms for the stages of heat and maturation</note>, as well as natural, preternatural, and the "less natural" fire that does not burn. Likewise, consider the hot and dry, or moist and cold fire, which you must correctly prepare. Without the right matter and the proper fire, you will never reach the intended goal. 

I hand the matter to you: you must arrange the form in order. Here, however, I am not speaking with you about "substantial" or "accidental" form <note>These are technical terms from Aristotelian philosophy; "substantial form" is the essence of a thing, while "accidental form" refers to its non-essential properties like color or shape.</note>, but about the correct type or size of your vessel, and that you prepare your alembic correctly. Act prudently, and manage the work skillfully as befits nature: help me, and I will help you. # THE ALCHEMIST’S RESPONSE, IN WHICH HE CONFESSES
## his errors, and by praying for forgiveness for them,
## gives thanks to Nature.

->(The Alchemist.)<-

Dearest mother Nature, and, after the angels, the most perfect creature created by God, I now offer you honor and glory: for I indeed acknowledge and confess that you are the mother and empress of the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>the "great world" or the universe as a whole</note>, which was founded for man, as the <term>microcosm</term> <note>the "small world"; the belief that the human being is a reflection of the entire universe</note>. You are placed high in the <term>primum mobile</term> <note>original: "primum mobile"; the outermost sphere of the heavens which, in ancient astronomy, moved all the inner spheres</note>, so that you might revolve with your hands and transmute the lower things with your feet, and whether that happens out of love or the opposite, it reaches down to the lowest places of the earth. All these things you do by the command of your Lord; you who, by unceasingly generating, perform such high operations through your lofty <term>intelligences</term> <note>spiritual beings or forces associated with the celestial spheres</note> and the indestructible substances of the heavens, stars, and planets. From these, things are formed so purely that not undeservedly, at all times, you shall be worshipped and loved like a mother and teacher. Indeed, I confess that nothing lives without a soul, and that whatever exists and has essence comes from you and your power, in respect to the power and order received from God. I do not deny that you rule the entire mass, and that the matter of the elements is led under your command. ## Demonstration of Nature.

...you alone are able to have this knowledge. And in this way I have understood it, and I also do not despair at all that, if it should please God and you, I shall see the same with my own eyes in due time.

Now indeed, leaving the limits of time to their own place, I wish to know—and it is enough to know—how that matter may be obtained, how excellent and good it will become, and how much power it may confer in perfecting imperfect things.

That gold is the best of minerals is not unknown to me; nevertheless, it possesses no efficacy for surpassing its own perfection, neither in its form nor its matter. It has no greater operation by which it might perfect anything further than itself, whatever art a man might apply here. For if anyone should try to assert that gold ought to be turned back and reduced into <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: *argentum vivum*; mercury, often considered the "mother" or primary matter of all metals in alchemical theory</note>, he would be acting more foolishly than is right in this matter, since he can elicit nothing more from gold than what is already within it. What, therefore, does a man busily seek in it beyond that minimum which is inside, given that nothing more is to be found there? Such boldness is backward. Nevertheless, so that those <term>pseudo-philosophers</term> <note>original: *Philosophastri*; a derisive term for those who practice alchemy without true understanding, "alchemical pretenders"</note> might betray their own folly, they say that, by the benefit of their art, a body ought to be led backward and reduced into its <term>first matter</term> <note>original: *primam materiam*; the formless, primal substance from which all things are made</note>. 

Truly, from your instruction, it is not hidden from me that a reduction does not happen to things that have been made into a certain species or individual, unless that species is first <term>corrupted</term> <note>original: *corrumpatur*; in Aristotelian physics, "corruption" is the opposite of "generation"—the breakdown of a specific form so its matter can become something else</note>. Nevertheless, after that corruption, no <term>generation</term> of a similar species occurs unless the species first returns to its genus. Indeed, I affirm even more: that the destruction of gold is by no means the way of making gold. For if it once loses its species <note>its "gold-ness" or essential identity</note>, then a man is in no way able to restore it to the same; and furthermore, a subtle art would still be required if one attempted to reduce it into a <insert>proper</insert> powder. 

If, however, someone should perhaps propose to resolve it in such a way that he wishes to separate its composite, or body, into the <term>first mixture</term> which was made for it by the elements, he—whatever he may say—will never be able to lead that task to its end. For gold endures both heat and cold, and in the fire it is rendered more and more pure—

Therefore, in general, no one can truly affirm that "like generates like" in every instance. Plants receive nourishment and life, and they sow and plant themselves; minerals, however, perceive nothing, and in their first year as in their last, they remain the same size. They receive their essence in the earth from the elements through you <note>Addressing Nature</note>, a process which is carried out without sowing, planting, or any other cultivation.

Furthermore, from your teaching, I have learned and discovered that the sayings of the ancient Philosophers—when interpreted through deceptive practice—should not be obeyed at all. Instead, one must observe only the true and essential Theory in which nature is central; for in that theory, all essence, matter, and substance consist. 

Now, however, I recall how a deceptive and <term>sophistic</term> <note>In this context, someone who uses clever but false arguments to trick others</note> seducer, who was nevertheless regarded as a great Philosopher, once tried to persuade me. He said: "For the correct <term>matter</term> <note>The starting material for the Alchemical Work</note>, nothing else should be taken but pure and crude quicksilver, provided it is first well mixed with gold." He claimed that from these two things well joined, something extraordinary would be made, and in that conjunction, one would make the other perfect. 

"If," that impostor continued, "you do this, you will then obtain the <term>Elixir</term> <note>A universal medicine or substance capable of transmuting metals</note>. But first, the four mixed elements must be separated from each other and each one purified; then they must be joined again, the great united with the small, and the subtle introduced into the thick—and in this way, the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>original: *lapidem Philosophicum*</note> is made." 

But I am not unaware that such ravings are mere frauds, and that such men are devoid of understanding. They deceive not only others but themselves as well; whether they be called Philosophers or Physicians, they understand nothing of this matter.

Likewise, it is by no means hidden from me what you have said: that only God Most High can create something from the elements, since He produced nature itself. He knows how to mix elements according to their quantity, to proportion their qualities correctly, and to join and mix elements properly, just as it seemed fit to Him. No one can be found who would dare to do the same or to deny His power. For He alone is the creator and the producer of all good things, nor is there anything in the world that was made without Him.

Therefore, let all the boastful <term>Chemical Sophists</term> <note>original: *Chimici Sophistæ*; a derogatory term for alchemists who use false methods, tricks, or purely chemical recipes without understanding the underlying natural philosophy</note> now be silent, and let them not hope to reap where they have not sown. These are the people who, through their false <term>calcinations</term> <note>the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to ash or powder</note>, <term>sublimations</term> <note>the process of heating a substance until it turns into vapor and then solidifies again, used for purification</note>, and <term>distillations</term>, drive away the spirits through smoke. Through their sophisticated <term>coagulations</term> and congealings, they try to persuade those who are unskilled in these matters—indeed, they even pretend to those who have actually completed the Great Work—that the elements of <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: *argentum vivum*; mercury</note> and gold will be correctly separated, a claim which in the end comes to nothing. 

For it is true that all things under heaven are made from the four elements, possess the correct quantity, and are mixed by nature in the right proportion according to their species. However, they are not mixed in such a way that all are properly unified, but remain distinct in their virtue—this is especially true of the matter that will become the <term>Philosophical Stone</term> <note>original: *Philosophici lapidis*; the legendary substance sought by alchemists to achieve transmutation and medicinal perfection</note>.

By these things, I also understand how in <term>red quicksilver</term> and the perfect body which is called <term>Sol</term> <note>original: *Sol*; Latin for "Sun," the alchemical name for gold</note>, the four elements are each united with one another in a unique way. They are mixed through such singular means that they cannot be separated by the benefit of human art. For all the ancient and true Philosophers write that fire and air are enclosed within water and earth, where they exercise their power and struggle violently with one another in a completely indissoluble way, such that no one but God and Nature can loosen that bond. 

I can truly affirm this and even demonstrate it philosophically: for fire is invisible to us, and air is incomprehensible <note>meaning intangible or unable to be grasped</note>. If anyone says that these elements can be seen individually, he is an impostor; for according to irrefutable principles, the elements are inseparable. Although the Sophists pretend and wish to affirm for certain that they can separate gold and quicksilver into the four constituent elements, they are nevertheless liars.

For if the two elements, fire and air, were so separated, then each would necessarily vanish. Although they <note>Referring to the "Sophists" or false alchemists mentioned on the previous page</note> may claim that they retain them, they are nonetheless completely ignorant of where they go; indeed, neither air nor fire can be seen or perceived. If, therefore, he now attempts to separate them, how, I ask, will he join them together again so that he might once more create a unified compound and true subject, if he is completely ignorant of the quantity and quality of the elements, and the method of their correct union?

Therefore, it is not at all appropriate for them to be separated, unless they are rejoined properly. That task must be entrusted to you, Nature, who well knows the art of arranging things, of composing the <term>Philosophical Stone</term> <note>original: *lapis Philosophicus*; the legendary substance sought by alchemists to transmute metals and heal the body</note>, and of making a proper mixture of the elements without separation. You have told me more than enough that the separation of elements and their repeated joining will be unnecessary; for no such art is to be obtained, and it is a mystery entrusted and established for you by God alone. Without any doubt, however, the Stone—or the <term>Elixir</term>—comes from you, though without the separation of elements, yet not without your instruments or the help of some wise man skilled in this matter. # ->Demonstration of Nature<-

There is a certain matter pertaining to Alchemy, just as you, Nature—to whom I am prepared to serve with both my body and my life—know much better than I do. Furthermore, it must be known that Alchemy accomplishes three specific things: First, it makes a certain metal perfect and living, and it <term>digests</term> <note>In alchemy, digestion refers to a process of slow, gentle heating to mature a substance</note> its spirit so that nothing in it is lost, just as experience itself testifies to this fact. Second, it cooks and digests the matter in a small vessel in such a way that, without the addition of any other single thing, it transmutes the body and spirit into one. For this reason, nothing new is to be added to it; nor does any mixing occur unless the Principles of Nature provide and bestow it. For whatever Nature produces for this purpose and leaves to us, that is taken by the <term>Art</term> <note>referring to the alchemical craft</note> for the work. Third, it proves that in fact, in the actual doing of the work, no separation of the four elements occurs in the making of the <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> from quicksilver <note>original: "argento vivo", or Mercury</note> and the Sun <note>original: "Sole", meaning Gold</note>, which is called deep red gold. Indeed, to think otherwise is a massive error, and is entirely contrary to noble Alchemy and fundamental Philosophy.

Truly, it is more certain than certainty itself that every elementary thing is nourished or fed by the elements themselves. However, if these elements—which are now well-disposed and composed into a single subject just as Nature brought them forth—are then separated, that subject becomes corrupted and depraved. The excellent bond that held the elements together is broken, and there is no longer a mixture; instead, the thing is reduced to nothing again by being separated into the four elements. 

For if a father is to beget a son, he must by no means be destroyed first; rather, it is enough that the generating spirit goes out with the seed itself, which the female seed conceives and preserves in heat. Such a spirit generates the infant and the form of its limbs, just as <term>Avicenna</term> <note>A famous Persian physician and philosopher often cited in alchemical texts</note> testifies in the appropriate place. In a similar way, this is compared with pure gold, which is the true matter of the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term>. For it is the "father" who prepares and establishes all things; therefore, he is not to be destroyed or corrupted, nor separated from his elements. Instead, it is enough that the Sun <note>Gold</note> as the father, who breathes in his spirit, transmits virtue and efficacy through it, in virtue and...

It is thus highly necessary that we imitate **Nature** and use her instruments in the way she makes the elements. Without this guidance, we will not be correct imitators in the bringing forth of the form of this **Stone**, nor in the investigation of the means looking toward this goal—the means through which one reaches the instruments that **Nature** uses in minerals while she gives **quicksilver** its form. But if we do otherwise, then we are destroyers of that which **Nature** has composed and disposed for an end, while we so shamefully separate the mixture against your commands, O **Nature**. Nonetheless, as **Aristotle** says, we must <term>transmute</term> the elements so that we may find what we seek.

And for this reason, O **Nature**, you have wisely led me to your path, for which benefit I both give and hold immense thanks. For from you alone have I learned so much that all my works would otherwise be of no value. # PHILOSOPHICAL SUMMARY,

### OF NICOLAS FLAMEL. <note>Nicolas Flamel (c. 1330–1418) was a French scribe and manuscript seller who posthumously became one of the most famous figures in alchemy, legendary for allegedly discovering the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

**H**e who strives to obtain the knowledge of metals, and the certain science of how they are mutually transmuted <note>original: "transmutetur"; the alchemical process of changing one substance, typically a base metal like lead, into another, like gold.</note> among themselves, must of necessity know above all else from what matter they originate, and how they are simultaneously formed within their minerals. Lest an error be made here, one must observe and examine the transmutations as they occur everywhere within the veins of the earth. Therefore, they can also be transmuted outside of the minerals, if they are first made spiritual, so that they may arrive at their own <term>sulfur</term> <note>In alchemy, "Sulfur" represents the active, masculine, and combustible principle of a substance, not merely the chemical element.</note> and <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"; also known as Mercury, representing the passive, feminine, and fluid principle.</note>, which nature produces. For indeed, all metals are formed from sulfur and quicksilver, which are the two seeds of all metals; one of these is of the masculine sex and temperament, while the other is of the feminine. Moreover, those two seeds are composed of the elements. And the first indeed, namely the masculine seed which is called sulfur, is nothing other than fire and air; and it is true sulfur, like fire, without a changeable or metallic nature—not, however, that common sulfur <note>original: "vulgare"; alchemists distinguished between "vulgar" materials found in shops and "philosophical" materials refined through their art.</note>, which is of no metallic substance. The other feminine seed, which is called quicksilver, is nothing other than earth and water. The ancient sages prefigured these two aforementioned seeds as two Dragons or serpents, one of which had wings, while the other had none. The Dragon without wings is sulfur, never [flying away] from

# Philosophical Summary.

...flying away from the fire. The **winged serpent** is **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum"; also known as Mercury. In alchemy, the "wings" symbolize volatility—the tendency of a substance to evaporate or escape when heated.</note>, which is carried by the wind; it is the feminine seed, made from water and earth. For this reason, it also flies away from the fire at its certain hour, and is inconstant within it. But if indeed those two seeds—which had been separated from one another—are reduced again into one, and become united through triumphant nature in the **book of Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurij libro"; likely a metaphorical reference to the "record" or fundamental substance of Mercury, which Flamel describes as the "mother of metals."</note>, which is the first of metals and the mother of metals, then the Philosophers call it the **flying Dragon**. This is because the Dragon, ignited by its own fire, scatters fire and a poisonous vapor into the air during its flight. 

Mercury does the very same thing: when it sits in its place within the vessel above the external fire, and when the fire is rightly governed, it ignites the internal, natural fire that is hidden in its depths. Then, one will be able to see how that external fire, which is called the **vegetable fire** <note>In alchemy, "vegetable fire" or "ignis vegetabilis" refers to a gentle, life-giving heat, similar to the heat that causes plants to grow, rather than a destructive forge fire.</note>, inflames the natural heat of the Mercury. A more watchful observer will see a certain poisonous smoke or vapor exhale into the air, which will have such a stench and be such a most destructive poison; this is nothing other than the **Dragon’s head** <note>original: "Draconis caput"; a term often used to describe the initial, volatile stage of the work or a specific chemical byproduct.</note>, which comes forth very swiftly from **Babylon** <note>In alchemical allegory, Babylon often represents the chaotic, unrefined state of the "prime matter" or the dark, confused stage of the chemical process (the nigredo).</note>, which is surrounded by two or three miles.

Other Philosophers, however, have compared this Mercury to a **flying lion**, and they named it so because the lion devours many kinds of animals and refreshes and gladdens itself by this voracity at its own pleasure, except for those animals that can violently resist its fury. In the same way, Mercury also acts, for it has such an operation within itself that it immediately strips any metal of its own form, consumes it, and devours it. 

Nevertheless, I signify to you that there are two metals, namely **gold** and **silver**, which are able to withstand it; although it may be known that if Mercury is excessively inflamed, it devours even these two metals and hides them in its belly. However, whichever of these happens, it is certain that the metal is not destroyed in the belly of the Mercury. For they are more perfected in their nature and more hardened than Mercury itself, since Mercury is an imperfect metal—and yet, nonetheless, the substance of perfection is within it. Common gold, which is a perfect metal, as well as silver and all imperfect metals, originate from Mercury. Therefore, the ancient Philosophers call it the **mother of metals**; and from this it follows...

# *Philosophical Summary.*

...because, when it is formed into something, it contains a double metallic substance within itself. And first, indeed, it contains the substance of the **inner moon** <note>original: "lunæ"; in alchemy, the Moon symbolizes Silver.</note>, and then also of the **sun** <note>original: "solis"; the Sun symbolizes Gold.</note>, which is a metal unlike the other. Mercury is formed from these two substances, which are nurtured in a spiritual <note>In this context, "spiritual" refers to a volatile, non-solid, or vaporous state rather than a religious one.</note> manner within its body. As soon as Nature has formed that Mercury from those two mentioned spirits, she then labors to make them perfect and physical. But when these two spirits have matured, and the two **seeds** <note>original: "spermata"; the fundamental reproductive principles of metals.</note> have awakened, they desire to take on their own physical bodies; when this happens, the mother, **Mercury**, must necessarily die. Once naturally **mortified** <note>original: "mortificatus"; "Mortification" is the alchemical process of "killing" a substance—usually by changing its form or color, such as turning liquid mercury into a solid powder—to allow for its rebirth into a higher form.</note> in this way, she is no longer able to bring herself back to life as she was before.

Certain boastful and arrogant **Chemists** <note>The author uses "Chimici" to refer to "puffers" or false alchemists who focus on physical shortcuts rather than true natural philosophy.</note> try to claim in obscure words that one ought to transmute perfect and imperfect bodies into "running" <note>liquid</note> Mercury; but deceit and a **snake in the grass** <note>original: "anguis in herba"; an idiom for a hidden danger or deception.</note> lurk there. It is indeed true that Mercury consumes certain imperfect metals, such as **lead** or **tin**, and increases them in quantity without effort; but by that very act, it loses its own perfection, so that it is no longer Mercury in this state. But if it were mortified by **Art** <note>Alchemical practice or human intervention.</note>, so that it could no longer make itself living [liquid], then it would be transmuted into another thing, just as happens with **Cinnabar** <note>original: "Cinnabari"; mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral.</note> or **sublimate** <note>Mercury that has been heated into vapor and then condensed into a solid crust.</note>. 

For when it is **coagulated** <note>turned from a liquid into a solid</note> by Art—whether that happens slowly or quickly—then its two bodies do not take on a fixed body, nor would they preserve it, as can be seen in the passages of the earth. Lest anyone err here: it can just as little be coagulated by nature underground without a **fixed grain** appearing, and from the two seeds, it must bring forth some true germ, as is seen in the **veins of lead**. For there is no vein of this kind where some fixed grain does not appear—namely of gold and silver—and that in substance and nourishment. The first coagulation of Mercury is the **ore of lead** <note>original: "minera plumbi"</note>, and it is indeed most suitable and convenient for bringing it [Mercury] to perfection and **fixation** <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable in fire.</note>. For as was said before, the ore of lead is not without a fixed grain of gold and silver, which grains nature supplies there:

# Philosophical Summary.

...it can <term>multiply</term> <note>In alchemy, "multiplication" refers to the process of increasing the power, weight, or medicinal virtue of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> itself in this way, so that it may better reach full perfection and power, just as I myself have experienced, and can both affirm and confirm for certain. For as long as it is kept within its **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio"; here referring to the "Philosophical Mercury," a primordial substance believed to be the source of all metals.</note>—that is, not separated from its **ore** <note>original: "minera"; the source material or "womb" in which the alchemist believes the metal "grows."</note> but well-guarded—then it can multiply itself, provided it can draw substance from its Mercury (for every metal that is still in its ore is Mercury).

But if the **fixed grain** <note>The "fixed grain" is the solid, stable part of the metal that has reached a certain level of purity.</note> is taken away and separated from its Mercury, which is its source, it will then be like a green, unripe fruit on a tree. After the flower is gone, the fruit is formed and becomes an apple. But if someone were to pluck that unripe fruit, its primary formation would be ruined. For man has no knowledge to grant substance or maturity in the way that internal Nature does while the fruit still hangs from the tree and can receive its substance and nourishment from Nature. Therefore, for as long as maturity is expected, the fruit draws in its flavor and juice, both increasing and nourishing itself, until it reaches perfect ripeness.

It is prepared in a similar way with **gold**. For if the grain is made by Nature and returned to its Mercury, it is then sustained by that same Mercury in a daily and unceasing manner, and is brought back into its perfect Mercury, just as it is in itself. Then one must wait until it gains some substance from its Mercury, not unlike what happens with the fruits of trees. For just as **Mercury** is the **tree** of both perfect and imperfect metals, so too those metals can have no nourishment from anywhere else except from their own Mercury.

If, therefore, you perhaps wish to harvest the fruit from Mercury—which is the shining and glowing **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: "Sol & Luna"; in alchemical texts, the Sun always represents Gold and the Moon represents Silver.</note>—and if it should happen that they are joined together not far from one another, yet in such a way that it happens without a longer delay; then do not think that you can rejoin, multiply, and increase them without change, as Nature did from the beginning. For if the metals are separated from their ore, they are then like those fruits picked too prematurely...

# Philosophical Summary.

...fruits of trees are found, which never arrive at their proper size and perfection. Similarly, both by nature and experience itself, it is known regarding the fruits of trees that if an apple or a pear is once plucked from the tree, it would then be great folly if anyone should try to graft it back onto the tree and in this way expect the maturity of that fruit. For the more it is handled by the hands—as experience similarly testifies—the more and the more quickly it withers. 

And in the same way, the matter stands with metals. For if anyone should try to take common metallic **gold** <note>original: "aurum"</note> and **silver** <note>original: "argentum"</note> and reduce both those metals into **Mercury** <note>The liquid metal quicksilver; alchemists believed it was the "seed" or "womb" of all other metals.</note>, he would be acting completely foolishly. For here no subtle art could be found by which one would not deceive himself, even if he used various waters, **cements** <note>In alchemy, a "cement" is a pasty substance used to refine or color metals at high heat.</note>, or infinite other things of that kind which cannot be individually recounted. He would constantly miss the mark, and the same thing would happen to him as to those who wish to pluck unripe fruits and then tie them back to the trunk. 

Although some true Philosophers have rightly and well said that if **Sun** <note>original: "Sol"; the alchemical name for gold.</note> and **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"; the alchemical name for silver.</note> are properly joined by means of the right Mercury, they then make all other <term>imperfect metals</term> <note>Metals like lead, tin, or iron, which alchemists believed were simply "sick" or "immature" versions of gold.</note> perfect. In this matter, however, most men miss the mark, having nothing else on earth but these three—**vegetable, animal, or mineral**—which are joined in one thing. 

For they do not take care to realize that the Philosophers speak not of common gold, silver, and Mercury—which are all dead and no longer receive any substance, but remain in their **being** <note>original: "ESSE"; here meaning a fixed, static state of existence that can no longer grow or change.</note>—and none of them is able to help another toward perfection. Indeed, they are truly fruits that are plucked from trees before their time, and for that reason are considered worthless. In them, indeed, what is sought is by no means found; they have nothing more than what they themselves need. 

Therefore, the fruits must be sought on the tree, which leads directly to them, and whose fruit daily becomes larger and increases more and more as long as the tree extends. And this work, indeed, is a sight of the greatest joy. By this means, that tree can be planted without the gathering of fruits, and transported into other moister, more fruitful, and better places: which indeed, perhaps in one day [gives] more [nourishment] to the fruit...

# Philosophical Summary.

...can contribute more nourishment than it would otherwise have received from another soil in the space of a hundred years.

Therefore, by this very fact, it must be understood that one ought to take **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium"</note>, which is the most highly praised tree, which possesses within itself—and indeed indissolubly—the **Sun** <note>The alchemical name for gold.</note> and the **Moon** <note>The alchemical name for silver.</note>. Then, let it be transferred into another soil, somewhat closer to the Sun, so that by this means a wonderful benefit may be obtained; in this matter, the **dew** <note>In alchemy, dew was often considered a "celestial" water that carried the influence of the stars down to the earth to animate matter.</note> is abundantly sufficient. For where it was previously planted, it was so tossed and weakened by wind and cold that very little fruit could be expected from it; in that place it remained for a long time and brought forth no fruit at all.

Truly, however, there is a certain **Garden of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophis hortus"; a metaphor for the sealed vessel or the specific chemical environment where the "Great Work" is perfected.</note> in which the Sun dwells unceasingly, both in morning and evening hours, by day and by night. It is there with the sweetest dew, by which it is well sprinkled and moistened; the earth of this garden produces trees and fruits which are planted there, and they receive proper nourishment from a most pleasant pasture. This happens daily, and there they are strengthened, vivified, and do not wither in the least—scarcely less in one year than they would have in a thousand years in another place where they were plagued by the cold. 

Therefore, let them be taken and warmed assiduously night and day over a fire in an **alembic** <term>Alembic: A distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube, used to refine substances through evaporation and condensation.</term>. However, this should not be a fire made of coal or wood, but a clear and transparent fire shall be made, not unlike the Sun itself, which must never be hotter or more burning than is right, but must remain at the same temperature at all times. For the vapor is the dew and the **seed of all metals** <note>original: "semen omnium metallorum"</note>, which must not be altered. 

One can see in growing fruits that if they have too much heat without a moderate amount of dew, they remain dry and die upon their branches, reaching no perfection at all. But if they are sustained on the tree by heat and a moderate humidity, then they become elegant and fruitful. For heat and humidity are the nourishment of all earthly things, namely of animals, vegetables, and minerals. For this reason, fires stirred up from coal and wood are least suitable for them; those are violent fires which do not nourish in the way the heat of the sun is accustomed to do, which also all...

# Philosophical Summary.

...preserved corporal things, for the reason that it becomes natural. To this end, even the true Philosophers have chosen no other fire than the **natural** one, which they follow—not because the Philosopher does exactly what nature does, for Nature created all things, namely vegetables, minerals, and animals, each in the specific rank over which it holds sway.

In a similar way, I will not say now that men make natural things by their art; rather, if nature completes or operates upon such things, then by human art they are rendered more perfect than they were when made by nature. And in this way the ancient Philosophers, for the instruction of us all, labored at nothing else than working naturally with the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"; alchemical silver</note> and the true mother, **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>. From these they made the **Mercury of the Philosophers**, which, in its operation, is much stronger than natural mercury. For while the latter only lends its effort to simple metals—whether perfect or imperfect, cold or hot—the **Philosophical Stone** <note>The legendary "Lapis," the goal of the Great Work, capable of perfecting matter.</note> serves even the "more-than-perfect" and imperfect metals, so that it might quickly perfect and restore them, and that without any loss, addition, or change. It leaves them in the same state as they were created by nature, yet neglects nothing. 

I will not say the same here now—that Philosophers join all those three to better perfect their Mercury—as certain men unskilled in things and unlearned **Chemists** <note>original: "Chimici"; often used dismissively here to refer to those who follow only the "letter" of chemical recipes without philosophical understanding.</note> do, who take common gold, silver, and mercury and handle them so poorly that they vanish in smoke. In that way, they strive to perfect the Mercury of the Philosophers, yet they by no means reach it, for it is the **first matter** <note>original: "prima materia"; the primordial, undifferentiated substance from which all things are created.</note> of the stone and the true mineral. 

But if they wish to reach it and find something good, then it is necessary for them to betake themselves to the **mountain of the seven** <note>original: "montem septimorum"; likely a reference to the seven planetary metals (Gold, Silver, Mercury, Copper, Iron, Tin, Lead).</note>, where there is no level ground, and from the height to look down upon the **sixth** <note>Likely referring to the sixth planet/metal in a traditional descending order.</note>, which they will see from afar. At the peak of that mountain, they will recognize the triumphant **Royal Herb** <note>original: "Regalem herbam"</note>, which some Philosophers have called mineral, and some vegetable, and which is named **Saturnine** <note>original: "Saturnialis"; relating to Saturn, the god/planet associated with the metal Lead and the beginning of the alchemical process.</note>. However, let the **bones** <note>In alchemical jargon, "bones" usually refers to the solid, calcined remains or the "caput mortuum" left after distillation.</note> be left behind, and let the pure and clean **broth** <note>The distilled essence or "mercurial water" extracted from the material.</note> be taken from there; in this way, the better part of the work can be done. And this is the right and subtle **Mercury of the Philosophers** which you ought to take.

# Philosophical Summary.

Z 2

And first indeed he will perform the <term>white work<note>Latin: *opus album*; the penultimate stage of alchemy, resulting in a white tincture that transforms base metals into silver.</note></term>, and then also the <term>red work<note>Latin: *opus rubrum*; the final stage of the Great Work, resulting in the Red Stone or elixir capable of making gold and healing the body.</note></term>, if you have well understood my discourse. For each of these is nothing other than what they call the <term>practice<note>Latin: *practica*; the actual physical laboratory operation as opposed to theory.</note></term>. The <term>Sun and Moon<note>Latin: *Sol & Luna*; alchemical code for gold and silver, or the active and passive principles of the work.</note></term> are prepared in one and the same way, from which the white and the red arise in the practice—which is so simple and light that even a woman at her spinning wheel could complete it without hindrance; or, as if she were to place eggs under a hen in winter time for hatching, and yet not wash them. For eggs placed for hatching are not washed, but are placed under the hen just as they are. No further labor is required in this than that those eggs be turned daily, so that the chicks may emerge better and more quickly. 

This has now been declared more than enough. To draw out an example: first, do not wash your <term>Mercury<note>Latin: *Mercurium*; refers here to the "Philosophical Mercury," the fundamental substance of the work, not necessarily common quicksilver.</note></term>, but take it and place it with its like—which is fire—into the ash, which is the straw, and into a single glass vessel, which is the nest, without any other thing, in some suitable <term>alembic<note>Latin: *alembico*; a distillation vessel, though here used as a metaphor for the "house" where the transformation occurs.</note></term>, which is the house. And then, from there, a certain chick will emerge, who will free you from all diseases with its blood, and will feed you with its flesh, and will clothe you with its feathers, and guard you from the cold. 

Toward this end, I pray and beseech the supreme Creator of all things that He might deign to most mercifully bestow His grace upon all faithful <term>Chemists<note>Latin: *Chimicis*; practitioners of alchemy.</note></term>, that they may find a chick of this kind from which to sustain themselves; just as I have received that small portion which I have declared here from above, from God the Father, who also bestowed it upon me out of His love and according to His goodness. I have therefore written this present little work for you, so that you might seek with greater desire and enter upon the right path. Indeed, I have

**A**fter so many deceptions, my dearly beloved friend and brother, have been presented to simpler folk in the celebrated **Chemical Art** <note>original: "ars Chimica"; here referring to Alchemy, the art of transmuting metals and seeking the Philosopher's Stone.</note> by certain **pseudo-chemists**, whose writings are nevertheless nothing other than mere impostures and lies; although the aforementioned simple-minded ones—who judge such things to be of great importance—believe these lies more than is right and proceed further in their labor, they thereby cast themselves into difficult labors and immense troubles. Indeed, because what is begun from a misguided and poor understanding can never be brought to any praiseworthy end.

For this reason, you see that the greater part of men who in our present day betake themselves to this distinguished Chemical Art are hunting for false chemical processes, persuading themselves for certain that they have found the true and right art there. This art, however, is described in books not without **parables** <note>Alchemical "parables" are allegorical or metaphorical descriptions used to hide secrets from those the authors deemed unworthy.</note>; but, on the contrary, many false **recipes** <note>original: "R."; the standard abbreviation for "Recipe," used here to denote alchemical formulas or prescriptions.</note> are found in more than enough abundance. These were devised by false and wicked men who themselves knew nothing of the truth beforehand; and therefore, they were unable to write anything truthful concerning it. Thus, both the reader and the writer understood equally much—namely, very little—of what pertains to nature. 

If these writers had indeed known the requirements of nature, they would never have written such formless confusions and **recipes**, nor would they have attempted to defend them by their false **sublimation**, **calcination**, **distillation**, **solution**, **coagulation**, and feigned **putrefaction** and **corruption** <note>These are the standard chemical operations of the alchemical "Great Work." The author argues that frauds misuse these terms to mask their ignorance of natural laws.</note>. One may see this daily among those unskilled in such matters, who squander all their wealth through their false pollutions. All of this occurs through pseudo-chemical books, which are accustomed to teach falsely regarding erroneous **regimens** <note>The specific sequence of heating and timing required for a successful alchemical transformation.</note> that do not conform to nature in the slightest.

# The Way of Truth.

Processes of this sort, dealing with useless and less essential matters, share no common ground with true Chemical operations. Instead, true processes follow venerable Nature, just as she prepares substances within the veins of the earth; and they do so without the [need for] solution, coagulation, or putrefaction <note>These are standard alchemical stages (dissolving, thickening, and decaying), which the author argues are often over-complicated by frauds.</note>, for the process is in itself quite simple. 

For consider and weigh within yourself, I beseech you, my friend: all these instruments, <term>alembics</term> <note>Distillation flasks with a cooling "beak."</note>, <term>retorts</term> <note>Glass vessels with a long neck turned downward, used for distilling liquids.</note>, <term>circular glasses</term> <note>Also known as "pelicans," these vessels allowed for continuous circulation of vapors.</note> and <term>sublimatories</term> <note>Vessels used to turn solid substances into vapor through heat.</note>, the various types of fires, and the diverse materials—tell me, are they found in the veins of the earth where metals flourish and grow? Does Nature, in those same veins of the earth, employ so many and such various alembics or glasses? Does she use so many materials, such as <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: "atramentum sutorium"; literally "shoemaker’s blacking," a term for metallic sulfates like green vitriol.</note>, <term>salt</term>, <term>arsenic</term>, <term>Mercury</term>, <term>sulfur</term>, and other ridiculous follies? These things are passed over here on purpose "with a dry foot" <note>original: "sicco pede"; a Latin idiom meaning to pass over something quickly or without getting bogged down in details.</note>, yet the Chemists use them, and by them, they shamefully lose both their time and their fortunes in a completely backwards manner. 

For this reason, they are not undeservedly called ignorant of reality. Though they busy themselves daily in Chemistry, they nevertheless persist in their shameful solutions, coagulations, distillations, putrefactions, and other worthless, frivolous things. Thus they waste their time and wealth recklessly, as we have said, even though Nature is so simple and completes her labor in an equally simple fashion. 

What profit is there for us, then, in such foul deception by <term>pseudo-chemists</term> and in their most laborious toil? All these things are esteemed as mere foolishness by true craftsmen; indeed, they are daily held in mockery because they do not open their eyes wider, but stubbornly persevere in those <term>sophisms</term> <note>In this context, "sophisms" refers to false alchemical theories or deceptive recipes that sound logical but lead to failure.</note>. In these errors they must linger, and finally even die, since they busy themselves with nothing more than searching for and reading such "sophistic" books. All their actions, therefore, are based on sophistry and are not Philosophical; for that reason, they can never arrive at any true art or reality.

However, I wish this to be truly affirmed to you now: as long as you love lies rather than the philosophical art, the truth will not be revealed to you. This is so even though I myself have persevered in such <term>sophistic</term> regimens, and in <term>subliming</term>, <term>distilling</term>, <term>calcining</term>... <note>The text ends here mid-sentence, indicating the author is about to recount his own past failures in laboratory work before he found the "Way of Truth."</note>

# The Way of Truth.

I labored by circulating [liquids], nor did I spare even certain substances such as urine, salt, <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: "atramento sutorio"; literally "shoemaker's blacking," a common term for metallic sulfates like copperas or green vitriol.</note>, alum, and so forth. I tormented myself with various labors involving hair, wine, eggs, bones, and every kind of herb. I tested <term>Arsenic</term>, and <term>Mercury</term> with <term>sulfur</term>; I put all minerals and metals to the proof. I reached them through "strong waters" <note>Corrosive acids, such as nitric acid.</note> and lyes, both by dissolving and by thickening. I practiced the arts of amalgamating and precipitating, and yet I derived no pleasure or joy from it. I had placed great faith in the <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: "Quinta essentia"; the "fifth essence," a pure, medicinal, or transformative extract thought to be more refined than the four physical elements.</note>, but here too I found myself deceived.

Therefore, beloved brother, I most diligently warn you: if you wish to take up the search for so excellent an art, do not intrude upon the sophistical and common systems of the <term>sublimation</term> of <term>Sulfur</term> and <term>Mercury</term>, nor the dissolving of bodies or the thickening of spirits. Do not trouble yourself with their expensive <term>alembics</term> <note>Glass distilling apparatuses with a cooling "beak."</note>, as they are poorly suited for the true art. For as long as you have not investigated the true essence of nature, just so long—believe me—will you remain without comfort, and at last you will discover that this art is nothing but a fiction and a lie.

If you desire to seek profit, you must therefore renounce <term>sublimation</term> <note>The process of heating a solid until it turns into vapor and then solidifies again.</note>, <term>calcination</term> <note>Reducing a substance to powder or "ash" through high heat.</note>, <term>solution</term> <note>The act of dissolving a solid into a liquid.</note>, and <term>coagulation</term> <note>The thickening of a liquid into a solid.</note>, along with <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The breakdown or "rotting" of a substance, which alchemists believed was necessary to release its inner spirit.</note> itself. Instead, you must become a disciple to seek the true foundation of Philosophy. This foundation, according to its genuine meaning, will be able to show you a different [kind of] solution and coagulation, and likewise a different system, which is natural and agrees with Nature herself.

For just as Nature works within the veins of the earth where metals grow, so also must you follow Nature here. For you see that Nature employs no more than one single substance in her essence, and in that aforementioned substance you see all things hidden. This substance, moreover, requires no other labor than <term>cooking</term> <note>original: "coctio"; the application of steady, gentle heat. In Alchemy, this is the central process of maturing a substance, much like an egg being hatched.</note>, through which it is raised up more and more, to its highest degree. From this simple <term>cooking</term> and graduation, crafty sophists have devised the names of <term>solution</term>, <term>coagulation</term>, <term>calcination</term>, <term>putrefaction</term>, <term>sublimation</term>, and other names of phantasms; they have fashioned an entirely different essence from the true, simple essence or <term>cooking</term>...

...they have fabricated, and in this way they have cast a simple and true art into the greatest difficulty, just as if so many troubles, and such great labors and expenses, were required for it. This, however, was devised by them falsely, out of pure hatred and envy, so that by this reasoning they might lead followers away from the true art and involve them in extreme poverty. They will find it most difficult to justify this before God, while they have given little thought to what **Christ** says: **LOVE YOUR NEIGHBOR AS YOURSELF**. They have trampled the truth under their feet and substituted lies in its place, which they have adorned in a marvelous way, and they have written massive books about it—as if the <term>correction of metals</term> <note>original: "metallorum correctio"; the process of "perfecting" or purifying base metals into gold.</note> were a work so laborious and difficult, when it is nevertheless merely a certain simple **cooking** <note>original: "coctio"; a central alchemical concept referring to the slow application of heat to mature or "ripen" a substance, similar to digestion.</note>.

For as long as you cook, for so long you also <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: "putrificas"; the stage where the substance breaks down, often turning black, which alchemists saw as a necessary death before rebirth.</note>, and the substance becomes subject to decay, much like a grain of wheat which, having been cast into the earth, is preserved in that same earth by the heat of the Sun; and through natural rain, it must first rot before anything new grows from it. This they have called **putrefaction** and **solution**. In the same way, you also <term>sublimate</term> <note>original: "sublimas"; to refine a substance by turning it into vapor and then back to solid.</note> during the **Cooking**: indeed, they named the "correction" of the substance "sublimation" and "multiplication" <note>The process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine.</note> so that they might better deceive the simple-minded. In a similar way, you also <term>coagulate</term>: for when moisture is changed into the nature of fire, so much so that it can resist fire and is neither consumed nor vanishes as smoke, they then call that **coagulation**. In this cooking, the **Philosophers** <term>circulate</term> <note>original: "circulant"; the cycling of a substance through evaporation and condensation within a sealed vessel.</note>; for in it, fire is united with water, lest the fire be entirely burned up—just as we see daily that water protects all things from fire as long as the water is available. Similarly, the water in the cooking takes care of the fire and unites itself with the fire, so that it may become entirely pure fire; and thus it was called **circulation** or **conjunction** by the ancients.

And by this reasoning, you see how they have devised so many names for that simple cooking and established so many false procedures to seduce men. They have imposed those diverse names upon this single substance so that no one might perceive what it actually was, from which (through divine grace) so many excellent and outstanding things are prepar-

...they were prepared. First, they call that our <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Merc."; in alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of liquidity, volatility, and the "spirit" of a substance.</note>, by which they understood nothing other than the moisture which began to unite itself a little with fire, and so was compared with Mercury. And they also called it our <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original: "sulphur"; the alchemical principle of combustion, oiliness, and "soul."</note>, which is nevertheless nothing else than the fire itself, which lies hidden under the water or moisture, and is **cooked** by the water even to its highest degree.
