As for other names—**Orpiment**, **Arsenic**, **Marcasite**, etc.—those were not devised by the Philosophers <note>The "Philosophers" refers to the true masters of alchemy, as opposed to the "sophists" or fraudulent practitioners.</note> but by unskilled scoundrels and sophists who were ignorant of the truth itself. Therefore, dismiss such impostors from now on, and at least imitate nature, which requires only a simple <term>cooking</term> <note>original: "coctionem"; the central alchemical process of applying steady heat to mature or "ripen" a substance.</note>: and in this way no one will deceive you.

If, therefore, you are now no longer so deceived, and wish to weigh nature a little more deeply, you will without any doubt easily recall to memory what that matter is from which metallic creatures are brought forth. Above all, however, you must rightly understand the metallic nature—why **the Sun** <note>Gold</note>, **the Moon** <note>Silver</note>, **Venus** <note>Copper</note>, **Mars** <note>Iron</note>, **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note>, and **Saturn** <note>Lead</note> are metals and what their origin might be. You must also know beyond doubt that all created things are distributed into three Kingdoms: namely, <term>vegetable</term>, <term>animal</term>, and <term>mineral</term>, and that all things are comprised within these three. For all herbs, all wood, and trees are called **vegetables**; next, all living animals, or whatever is comprised under flesh and blood, are **animals**; finally, all metals and stones, and other things which give off no flame from themselves, are **minerals**, and are comprised under the mineral nature.

You see, therefore, my brother, that all things are divided into three different Natures and are contained within them. Even though they are indeed distributed into three distinct Kingdoms, nevertheless they all have but a single principle from which they are animated or born. For through different <term>cooking</term>, that <term>first matter</term> <note>original: "prima materia"; the primitive, formless base of all matter.</note> is transmuted into three paths, and, according to the quality of the **cooking**, that unique and common substance...

...bestows diverse natures. Therefore again, just as I did before, I faithfully advise you to desert all those sophisticated <term>sublimations</term>, <term>coagulations</term>, and <term>putrefactions</term> <note>These were standard stages in alchemical laboratory work: purifying by vapor, solidifying liquids, and breaking down matter through rot.</note> of the Chemists, along with the ridiculous old wives' tales which they still labor over today. Instead, adhere only to the simple and natural <term>cooking</term> <note>original: "coctioni"; the process of maturing a substance through steady, gentle heat.</note> of the right and true substances. I affirm this to you for certain: this path will lead you to and accompany you toward the true substance of natures. For Nature is exalted or corrected by no other thing or way except only through the natural cooking of **Essences**. For it is, my brother, the **Essence** that is the principal thing, "for the sake of which the bride leads the dances" <note>original: "sponsa choreas ducit"; a metaphorical expression meaning that this Essence is the central cause or the prize that makes the whole effort worthwhile.</note> (that is, upon which the whole business depends). Nevertheless, the sophisticated Chemists are so crude and unskilled in these matters that they cannot comprehend this with their dull senses; instead, day after day, they torment themselves with so many different substances contrary to Nature. These things are entirely unsuitable for the art—it is no different than if I were to try to sow horn, wood, or stone, and hoped for a harvest of natural grain. It is altogether impossible to make the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: "solem & Lunam"; in alchemical shorthand, these always refer to Gold and Silver.</note> from every kind of substance that can be imagined. They can only be made from the single Essence of natures, from which all things obtain their origin and afterward distribute themselves into various substances through various cookings. In this way, every individual thing has its own peculiar cooking within nature. Therefore, if we wish to arrive at the true art of **Chemistry**, we must labor no differently than nature herself performs her labor in the veins of the earth.

Moreover, the ancients made mention of many colors, such as black, white, yellow, and finally red, green, and other colors. This, however, is nothing other than mere deception used to seduce you, so that you are forced to betake yourself to other natural paths and remain stuck in ignorance. For some of the ancients were quite subtle, and they labored specifically to adorn their speeches and ideas with so many allegorical words so that the common people could not easily understand their true intentions.

<header>The Way of Truth.</header>

<sig>Aa 3</sig>

Therefore I exhort you again and again, like a faithful friend, do not allow yourself to be led astray when they speak of the color black—as if you were required to have or take a black substance, or as if the **matter** <note>original: "materia"; the raw physical substance used in the work.</note> must become black, white, and red during the labor itself. Rather, they made mention of "black" for this reason: because the **Essence**, at the very beginning, mixes itself with some glowing physical fire, and once this happens, a liquid is separated from the **Essence** like a kind of black smoke. The Ancients called that black smoke the "black raven," but the **Essence** itself they called the "raven's head" <note>original: "corvinum caput"; a term often signifying the beginning of the "nigredo" or blackening stage, which represents the death or purification of the matter.</note>. 

Thus, it is necessary that you properly observe this aforementioned separation. Indeed, from that separation the ancient sages took the opportunity to investigate the three natures—namely vegetable, animal, and mineral—and they learned so much from it that they realized the separation of these natures was nothing other than a defect of **cooking** <term>cooking</term> <note>original: "coctio"; the natural process of ripening or perfecting a substance through steady heat.</note> within nature. 

Later, they pondered the matter more deeply: specifically, how those **essences** which are less "cooked" by nature might be assisted by common fire in a natural way. They sought a way to use art to perfect the **essences** (which are already combustible) and their liquids (which the Ancients, out of envy <note>In alchemical literature, "envy" refers to the "Envy of the Philosophers," where authors intentionally used confusing names to hide secrets from the uninitiated.</note>, named **Mercury**) which are separated as black from the **Essence**. This was done so that the **Essences** might remain safe and protected from burning by the Liquid, and so the liquid would not separate itself from the **Essence**. 

The Ancients called that "our **sulfur**." For after this preparation, the **Essence** is no longer vegetable nor animal; instead, through **Cooking**, it has become a Mineral **Essence**, and is therefore called **sulfur**. The **Essence** is nothing other than a kind of elementary fire, and its liquid, which is guarded from burning, is true elementary air—so much so that, since air is hot and moist by nature, it is called **Mercury** by the envious. 

Since air embraces the nature of fire within itself, and in turn, elementary fire possesses the nature of air, a true conjunction must be made from these two by adding their likes. These are the physical matters, namely fire and water, which are visible to us. However, these physical elements are nothing other than an aid to the **essences** of the elements, by which they can be naturally reduced to their highest degree. And this gradation is the right and true **Alchemy**, and besides it [none]...

...there is no other way. The pseudo-chemical art of today's pretenders <note>original: "sophistarum"; here referring to charlatans or false alchemists who use trickery rather than natural philosophy.</note> consists of nothing but a waste of money and time.

Some people, however, in place of the simple and true Essence, have established another kind of "essence" with which they have deceived the whole world and caused great harm to many people. Whether they have done rightly and well, I leave to God, the just judge of all. Indeed, it would be much better if so many writings...

One should observe her wondrous operation, not only in the production of metals, but also in the sprouting of all the fruits of the earth. One should place before one's eyes and carefully weigh her <term>circulation</term> <note>The perpetual cyclic movement of moisture and life-force through the earth and atmosphere.</note>—how she works in both summer and winter, spring and autumn, by day and night, through steady heat and warmth. 

For if it were known to you from the very foundation from what things and in what way **Nature** brings each thing to its growth, bloom, fruit, and perfection, then you would also, without difficulty, lay your hands upon the sprouts of the earth. From the very same material which nature uses in the caverns of the earth to produce various sprouts, you would also bring your own intention into effect, according to your own desire.

# ->*The Way of Truth.*<-

Then you are already fit for the true art, and you learn from your own self what exactly the matter and the true labor will be, in which you can safely trust; at the same time, you will see how many useless labors you have endured, where the great blindness in which you entangled yourself will seize you with amazement. Consider therefore, and indeed with the highest diligence, what the **metallic Nature** is, and for what causes metals were made; for they, just like other created things, receive their origin in the same way.

In a similar manner—just as an infant is generated from the male seed in the mother's womb through the benefit of cooking <note>original: "coctionis"; a standard alchemical and medical term for the 'ripening' or 'digestion' of matter by heat</note>, and as a chick is prepared from an egg through the natural brooding of hens—so too do metals have a certain secure substance from which they are born. However, my brother, you must not understand or remain stuck in the suspicion—as false scoundrels have taught you—that **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> and **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"</note> are the primary matter of metals. Indeed, in the veins of the earth where metals grow, neither **Mercury** nor **sulfur** are found; they invented this simply for the purpose of deception, just as they also fashioned an elemental fire called **sulfur**, and a liquid called **Mercury**. In a similar way, they called the elemental fire our **Sun** <note>original: "Solem"; the alchemical symbol for gold</note>, and our liquid the **Moon** <note>original: "Lunam"; the alchemical symbol for silver</note>, and by that very act they led men astray. They also named them "spirit" and "soul." They called the elemental fire the "soul," and the elemental liquid the "spirit," for the reason that elemental things are invisible. Thus also, the soul and the spirit behave no differently. For the soul is an invisible fire, and the spirit is an invisible moisture. They called the external, essential fire and water "bodies" because they are visible and tangible; from these, <term>Workers</term> <note>original: "Laboratores"; referring to practical alchemists who work at the furnace</note> understand metallic bodies and propose them to be dissolved by someone, though this is false. They called them bodies because this visible fire and water are tangible, while elemental fire is spiritual and invisible. Therefore, do not allow yourself to be led astray by those "clever" <note>original: "naſutulis"; literally "those with big noses," a classical idiom for people who are overly critical or think themselves superior in wit</note> Ancients, for they are subtle; unless you guard yourself against them, they will cast you into snares, referring you to metallic bodies when they actually only mean the **metallic essence**.

They show the way toward manifold and diverse materials and substances—

# ->*The Way of Truth.*<-

Bb 3

...they show [many ways], yet a single and true way is sufficient for truth. They propose many and diverse solutions, coagulations, sublimations, calcinations, and putrefactions <note>These are the traditional "Twelve Gates" or stages of alchemy, which the author here dismisses as distractions from the natural process.</note>, all of which are of no consequence, and which Nature does not use in the veins of the earth where metals grow. For venerable Nature does nothing more than cook the **elemental fire**, which is raised up and strengthened by its own **liquor** <note>original: "liquorem"; refers to a primordial fluid or "liquid" essence, not necessarily water.</note>, which it then changes from one nature into another through a constant process of cooking. Thus, as was said before, all things have been distributed into three natures; and although these three natures are physically distinct—namely, the **vegetable**, the **animal**, and the **mineral**—nevertheless, they are elemental, or, in the hidden realm, have arisen from one single substance. They all have a single, unique root from which they flourish and grow, which the Ancients—for the sake of deception—called **prime matter** <note>original: "primam materiam"</note> or **Hyle** <note>original: "Hyle"; a Greek term used by philosophers to describe the fundamental, formless substance of the universe.</note>. It is nothing other than hidden **elemental fire** with its **liquor**, which the Ancients also called **radical moisture** <note>original: "radicalem humorem"; the vital fluid thought to sustain life and existence in all things.</note>, and they spoke not unskillfully: for this liquor is the root of all created things.

Now, the reason this moisture, together with its fire, is divided into different Natures happens in no other way than through various **coctions** <note>original: "coctiones"; the alchemical process of refining or ripening matter through steady, natural heat.</note> that take place in nature. For one Nature is cooked more thoroughly with its elemental fire by means of its moisture than another; of these, the **vegetable Nature** is the least cooked, because its essence is easily burned, and its liquor is very easily separated from the elemental fire by the aid of common fire.

The **animal Nature** is not much different in its degree of cooking, as its essence is likewise easily burned. Therefore, the **mineral nature** is at the highest level of cooking, because the **metallic liquor** is more thoroughly and better united with the elemental fire through cooking than those other two natures mentioned before. For this reason, metals also resist common fire better than created things included under the vegetable and animal nature—as can be seen in the fact that metals placed in fire do not give off the kind of flame that wood does; for its essence <note>original: "essentia"</note> [is bound] with the liquor, just as the metallic moisture with its [own]

...the essence has been cooked, and the joining of the **liquor** <note>the primordial fluid mentioned on the previous page</note> with the essence was not yet metallic, but simply **vegetable** <note>referring to a lower level of maturation, like that of plants, rather than the "mineral" or "metallic" level</note>, which is consumed in black smoke. However, once the essence has reached maturation through natural cooking, it does not remain in that vegetable state; it has now become **metallic**. At this stage, it is consumed by ordinary fire in the form of white smoke—just as you see when **imperfect metals** <note>base metals such as lead or tin</note> release white fumes when they are melted in a furnace.

Therefore, just as the vegetable essence is purified through natural cooking and changes from a black smoke into a white one: in the very same way, and for that exact reason, the **Ancient Sages** <note>original: "Veteres Sapientes"</note> said: *You must first blacken before you whiten; then you must whiten before you redden.* **Reddening** <note>original: "rubrefactio"; the final stage of the alchemical Great Work, representing total perfection</note>, however, should be understood as the act of making a thing full and perfect. This is just like the **Sun** and the **Moon** <note>the alchemical names for Gold and Silver</note>; through cooking, these two noble metals are rendered perfect, their essence is entirely united with the liquor, and they are transformed into pure fires. It is for this reason the Ancients called them "reddenings."

For this very reason, dear friend and brother, do not let the obscurely written books of the Ancients lead you into error. Instead, learn to understand the metallic nature in its simplest, most fundamental form. Once you do this, you will easily grasp the language and phrases used by the Ancients. You will not have to search aimlessly like other **Chemists** <note>original: "Chimicis"; here referring to "puffers" or laboratory workers who followed literal, physical recipes without understanding the underlying natural philosophy</note> who take the words of the Ancients literally. They convince themselves that they must take a physical substance and rot or dissolve it for a long time until the matter turns black. They believe that after this, the substance must be washed, **calcined** <note>burned to a powder</note>, and processed until the blackness vanishes and it begins to whiten. They think the fire must then be increased for an equally long time, and the matter worked until it turns red. This, however, is an entirely false and non-philosophical labor—it is merely **sophistical** <note>deceptive or based on false logic</note>. 

Thus, all the teachings of the Ancient Philosophers are misunderstood as a set of literal chemical recipes by those who do not understand the true nature of things. The Ancients themselves were not displeased by this confusion; in fact, they deliberately wrote and spoke so obscurely that hardly anyone could grasp their true intention. Indeed, they all direct us toward metals and make frequent mention of **Mercury** and **Sulphur**, but they do so only to lead the unworthy astray. And although the true metallic essence...

...it will become matter which, through a certain natural <term>cooking</term> <note>Latin: *coctio*; the alchemical process of maturing a substance through gentle, sustained heat, similar to how fruit ripens</note>, must be raised from the lowest to the highest degree. For experts and those who understand the matter well, they might speak of this without error; nevertheless, for those ignorant of these things, it is a deception, as they have gathered only by conjecture from the books of the Ancients that the essence must be taken from metals. Consequently, one might believe it necessary to torment oneself and labor for a long time until reaching perfection. But that is equally deceptive and is to walk in erroneous paths.

Indeed, the metallic essence can hardly be separated from **perfect metals** <note>gold and silver</note> without damage; for if it were to be separated by fire, then the **liquor** <note>the primordial fluid or "radical moisture"</note> would fly away, and the essence would be burned up along with the earth itself. Even if one tried to separate the essence of **imperfect metals** <note>base metals like lead, tin, or copper</note> using **strong waters** <note>original: *aquas fortes*; corrosive acids like nitric acid</note>, arsenic, **water of life** <note>original: *aqua vitae*; here referring to a concentrated solvent or alcohol</note>, or **lye** <note>original: *lixivium*; a caustic alkaline solution</note>, the essence—along with its liquor—would by no means tolerate that foreign moisture, but would instead be corrupted. For the metallic nature desires nothing foreign, nor can it endure it; if by chance something foreign joins itself with the metallic liquor, it has already fallen from its degree, vanished from the metallic essence, and been placed into the **Sophistic Order** <note>the realm of "sophistry" or false alchemy, where results are superficial or fraudulent rather than truly transformative</note>. You must guard yourself against this above all else.

Furthermore, if you wish to separate the metallic essence from perfect metals by any single way, it would be equally impossible for you. Since the liquor is perfectly cooked with its **elemental fire**, and so united with the "earth" through that cooking, it cannot be separated by fire or water. And even if you tried to set apart that same essence through water, the essence would nonetheless be dissolved with the earth, and then it would coagulate again in the same form in which it existed before. Nor can any moisture be joined with the moisture or liquor of perfect metals in a way that could harm or corrupt them, as usually happens in the liquor of imperfect metals. It is therefore not at all necessary that you sweat so much and torment yourself so greatly, even though the essence with its liquor is no closer to "cooking" in anything else than it is in metals.

Hence the Ancients also said that <term>sulphur</term> <note>in alchemical theory, sulphur represents the active, "soul" principle that gives metals their color and properties</note> exists in nothing other than metals, and for that reason they named the metallic liquor <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: *argentum vivum*; the "mercury" or fluid "spirit" principle of metals</note>...

# ->The Way of Truth.<-

...named <note>completing the word *nuncuparunt* from the previous page</note> it. It truly matters little what names they bestow upon it; for it is nothing other than the **extended eagle** <note>original: *extensa aquila*; likely an alchemical metaphor for a sublimated or "uplifted" volatile substance</note>, or elementary fire with its own elementary **liquor** <note>the fundamental moisture or fluid of the substance</note>. As has been said, this liquor must necessarily be joined with its fire through natural <term>cooking</term> <note>original: *coctio*; the process of maturing a substance through steady, gentle heat</note> until both become indivisible. For the liquor protects the fire from being consumed, so that both may remain constant and endure even in ordinary fire. 

The Ancients named this the **Elixir**, which is essentially the same as a "cooked fire." In this, they spoke well and gave it the correct name: for through this cooking, that which was previously raw and uncooked is perfected and fully matured. This is that entirely "cooked" substance which breaks down imperfect metals and strips them bare, because they cannot withstand the fire.

Therefore, you should not regret spending your effort on this "cooking," since all those labors with which the **chemists** <note>original: *Chimici*; here referring to "vulgar" alchemists who use overly complex or violent methods</note> occupy themselves are perfected through this single, simple cooking alone. Through cooking, the matter is purified, **sublimated** <note>purified into a vapor and resettled</note>, and dissolved; indeed, all things are accomplished through cooking alone. If I am to advise you, then I must also help you: dismiss all other **putrefactions, solutions, coagulations, calcinations, or sublimations** <note>these represent the "Twelve Gates" or standard laboratory operations of traditional alchemy, which the author views as unnecessary distractions</note>. They produce no benefit, only loss, and they cast many into ruin. You can hereafter protect yourself and be cautious of such ruin, as I have written down my simple information coming from a faithful heart. I hold the unwavering hope that you will understand my faithful admonition and what you must further undertake to complete the work and follow Nature's own path in cooking. For I have faithfully laid out for you the clearer, more manifest, right, simple, and true truth, without any fables or parables; and so help me God, I mean well and faithfully by you.

Nevertheless, you must inquire diligently by reading and weighing what I have prescribed for you here. Nor should it surprise you that I call you away entirely from the common and erroneous path: for you must walk another way if you wish to reach natural truth. Therefore, you must humbly and faithfully pray to **God, Thrice Greatest and Best** <note>original: *DEUM TER OPT. MAX.* (Deo Optimo Maximo); a common dedication to the Divine</note>, that He might most mercifully deign to grant you the true **Philosophic spirit** <note>the mental clarity and divine inspiration required to understand alchemical secrets</note>. May He teach you to rightly recognize the **light of nature** <note>original: *lumen naturae*; the wisdom found in the physical world that mirrors divine truth</note>, so that you may at last reach the desired and longed-for end.

->THE END.<-

->[Engraving: The Philosophical Tree]<-

<note>This complex engraving, crafted by Matthäus Merian, serves as a visual map of the "Great Work." At the center is the Tree of the Metals, bearing seven stars representing the planetary metals: Gold (Sun), Silver (Moon), Mercury (Mercury), Copper (Venus), Iron (Mars), Tin (Jupiter), and Lead (Saturn). The surrounding medallions containing a unicorn, eagles, and a mermaid represent the various volatile and fixed states of the matter. At the base, the three figures—a warrior on a lion, a philosopher, and a courtier—represent the different "regimens" or stages of mastery over the sulfurous and mercurial principles.</note>

<margin>The Tree of Knowledge.</margin>

In this single figure, the wise student may behold the entire process of our Art. As the tree draws its nourishment from the earth and is perfected by the heat of the Sun, so too does our **Stone** <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note> grow from a humble "earth" through the steady application of natural heat.

The **Sun** and the **Moon** <note>original: *Sol et Luna*; representing the masculine/Sulfur and feminine/Mercury principles</note> look down upon the work, for without their balanced influence, the tree can bear no fruit. The seven stars are the seven steps of **sublimation** <note>the process of vaporizing and condensing a substance to purify it</note> and fixation. 

Observe the **Unicorn** <note>a symbol of the pure, penetrating Spirit of Mercury</note> and the **Crowned Eagles** <note>symbols of the "volatile" parts of the matter that have been "fixed" or brought under control</note>; these are the spirits that the chemist must learn to bind. At the root of the tree sits the **Lion** <note>the "Red Lion," a symbol of the raw, energetic force of nature or philosophical sulfur</note>, which must be ridden and tamed by the solar warrior. 

<margin>Nature is one.</margin>

All that has been written in many books is here condensed into one image. Do not seek elsewhere for the secret, for the **Tree of the Philosophers** grows in the garden of Nature, requiring only the "water that does not wet the hands" and the gentle fire of the spirit.

...may He bestow His divine help, by which you may be able to happily promote and complete that work to His praise and the correction of your neighbor, with His divine blessing.

If, therefore, you now wish to obtain **wisdom** <note>original: *sapientiam*; in alchemical literature, "Wisdom" often refers to both spiritual insight and the practical knowledge of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> and ask it of God, then, like a wretched sinner, implore His divine blessing, so that you may receive these gifts worthily. For this **treasure**, gift, and storehouse <note>original: *thesaurus, donum, & gaza*</note>, given and blessed by God, is above all earthly treasures. No one receives it from God unless they show themselves to be humble, upright, gentle, and faithful in all things, and unless they keep the divine precepts through God's bounty and blessing, as far as is possible given the weakness of human nature.

# EXHORTATION AND INSTRUCTION
### *for all lovers of this art, in which they may behold themselves, as in a mirror, to see what is practiced and essential in the foundation of the art, whether it be possible or not, so that the true art may be reached, and how matters stand regarding it.*

**E**very one of you, but especially my dearly beloved children now here, I faithfully wish to warn without any deceit: namely, that you should abstain from all fantasies <note>original: "phantasmatibus"; here meaning delusions or unscientific imaginations</note>, and for the sake of these matters, with the help of divine grace, I will diligently instruct you.

First, I wish for you to be requested and faithfully warned to especially beware of the common alchemy of the masses. Indeed, I have experienced so much that I would wish to advise you before you set your hand to this work, because this art is so hidden that no mortal on earth can find it unless the Sun and Moon <note>In alchemy, the "Sun" (Sol) and "Moon" (Luna) often represent Gold and Silver, or more abstractly, the active/masculine and passive/feminine principles (Sulfur and Mercury).</note> come together. Even if you know the stone, but do not know its preparation, then your knowledge of it will profit you nothing; just as if you knew the correct labor but did not know the true stone, your wisdom would then be nothing and lost. Therefore, we shall praise God for this experience and pay Him the thanks that are due.

# ON THE TREASURE AND THE TINCTURE.

**I**f, therefore, you have made such progress in your labor and have attained the **Redness** <note>original: "rubrum"; this refers to the *Rubedo*, the final "red" stage of the Alchemical Great Work signaling the completion of the Stone</note>, you must further understand that you possess a treasure which the whole world could not pay for. For that substance transmutes all metals into true gold, which is much better than the gold produced by the preparation of the **Sun** <note>In alchemy, "Sun" (Sol) refers to gold</note>: for this reason, it also surpasses all other gold in medicine. Indeed, it heals all physical bodies if a grain of that tincture the size of a "poor man's grain" <note>likely referring to a tiny seed or a small measure of weight</note> is drunk in wine; its other virtues are so many they cannot all be recounted.

If you wish to have a tincture for the **Moon** <note>Silver</note>, then take five half-ounces <term>semuncia|a Roman unit of weight equivalent to half an ounce</term> of the **Redness** and cast it upon five hundred half-ounces of well-calcined <note>original: "ustulatae"; burned or heated to a powder</note> silver. Once these are melted together, the whole mass is converted into the tincture and medicine. Then take a half-ounce of that, and cast it upon five hundred half-ounces of **Venus** <note>Copper</note> or other metals, and it is then changed into true silver. Regarding the **Redness** for which you have labored so much: take one part of it to a thousand parts of gold, and it is converted into the tincture and medicine. From that, again add one part to a thousand parts of copper or other metals, and it is then converted into true gold. Furthermore, you have no need to buy gold or silver for this; for you perform the first addition with only a **Drachma** <term>Drachma|a small unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</term>, and from there you always tint more and more.

It is also necessary to know that only two things belong to this art: one is the **Body**, and the other is the **Spirit**. Of these, one is constant <note>stable/fixed</note>, and the other is fleeting or inconstant. These two must be mutually exchanged: that is, the body must become water, and the water must become the body. Then the body becomes water within itself again, and those two must be united with one another—namely the dry with the moist—so that they cannot be separated. But if they are to be joined, then this must be done from one single thing: for any thing assumes nothing other than its own proper nature. It is the same with our art, where the matter is joined by nature, and not made by the hands of men. It [is joined] in...

# EXPLANATION.

**Y**ou should know that this Salt is produced just as that philosopher Geber says: although in the beginning it has no appearance of Salt, it is nonetheless called Salt, and it truly is Salt. It is almost black and foul-smelling—for during the labor it becomes like gore <note>original: "cruoris"; often used to describe the thick, dark state of the matter in the early stages of the Great Work</note>—but through a long duration it is rendered white, pure, and clear. This is the good and noble Salt. Through its own power, it becomes impure and then pure. It dissolves and coagulates itself; that is, as the Philosopher says, it unlocks and locks itself. While it coagulates, it "locks" the art; while it dissolves, it "unlocks" the art. No other salt can do this except this specific Salt of the Philosophers. ## of our Stone.

**A**lexander the Great, King of Macedonia, says thus to us in his Philosophy: Know this, that Salt shall become fire and dryness. Fire coagulates, and its nature—hot, dry, and penetrating even to the bottom—has this property: it whitens what Sol <term>Sol|The alchemical symbol for Gold or the masculine, active principle</term> and Luna <term>Luna|The alchemical symbol for Silver or the feminine, passive principle</term> [contain] through the intensity of the fire and its temperance—that of the natural fire—while Sol drives the redness and Luna drives the whiteness of the bodies toward a spiritual nature, and removes from the bodies all blackness and evil sulfurs. The highest GOD from heaven has not only blessed creatures in this way, but praise, excellence, power, and wisdom are also to be recognized in Salt: He who can dissolve and coagulate <note>original: "solvere & coagulare"; the fundamental alchemical operation of breaking down matter into its components and then recombining them into a higher form</note> knows well the secrets of this art. # FROM THE ELDER, CONCERNING MATTER AND *form, another understanding.*

According to the Philosopher <note>likely referring to Aristotle, the primary authority on "Matter and Form"</note>, those natural things are they which have been born and operated through nature from a natural origin—namely, Matter and Form—just as a stone is from a tree <note>This metaphor suggests that the alchemical stone is a natural outgrowth of its specific "seeds" or origins</note>; Matter and Form, through nature, are different than what nature is properly; and that which is joined from these two is naturally called the nature of our Stone. In its first part, **Lunaria** <note>original: *Lunaria*; a term for the alchemical silver-work or "Moon-plant"</note> powerfully arises from a certain white coagulated earth, as the Philosopher says: see our **Sun** in our **white earth**. However, let the instrument by which our art is joined be water rectified <note>purified by repeated distillation</note> twice or thrice through a <term>B. M.|Balneum Mariae; "Mary's Bath," a gentle heat source similar to a double boiler</term>. The vapor of this water comes from a fatty nature <note>original: *pingui natura*; in alchemy, "fatness" refers to the sulfurous, oily essence of a substance</note>, and the thing nearest to our Stone in this fatness is a hidden substance and a permeating oiliness, which is the ultimate consolation of the human body. And with this water, the internal <term>mercurius|mercury or quicksilver</term> of the metals is to be drawn out. It is concluded, therefore, that our stone is made from the elements of the two lights <note>The Sun (Gold) and the Moon (Silver)</note>, and it is called our <term>argentum vivum|quicksilver or mercury</term>, and **incombustible oil**, the soul and light of bodies; for it grants a unique, eternal light and life to dead and imperfect bodies. Wherefore, my son, I diligently pray and beseech you that you express our quicksilver from our stone, and that you do so with great understanding and agility.

## THE PURIFICATION OF THE EARTH FROM its superfluous Earth.

Beforehand, you should diminish, grind, or <term>calcine|heat to a high temperature to reduce to powder or ash</term> that said earth or matter, so that you may receive its water and spirit. Then shut it in a glass vessel and pour common **water of life** <note>original: *aquam vitae*; likely a strong distilled spirit or solvent used for extraction</note> over it, so that it floats above the matter by the width of three or four fingers. Then move it to the heat for an hour, and distill it by means of a bath. Afterward, <term>calcine</term> the dregs <note>original: *feces*; the solid remains after distillation</note> again, and extract them with their own water just as you did before, until you find nothing more in the earth. Keep that earth for another labor; keep also all those extracted waters, and distill them through a <term>M.B.|Mary's Bath</term> with some gentle fire,

# ANOTHER UNDERSTANDING 
## *of our Stone.*

My sons, know that the stone from which our art is worked has not touched the "earth of the earth" <note>original: *terram terræ*; likely referring to common, unrefined soil</note>, but is caught before it is born. For if it has touched the ground, then it is no longer useful for our art, even though in its first birth it was generated by the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>Sun and Moon are alchemical symbols for Gold and Silver, or the masculine and feminine principles</note>, and was required from the earth in its growth. For it received its first birth in the earth, and yet it is broken, destroyed, and killed; but the **Sun**, the "son" of this work, is generated through vapor by a certain tempered heat and is born anew. It comes into the sea with the wind, lies there, and then comes from the sea to the land with the wind, and quickly vanishes again. 

But if you wish to work with it, you must walk with it and catch it in the air before it reaches the ground, otherwise it evaporates. As soon as it brings itself from the sea to the land, be present immediately, and enclose it in your glass, and work with it as you know how. So that you may recognize it correctly: it comes with wind, rain, and thunder; then observe it well, for it cannot escape you. And although it is born anew every day, it has nevertheless existed since the beginning of the world; however, as soon as it falls to the ground, it is no longer of any use to our art.

## THE SUN IS ITS FATHER, *and the Moon is its mother.* <note>original: "SOL ILLIUS PATER, LUNA vero mater est." This is a famous quote from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, a foundational text of alchemy.</note>

**I**f these two are spirits, then they give birth to the stone: the Sun is <term>sulfur|the active, masculine, and combustible principle in alchemy</term>, and the Moon is <term>mercury|the passive, feminine, and fluid principle</term>, and from these the stone of the wise is made. Make it from one part sulfur and four parts mercury. That sulfur expresses the <term>soul</term> to it, so hold fast to the one—hot and dry sulfur—and the other—cold and moist mercury. Understand me correctly and observe: just as it is dissolved again into water (which was water before), so also the <term>body|the solid physical substance</term> is dissolved into mercury, which was mercury before.

### CONCERNING THE FIRST MATTER, OR THE SEED *of metals, which is included in every seed: they are two, namely the Husband and Wife.*

**M**etals are created things, and likewise are the seeds of the earth, just as other seeds of herbs are. Therefore, it is also necessary for them to be moved in their own earth, in which they generate and bear fruit, just like other created things. For unless that were to happen, then no metal would have grown. And the seed is the metal which has been liquefied from the earth; and if the seed is cast into the earth, then it has its own growth just as other growing things do. Wherefore the earth must be prepared by us—namely, the <term>first matter|prima materia; the original, formless base of all substance</term>—and our seed must be cast into it, and then it will bring forth its fruit according to its kind. Therefore, for generation from one single thing, this motion is required: that is, from the first matter, which earth created and not man, it shall become the stone. Whether it be <term>fixed|stable and resistant to fire</term> (that is, constant) or <term>volatile|tending to evaporate or "flee" when heated</term>, let it conversely be made fixed; that is, let the body become spirit, and the spirit become body. And then from that, the medicine is made,

# AN ELEGANT INSTRUCTION
## ON THE TRUE ART.

According to the opinion of the Philosophers, no "solution" of the body takes place without the <term>coagulation|The process of turning a liquid or gas into a solid state</term> of the spirit: For as soon as the spirit is transmuted into the body, it then possesses its power. Know, however, that since the spirit is still <term>fugitive|Volatile; a substance that easily evaporates or escapes when heated</term>, and not yet "fixed" or constant, it cannot yet perform its work. If, however, it becomes fixed, it works immediately. Therefore, one must act with it just as a baker acts with bread: take a little of the spirit and give it to the body, just as a baker adds <term>leaven|Yeast or a starter culture</term> to flour, and then the leaven converts the entire substance into leaven. Our spirit does the same thing, that is, it ferments...

Therefore, look well to yourself, lest the talent committed to you remains buried <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25), urging the reader not to hide their wealth or knowledge</note>, but trade with it for the honor of God and the benefit of your neighbor: For every man is given to man for help, so that he may be relieved in this way, and God mostly comforts man through other men: Examples of this thing, in the <term>Holy Scripture</term>, we have in Joseph, Habakkuk, Susanna, and others.

## Gloria Mundi.

For just as Almighty God created all things from dryness and moisture: so also this art of ours shall be born through His divine grace. If any man, therefore, now knows the beginning and the course of nature, he already possesses the understanding of our art. But he who is ignorant of that, to him this art seems impossible, although it is as easy as baking bread and brewing beer. <note>The author uses these domestic metaphors to stress that alchemy is not "supernatural" but rather a refinement of natural processes that follow the same laws as cooking or fermentation.</note> Thus, according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, it was from the beginning, when God through His divine providence willed that heaven and earth be made according to wisdom: yet nothing was at hand that had any particular name, except for one single matter alone: that was neither dry nor moist; it was not earth, nor air, nor fire, nor light, nor even darkness, but one matter, like a vapor or a mist, so that it could neither be seen nor touched. It was called <term>Hyle|A term derived from the Greek 'hylē,' meaning wood or raw material; in philosophy, it refers to the fundamental matter of the universe before it has been given form.</term>, or <term>prima materia|The 'First Matter,' the chaotic, unformed substance that alchemists believe is the starting point for creating the Philosopher's Stone.</term>. For where a thing must be made anew out of nothing, then that "nothing" must be united: and it is necessary that it become one thing, from a single thing a palpable matter, and from palpable matter one body, to which a living soul is given, from which, by the grace of God, it receives a form similar to its own kind.

So also it must be noted that when God caused matter to be made, it was then dry and constrained by moisture. If, therefore, anything moist was to grow from it, then it was necessary for it to be separated from the dry, such as fire for itself, and earth also for itself: it was also necessary for the earth to be sprinkled with water if anything moist was to grow from it; for without moisture, nothing can grow. In a similar way, nothing grows in water unless earth is present in which it may stand. If, therefore, water must moisten the earth, then matter must be present there which floats upon the water. For example, the wind <note>In this context, 'wind' often refers to the element of Air, which alchemists believed carried the 'vital spirit' or moisture through the atmosphere.</note> provides water to the creatures; for unless it breathed or existed, then the water would be unable to assist them, and the water also, by flooding the earth all at once, would run back into the sea, where all waters have their return and influx, and from there they never return. All those inhabiting the earth would also be forced to perish and waste away due to dryness and parched conditions. For this reason, one element, without the support of the other, is unable to bring forth any fruits; nor would any thing be present that could compel the wind and drive it to work, for otherwise it would always remain at rest. Therefore, fire is at hand, which forces and drives it to labor and motion,

When we have taken it, then we cut off its hands and feet, and at last we even tear off its head. <note>These violent images are standard alchemical metaphors for the process of "mortification" or "calcination," where the raw material is broken down and stripped of its initial physical form to reach its inner essence.</note> Having done this, we lead it to the **red**, and if we find any blackness in it, we cast it away along with the intestines and the stench. <note>The 'stench' and 'blackness' refer to the *Nigredo* stage, the first phase of the work characterized by decomposition and a foul smell.</note> If it has been purified, then we take its parts and join them together again, and then our **King** <note>The 'King' represents the perfected Stone or the finished Gold.</note> revives; he never dies, and has been made so clarified and subtle that he penetrates all hard bodies and renders them more subtle than himself. Furthermore, you should know that when Almighty God formed Adam and placed him in Paradise, He then showed him two things, and did so with the following words: "Behold, Adam, here are two: one **fixed** <note>original: 'fixatum'; referring to a substance that is stable and does not evaporate in fire.</note>, or constant, and the other **volatile** <note>original: 'fugax'; literally 'fleeing' or 'shunning,' referring to substances that evaporate easily.</note>; do not reveal their hidden virtue to all your sons."

My brother, earth is fixed and water is volatile, just as you see: if any thing is burned, then the inconstant part flies away, and the constant part remains lying there, like ashes. If you pour water on them, then a **lye** <note>original: 'lixivium'; a strong alkaline solution made by leaching ashes, used here to demonstrate how the 'soul' or 'salt' of a substance can be extracted.</note> is made from them, for the efficacy of the ashes passes into the water. If you now clarify the lye, put it into a copper vessel, and allow it to evaporate over a fire, then you will find the matter at the bottom which was previously in the lye; this is the **Salt of the matter**, from which the ash was burned.

**F**irst, it must be known that after Almighty God had, from the beginning, placed our first progenitor Adam, together with all celestial and earthly bodies, into Paradise, and had forbidden him from eating the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of Good and Evil under the penalty of eternal death; at that time, before Adam had transgressed the divine commandment, man had no need for anything at all, because he was still immortal. ...until the fourth **Monarchy** <note>original: "quartam Monarchiam"; a reference to the historical theory of the Four World Empires—usually Babylon, Persia, Greece, and Rome—common in medieval and early modern eschatology.</note>, for a long time, with that unique, most noble Medicine and blessed stone, they preserved their lives in good and healthy condition, intact and protected, and shielded themselves from death. Those who, above others, understood these great divine gifts somewhat better—some of them, I say, lived three hundred years, some four hundred, and others five hundred. Such were Adam and certain of his sons; others lived nine hundred years, like Methuselah and Noah. Even some of their descendants lived beyond that, such as Bacham, Ilrehur, Kalix, Hermes, Geber, Albanus, Ortulanus, Morienus, Alexander in Macedonia <note>Alexander the Great</note>, Anaxagoras, Pythagoras, and many others still, who possessed this noble medicine of the blessed stone, used it, and kept it under the strictest silence. They did not reveal it to the unworthy, who might abuse it for their own malice, just as God has always known how to block the path of petulant, bold, evil, and wicked men at all times.

Therefore, do not wonder that Almighty God has bestowed such a noble art upon the world, by which one can not only heal <term>animal bodies</term> <note>meaning the bodies of living creatures, including humans</note>, but also purify and <term>fix</term> <note>a process of making a volatile substance stable under heat</note> the bodies of metals, transmuting them into the most noble **Sun** and **Moon** <note>alchemical code for Gold and Silver</note>. Indeed, this can be accomplished even more easily than the healing of the fleshly bodies of animals. That this is manifestly true, you will be able to understand and learn more than enough from these three parts of my little book, which I have titled **THE GLORY OF THE WORLD**. Furthermore, you will be able to complete and prove this by your own actions, following the instructions of my doctrine which I have described in these treatises, provided you are willing to follow my teaching, which I have prescribed and handed down to you without any deceit, out of Christian charity and compassion.

But take care that your <term>talent</term> <note>a reference to the biblical Parable of the Talents; here meaning both the material wealth gained and the spiritual knowledge acquired</note> does not remain hidden. Instead, let it be used for the comfort of the poor and needy, for the edification of Christian schools and churches, and for the praise and glory of God, lest the divine wrath of eternal condemnation overwhelm your soul. May God most mercifully deign to turn this away and preserve us in His word.

## TO THE READER.

**L**est, my very dear Reader, you be long detained, but may instead understand my opinion and foundation as conveniently and certainly as possible—and so that the reading may perhaps not become troublesome and tedious to you—observe with the greatest diligence what I have revealed and named to you from the beginning, middle, and end of this, my **little work**. For such a reading will excite in you no boredom, but rather joy. Since, therefore, Almighty God—whose most holy name I am obliged to celebrate at all times, and to whom I am bound to pay due thanks through His divine grace—has granted me these things: the mastery, understanding, and experience of this noble and true art, I am nevertheless moved by brotherly charity and true faithfulness to bring to light this most noble treasure. This is the same treasure which I have attained by God’s grace through manifold expenses and troubles, and I bring it forth so that the minds of slanderers may be corrected, that you might be able to guard yourself from other, less necessary expenses, and so that I also may not be caught out as a false, envious, malevolent, or greedy man.

Therefore, I do not wish this noble treasure and most rich gift of God to die with me, or to be covered in rust and rot away. This is especially true of such an ineffable and consoling secret, which God Himself cherished, poured out with His *rosy blood* <note>original: "roseo sanguine suo"; a common alchemical and mystical metaphor linking the "Red Tincture" or the Blood of Christ to the life-giving power of the Philosopher's Stone</note>, sprinkled in His material time, and commanded that it not be revealed to those unskilled in things and the foolish. Wherefore also this noble medicine could not undeservedly be called the <term>Oil of Mercy</term> <note>original: "oleum misericordiae"; in alchemical lore, this refers to the restorative essence of the Elixir, often linked to the legendary oil sought by Seth from the Tree of Life to heal the dying Adam</note>, and that for many reasons which your own understanding will supply to you.

Therefore, it is not at all necessary that I speak or write more on that matter now; I shall explain, teach, and reveal it in a fitting manner as required, so that no one who is to labor hereafter can err or be seduced any further in <term>Philosophy</term> <note>referring to "Hermetic Philosophy," the contemporary term for the study and practice of alchemy</note>. Rather, they may have a certain, true, and cheerful access to the operation of this art.

Therefore, I, the possessor and communicator of this book, through Christian charity, wish you to be faithfully warned and requested to keep this my ->**PARADISIACAL TABLE**<-, titled **THE GLORY OF THE WORLD**, against all proud, unjust...

**A**s a fundamental conclusion serving as a preface for this book and the information I have shared thus far—and before I move on to this beginning of Philosophy—I will first declare my well-founded opinion. I do this so that any owner of this book may more quickly understand the "crowd" of Philosophers written about below. However, if one cannot sufficiently perceive and understand this opinion of mine, let them then consult the "Philosopher" who follows, where my opinion, along with each of the things previously mentioned, is explained with sufficient detail.

Since I have come to know the blessed and true <term>Art</term> <note>The "Art" refers to alchemy, specifically the "Great Work" of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note> and have recognized its matter and nature—insofar as the Lord has surely granted it—I have therefore communicated the same to you quite clearly in this book out of compassion. I have brought it to light not in a <term>Chancellery style</term> <note>original: "stylo Cancellistico"; referring to the overly formal, dense, and bureaucratic language used by legal officials, which the author avoids in favor of clarity.</note> or with <term>foot-and-a-half long words</term> <note>original: "verbis sesquipedalibus"; a classical idiom for pompous, overly long words.</note>, but rightly and simply, in a plain manner and appearance. Therefore, let everyone pay attention and read with great care, and then they will understand my meaning well. Truly, I am certain that many will try to kill me with insults and slanders, since this Art has never been so plainly revealed since the world was founded as I have now made it common knowledge. It is hidden from all the "wise" and "know-it-alls" <note>original: "nasutulis"; literally "those with big noses," a Latin idiom for critics or people who think they are cleverer than they are.</note> of this world; and to those who read this book of mine, I say it will ring strangely in their ears. I conclude my speech by approaching the very beginning of my opinion.

Sons and disciples of this Art, out of Christian charity and faithfulness, I make it known to you how truly you can and must now know, understand, and find the "arms" and operations of our <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and providing an elixir of life.</note>. Know, therefore, that the Stone of the Philosophers is found in "our trees," even in orchard trees in the air, in all creatures, in animals, and in all growing things that have a vegetable nature—both in that which grows and that which does not grow in its operation. When the Sun and Moon are moved in their <term>distillation</term> <note>In alchemy, distillation is not just a laboratory process but a cosmic cycle where celestial influences "drip" down into the physical world.</note>, it bestows upon all growing and living things their own particular species, nature, and—through divine grace—their efficacy and virtue. All those things, I say, obtain their elegance and form from the power of our **Stone** through the <term>conjunction</term> <note>The union of opposites, symbolized here by the Sun (gold/masculine) and Moon (silver/feminine).</note> of the Sun and Moon. Indeed, the Sun is the father and the Moon is the mother of this Stone; therefore, our children are the Sun and Moon, and they even possess the operation of the Sun and Moon. If, therefore, you now know this operation, form, and essence of that Stone, then you are truly blessed and are true artists. But if you do not understand it, and are ignorant of its operation, nature, and preparation, then I have said nothing to you; rather, beware of the labor of these things—that is my faithful advice—if you are ignorant of the beginning, middle, and end.

You should know and also observe, furthermore, that as soon as the seed of growing things—such as wheat, grain, barley, and other fruits of that kind—has ascended from the earth upward, as if into the air, in its growth by the operation of our Stone and through the maturity of the Sun and Moon; and once it has been made mature and must bring forth fruit again from itself, then, I say, it must be sown into its own natural, prepared soil. First, however, the field must be well-plowed and manured, in which the dung must necessarily rot. For the earth consumes the dung, no differently than humans consume food; it separates the subtle from the gross and draws in the soul of the growing thing, just as the earth receives its nourishment and restores it to the seed that has now been sown back into the earth, just as a nurse suckles infants at her breasts through the efficacy of the food she has eaten. In this way, the earth segregates the good from the evil and feeds other growing things (**FOR THE DESTRUCTION OF ONE IS THE GENERATION OF ANOTHER**) <note>original: "UNIUS ENIM DESTRUCTIO, ALTERIUS EST GENERATIO"; a core philosophical principle stating that for something new to be born, something else must decay or be broken down.</note> as much in this Art as in nature, and in this manner the moisture takes its nourishment from the earth, just as an infant takes milk from its mother or nurse. ## NOW FOLLOWS CONCERNING THE ORI-
## gin of metals.

**D**ear son, by these words I will signify and show to you the origin of metals—namely, from what source they obtained their beginning and their species. Then, from the very foundation, you will perceive how our art orders itself in every form and species, just like the metals themselves. In what manner that thing has its form and essence, I shall propose and teach according to the small measure of my talent and understanding, and as much grace as God has most mercifully bestowed upon me. So that you, Reader, may more easily and quickly arrive at the foundation of the true art, you have before you the visible, the mutable, and the immutable: namely, animals, trees, herbs, stones, metals, and minerals. These can reach no manual completion or perfection of operation except through the sole elements of fire by the help of nature. As you see openly, if the Sun inclines toward the seed, then all fruits burst forth. Then flowers and herbs grow, each according to its species and genus: and just as growing things are augmented from day to day in their growth, in the same way it is also compared with the metals themselves. Since as long as they remain in their natural stones within the earth of the mountains, for so long do they also have their perfect growth from the four elements of fire, and from the splendor of the Sun and Moon. For the Earth conceives the splendor of the Sun within itself, and they <note>the metals</note> are warmed by it just as well as in the common fields; then from that heat a vapor or spirit arises in the earth, which elevates itself upward on high, and takes with it also the swiftest elements, that which might not undeservedly be named the "fifth element": For it is the <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: "Quinta essentia"; the purest and most concentrated essence of a substance, thought to transcend the four physical elements</note>, being as it were the most subtle part separated from the four elements; and from this vapor, moisture exists, and it strives to fly away from the top of the mountains...

### *WHAT IS THE MERCURY OF THE PHILOSOPHERS?*

**M**ercury is nothing other than water and Salt: These two elements have been cooked together for so long a time in natural heat, and that heat joins and coagulates those two. When this is done, it is then called "dry water," which is not moist, nor does it wet anything, and it is named Mercury. However, I speak here not of raw Mercury <note>the common liquid metal quicksilver</note>, but of the Mercury by which the stars of the firmament work into the earth as one body, which is scarcely comprehensible. For the Philosophers say regarding the fifth element <note>the "Quintessence" or purest essence of a substance</note>: This is the virtue of all vegetable things, and its supreme efficacy brings about maturity and perfection; the other and lowest <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: Q. E., an abbreviation for *Quinta Essentia*</note>, which is in the earth and has been made partly corporeal within it, increases and multiplies the seed, which it conceives according to its own species, and thus it grows from the earth. And then the supreme Quintessence comes to the aid of the lowest, which removes the coarseness of the earth and renders the said seed mature. For it dries out the bad humors <note>unbalanced fluids or impurities</note> from the Quintessence of the earth—that is, the Mercury and the <term>Quintessence</term> of Heaven, which is the **Sulfur of the Air**. Therefore the Philosophers say: **Sulfur** is the hardening of **Mercury**, and this is indeed truly the case. Furthermore, they are wife and husband, and here on earth they generate many children. What man does not see this? For if perhaps you think that I wish to keep the truth from you, far be it from me, I say; for which thing I now offer you an example: You have common sulfur, which coagulates common Mercury, just as you see here and in other things; for common sulfur is poisonous, and common Mercury is lethal. How then could you extract anything good, which ought to help another, when that is not quite possible? For both of them stand in need of help for their perfection. ## THE THIRD TREATISE CONCERNING THE *Assembly of Philosophers.* <note>original: turba Philosophorum; one of the earliest and most influential Latin alchemical texts</note>

I will explain all of those authors, word for word, with every point and article in detail, so that every reader may perceive everything that the Philosophers keep writing about, and may thus approach the work more quickly and safely. For these things, praise the Lord, and pray for His divine grace upon me, so that I may better complete the purpose I have begun. Therefore, my reader, so that you are delayed no longer, but may reach the true understanding of this art of ours as well as those prepared Philosophers did: know now that Almighty God himself first handed down this art to our first father, Adam, in Paradise. For as soon as He had created him and placed him in Paradise, He then gave him this art, saying: "Adam, behold, here are two things: that which is above, which is fleeting, and that which is below, which is fixed. In these two, the whole mystery lies hidden. Observe it well, and do not communicate this power and efficacy hidden within it to your children, nor even to your descendants." Those two—

...moreover, together with all creatures under heaven, they shall serve and obey there, and I will subject to you all the virtue and excellence of the whole world: Therefore, when compared with the world, man is called the **Microcosm** <note>original: minor Mundus; literally "Lesser World," the idea that a human being is a reflection of the entire universe</note>.

# II. THE SAYING OF ABEL.

**A**bel, the son of Adam, wrote thus in his beginning: After God had created our father Adam and placed him in Paradise, He subjected all things—herbs, mountains, stones, and animals which were not yet named—to our father Adam, so that he might be the Master of all things. From this, nature seized the opportunity [to show] that man ought to be the mountain of all mountains, the stone of all stones, the tree of all trees, the root of all roots, and the earth of all earths, and he can even be so named and held as the same; for God granted to him that all things are preserved in man.

# III. SETH,

the son of Adam, describes it thus: Know, children, as often as, and how much <term>vinegar</term> <note>In alchemy, "vinegar" often refers to a sharp, acidic solvent rather than common household vinegar</note> is cooked in the art and reduced to ashes, just as much and as often it also extracts and makes the body white. If you cook it well and deprive it of its blackness, then it is transmuted into a stone, which is called the **white stone** <note>original: lapis albus; a stage of the alchemical work representing purity or the ability to transmute metals into silver</note> until it is broken; then dissolve it in well-tempered <term>water of the mouth</term> <note>original: aqua oris; likely a technical term for a specific solvent or "mercurial water"</note>, and know that the whole thing will become whiteness, which **redness** <note>original: rubedo; the final, most potent stage of the Great Work</note> follows; and know that the whole art is made only through the sharpest vinegar, the power of God, and the perfection of the work.

# IV. ISINDRUS,

in his beginning, depicts it thus: The air is quite vast, for the reason that air corrects a thing, whether it becomes thick or thin, hot or moist. For the density of the air arises from there when the Sun sets, or is turned, or is raised; that is, hot or cold, and it is dryness and thinness, and denotes winter and summer.

# V. ANAXAGORAS,

writes thus: I say that the Beginning of all things is God and His goodness. Therefore, the <term>subtlety</term> <note>original: lenitas; implying a light, refined, or spiritual quality of matter</note> of God also reigns under the earth, as does the density of all things, and density under the earth: from the time of creation, subtlety and sincerity represent themselves, while under the earth is density; but subtlety is not perceived except in the body itself.

VI. **SENIOR, also known as PANDOLPHUS**, <note>original: Senior, alias Pandolphus. VII. **ARISTEUS** <note>A legendary figure often appearing in alchemical assemblies like the *Turba Philosophorum*.</note> speaks briefly thus: Know that the earth is round, and not simply flat. For if the earth were straight and flat everywhere, then the sun would shine everywhere and from every side in an instant.

VIII. **PYTHAGORAS** writes to us thus: Note what happens—that which is touched and not seen, and that which does not know what is known and yet is not seen, is the heaven and earth alone. That which is not known is in the world, and the wholeness of it is in the senses, namely in sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. In sight, the difference between white and black is known; in hearing, the wholeness of good and evil is known; likewise in smell, a good odor; in taste, the bitter and the sweet; and in touch, thickness and thinness are known.

IX. **ARISTEUS**, in the second table, indicates the body which I have shown you; he reduces it into thin or soft leaves and pours our "sea-water" over it—that is, the **water of life** <note>original: aqua vitæ; in alchemy, this refers to a potent distilled solvent, not merely alcohol</note>—and cooks it on a gentle fire for so long until its blackness vanishes. By cooking, watering, grinding, and purifying, he works it so long until it becomes white and red <note>These represent the *albedo* (whitening) and *rubedo* (reddening) stages of the Great Work</note>.

X. **PARMENIDES**: Know that the Philosophers have written about many waters, and likewise many little stones and metals, and they wished to deceive you while you are searching. XI. **LUCAS**. Do you not notice what I say, "according to our custom"? It has already been coagulated before. I command you to take the living water from the Moon and draw it to our earth, until it becomes white, and then it shall become our **Magnesia** <term>Magnesia</term> <note>Not the modern chemical magnesium, but a symbolic term for the primordial "hidden earth" or the transformative matter of the Stone</note>, and then the "natures of natures" rejoice.

XXI. **THEOPHILUS**, Take white Magnesia, that is, quicksilver <note>mercury</note> mixed with the Moon <note>silver</note>: grind it for as long as it takes to become a thin water; then cook it until forty days have passed, and then the flower of the Sun <note>Gold, or the active sulfur principle</note> will appear in its full splendor. XXIII. **BASAN**, Lead the golden-colored one <note>the sun or gold</note> to the Bath with his wife <note>mercury or silver</note> after their marriage; and do not make the bath too hot, lest they both be deprived of their senses <note>An alchemical warning: excessive heat can destroy the "vitality" of the substances or cause the vessel to shatter.</note>: therefore, make the bath gentle, and keep it so until the body of the husband and wife becomes one single thing. Cook them for so long until they turn black, then white, and finally red <note>These represent the three primary stages of alchemy: Nigredo (blackness), Albedo (whiteness), and Rubedo (redness).</note>. **XXVI. SIRETUS**: In our art many things are required; that alone is our earth, our water, our black, white, and red earth, so that it may be made; and that with many colors which manifest themselves in it. All things are made through our permanent and living water. Why so? The true Philosophers used no other thing than the *water of life* <note>original: aqua vitae</note>, in which the whole secret work resides, in its own nature, through many operations, such as cooking, heating, distilling, roasting, sublimating, drying, moistening, and making white and red. **XXVII. MOSINUS**: The Philosophers have spoken of and named the art with many words and ways: sometimes in two, and sometimes in three, four, or five words, in which many err who do not understand our Scripture. **XXVIII. **XXIX. ORFULUS**: First, cook the matter with a gentle cooking, lest it grow hotter than eggs under brooding hens <note>a classic alchemical metaphor for the very low, steady heat required to "hatch" the Stone without destroying it</note>, so that its moisture is not burned away and the spirit of our earth is not destroyed. Furthermore, let the vessel be sealed tenaciously, so that the earth may break our body and its spirit may then be extracted, about which many have spoken; thus...

XXX. **BATHON**: If the material of our stone is known, along with the method of cooking and its colors as they reveal themselves—as if to say that it has as many names as it has colors—then in the first cooking it is called "putrefaction" <note>the 'nigredo' or blackening stage where the matter was said to 'die' before being reborn</note>. XXXII. **LEA**, the Prophetess, writes to us in these few words: "You, Nathan, should know that the flower of gold becomes the stone. Therefore, roast it for several days until it becomes like gleaming marble."

XXXIII. **ALKIUS**: Every day, look at the mountains before you—that is, the husband and wife <note>alchemical allegories for sulfur and mercury, or the fixed and the volatile</note>. Go, therefore, to their pits and dig out their earth before it passes away.

XXXIV. **BONELLUS**: To all followers of this art, I say to you out of charity and faithfulness: Abandon the labor of many different processes, for our matter is a single thing, and it is called the living and permanent water. XXXV. **HIERONYMUS**: Haters have destroyed our art and corrupted it with many words; they have even infected the entire work with poison...

**XXXVII. Rejoice, therefore, you unskilled ones, who must seek every day with one stone, with one earth, and sulfur, with alum, lime, saltpeter, etc., with your truth and the quest of the way, and find nothing: for do you not daily see mountains before your eyes, where you could have or obtain stones? The first [place] is found on the summit of two mountains; the second, in a certain mountain; the third, by the road in dung <note>original: stercore; a common alchemical paradox—that the highest matter is found in the filthiest places</note>; the fourth, in trees and air, whose liquid is the Sun and Moon, Mercury, Saturn, and Jupiter <note>Gold, Silver, Quicksilver, Lead, and Tin</note>—and there is only one vessel, one labor, one end, and one middle.

### XXXIX. MORIENES : 
Know that our matter <note>original: res nostra; literally "our thing," a common alchemical term for the substance of the Great Work</note> corresponds no more with human nature than any other thing in creation, because that which is born after putrefaction <note>the stage of "blackness" or decay where the matter dies to be reborn</note> and transmutation has increased. And if it does not putrefy for you, then nothing can be made from it; and all the mastery of the labor is in vain and of no value as long as the customary state <note>original: consuetudo; likely referring to the expected chemical reactions or "habits" of the matter</note> does not first present itself within it. Know therefore, that after you have seen all things and recognized them publicly, it is still impossible for you to arrive at this art until the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: Sol & Luna; symbols for gold/sulfur/masculine and silver/mercury/feminine principles</note> meet and become one thing, just like a body, which is known to **GOD** alone.

### XL. THE EMERALD TABLET: 
It is true, without any lie, and it is the most true of all: that which is above is also that which is below, for accomplishing the miracles of any one thing. And just as all things were born from one stone, so also all things were born from some common mass <note>original: massa; the primal chaos or first matter</note> which embraces within itself all four elements created by God. And among those miracles, this stone was born from that mass: its **Father is the Sun**, and its **mother is the Moon**; the wind carried it in its womb, and the earth is its nurse. Here is the Father of the whole world, its power is complete. If it is transmuted into earth, then the earth separates the most subtle from the hard by means of fire, and this is done gently and with great skill. And then the stone ascends from the earth into heaven, and descends again from heaven to the earth, and receives the power and virtue of both the higher and lower realms. When this is done, you possess the glory and brightness of the whole world; therefore all poverty and darkness shall flee from you. For it overcomes **Mercury** <note>original: Mercurium; here likely meaning the volatile or "quick" nature of spirit</note>, which is subtle, and it penetrates all firm and hard bodies. Thus the world was created; thus I am called **Hermes**, possessing three parts of the philosophy of the whole world.

### XLI. LEPRINUS says: 
The stone must be extracted from a double nature before the **Elixir** <note>a medicinal or transmuting agent</note> can be fashioned from it; that is, it is fixed in one essence and likewise from one matter which God created for this purpose, and without that matter no one can arrive at the art. Both of these parts must be purified before they are joined together again. And if a common body is transmuted into another—namely, the **fixed into the fleeting** <note>original: fixatum in fugax; the "fleeting" refers to volatile substances that evaporate or change easily</note>—from which the medicine is made, then this seasoning, potion, or salt restores all imperfect bodies to health and perfection, whether it is made into salt in the matter, as the lowest thing, which...
