# AN OPEN ENTRANCE
### To the
# CLOSED PALACE OF THE KING.
## AUTHOR’S PREFACE.

**A** *s an Adept <term>Adept: original Latin "Adeptus." In the alchemical tradition, an Adept is someone who has successfully performed the "Great Work" and created the Philosopher's Stone.</term>, I, Anonymus Philalethes <note>The name "Philalethes" is a pseudonym meaning "Lover of Truth." This author is traditionally identified as the American-born alchemist George Starkey.</note>, a Philosopher, possessing the secrets of chemical and physical medicine, in the year of the Redeemed World 1645, and in the twenty-third year of my age, have decided to write this little treatise. I do this to pay the debt I owe to the Sons of Art <note>A traditional term for fellow alchemists and dedicated students of the craft.</note> and to stretch out a hand to those tangled in the Labyrinth of Error. My goal is that it may be clear to the adepts that I am their peer and brother, while those who have been seduced by the trifles of the Sophists <term>Sophists: In this context, "Sophists" refers to "puffers" or false alchemists who use deceitful logic or incorrect materials rather than the true laws of nature.</term> may see and embrace the light, through which they may safely return. Furthermore, I predict that not a few will be enlightened by these labors of mine. These are not Fables, but real Experiments, which I have seen, performed, and known, as any Adept will easily gather from these lines. Therefore, as I write these things for the good of my neighbor, let it be enough that I have declared that no one writing in this art has ever written so clearly. Indeed, I laid down my pen several times while writing, for I would have preferred to hide the truth under the mask of envy <note>original: "sub invidiæ larva." In alchemical literature, "envy" (invidia) refers to the philosophical tradition of keeping secrets hidden from the "unworthy" or the general public to prevent misuse.</note>; but God compelled me, whom I could not resist, who alone knows hearts, and to whom alone be glory forever. From this I conclude without doubt that many in this last age of the world will be blessed by this secret. Because I have written faithfully, I have left no doubt for the studious Novice <term>Novice: original Latin "Tyro," referring to a beginner or someone newly entering the study of alchemy.</term> that is not perfectly satisfied. I also know that there are many who possess this Secret along with me, and I am persuaded there are many more whose friendship I shall shortly attain anew every day, so to speak. May the holy will of God do what pleases Him; I confess myself unworthy that such things should be accomplished through me: nevertheless, in these matters I adore the holy will of God, to whom all created things are bound to be subject, for whose sake alone He created them, and protects what He has created.*

<summary>This preface introduces the author as a young Adept (twenty-three years old) writing in 1645 to reveal alchemical truths that were previously obscured. He claims to write with unprecedented clarity under divine command, aiming to guide "Sons of Art" away from the errors of false alchemists.</summary>

## CHAPTER I.

### On the Necessity of the Sages' Mercury for the Work of the Elixir.

**W**hoever desires to possess this Golden Fleece <note>original: "aureo hoc Vellere." The Golden Fleece of Greek mythology was a common alchemical metaphor for the Great Work or the Philosopher's Stone.</note> should know that our gold-making powder, which we call our Stone, is nothing but gold digested to the highest degree of purity and subtle fixity to which it can be brought by Nature and skillful art; this gold, thus made into an Essence <note>original: "Eſſentificatum."</note>, is called our gold (no longer the common gold), and is the ultimate limit of perfection for both Nature and art. I could cite all the Philosophers on this matter; but I do not need witnesses, because I am myself an adept, and I write more clearly than anyone before me. Let whoever wishes believe it, let whoever can disprove it, let whoever likes criticize it; they will certainly reap this reward: profound ignorance. Subtle minds, I confess, dream of fantasies; but the diligent seeker will find the truth in the simple way of Nature. Therefore, let there be one single principle: that of purifying true gold. Our gold, which we require for our work, is twofold: namely, the mature, fixed yellow Laton <term>Laton: original "Latonem flavum." In alchemy, this refers to a "dead" or impure metallic body—often compared to brass—that must be purified and "whitened" to reach the state of the Stone.</term>, whose heart or center is pure fire, which is why it defends its body in the Fire, in which it receives its purification, so that nothing of it yields to the fire's tyranny or suffers from it. In our Work, this plays the role of the male, and is therefore joined to our whiter, rawer gold—the female seed—into which it releases its own seed, and finally both unite in an indissoluble bond; thus is made our Hermaphrodite <note>The alchemical Hermaphrodite (or Rebis) symbolizes the union of opposites—male and female, fixed and volatile—into a single, perfected substance.</note>, possessing the power of both sexes. Physical gold is therefore "dead" before it is joined with its bride, with whom the coagulating Sulfur <term>Sulfur: One of the three prime principles of alchemy (with Mercury and Salt). Sulfur represents the active, masculine, and "fixing" principle that gives form to the "fluid" Mercury.</term> which is within the gold is turned inside-out. Thus the Height is hidden and the Depth is revealed. Thus the fixed becomes volatile for a time, so that it may afterwards possess a nobler state by inheritance, in which it attains a superior fixity. It is clear, therefore, that the entire Secret consists in Mercury, about which the Philosopher says: "In Mercury," he says, "is everything that the Wise seek." <note>original: "In Mercurio eſt... quicquid quærunt Sapientes."</note>

### CHAPTER II.

## *On the Constituent Principles of the Sages' Mercury.*

The intention of some who work in this art is to purify Mercury in various ways: for some sublimate it by adding salts, some remove various dregs, and others attempt to bring it to life by itself alone. Through such repeated operations, they believe they have created the Mercury of the Philosophers, but they err, because they do not work within nature, which alone is improved within its own Nature. Therefore, let them know that our water is composed of many things, yet it is a single thing made from diverse Substances thickened into one Essence. Specifically, there is required in our Water: first, Fire; second, the liquid of Vegetable Saturnia <term>Vegetable Saturnia: original "Saturnia vegetabilis." "Saturn" is the alchemical name for lead, but "Vegetable Saturnia" refers to a specific "living" mineral solvent, often associated by later scholars with the starry regulus of antimony.</term>; third, the bond of Mercury. The Fire is of mineral Sulfur, and yet it is not strictly mineral, let alone metallic; but it is a medium between mineral and metal, participating in neither, a Chaos or Spirit. For our fiery Dragon <note>original: "Draco noster igneus." The dragon is a common alchemical symbol for volatile or acidic substances that must be "tamed."</note>, which overcomes all things, is nevertheless penetrated by the scent of Vegetable Saturnia, whose Blood thickens with the juice of Saturnia into one marvelous body; yet it is not a body, because it is entirely volatile, nor is it a spirit, because in the fire it resembles a molten metal. It is, therefore, truly a Chaos, which stands toward all metals as a mother.

## CHAPTER III.

### *On the Steel of the Sages.*

**T**he wise Magi <note>Ancient practitioners of the sacred arts.</note> have handed down many things about their Steel <term>Chalybs: Steel; in alchemy, this refers to a specific mineral or metal (often related to iron or antimony) that "attracts" the spiritual essence of gold.</term> to posterity, and they attributed no small importance to it; for this reason, there is no small conflict among the common sort of Alchemists as to what is to be understood by the name of Steel. Various people have given various interpretations of this. The Author of the *New Light* <note>original: "Author Novi Luminis." This refers to Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), an influential Polish alchemist.</note> wrote of this candidly, yet obscurely. I, so as not to hide anything out of envy from the seekers of the Art, shall describe it sincerely. Our Steel is the true Key of our Work, without which the fire of the lamp can be lit by no art. It is the ore of gold, a spirit exceptionally pure above all others; it is an infernal fire, secret, highly volatile in its kind, a wonder of the world, a system of superior virtues within inferior things <note>A reference to the "as above, so below" principle of Hermeticism.</note>, which is why the Almighty marked it with a notable sign, whose birth is announced through the East on the Horizon of its philosophical Hemisphere. The Sages saw it in the Age of the Magi and were struck with wonder, and immediately they recognized the most serene King born in the world. You, when you have seen his star, follow it even to the cradle; there you will see the beautiful infant,

## Chapter IV.
### On the Magnet of the Sages.

**J**ust as Steel <note>original: "Chalybs"; in alchemy, this usually refers to a specific preparation of iron or a "star-regulated" mineral.</note> is drawn to the Magnet, and the Magnet spontaneously turns toward the Steel, so also the Magnet of the Sages attracts their Steel. Therefore, just as I have taught that the Steel is the Ore of gold, likewise our Magnet is the true Ore of our Steel. I further make known that our Magnet has a hidden center abounding in Salt, which Salt is a solvent <note>original: "menstruum"; a liquid used to dissolve or extract essence from solids.</note> in the Sphere of the Moon <note>The "Sphere of the Moon" often refers to the silver-like or white stage of the process.</note>, which knows how to calcine gold. This center turns with an archetypal desire toward the Pole, in which the power of the Steel is exalted by degrees. In the Pole is the Heart of Mercury, which is the true Fire, in which is the rest of its Lord; sailing through this great sea, may he reach both Indias <note>A metaphor for the East and West, implying a complete or universal mastery over the material.</note>, and direct his course by the sight of the North Star, which our Magnet will cause to appear to you. The wise man will rejoice, yet the fool values these things little, nor will he learn wisdom, even though he has seen the central Pole turned outward, marked with the notable sign of the Almighty. They are so stiff-necked that even if they see signs and miracles, they still do not lay aside their false reasonings <note>original: "Sophismata"</note> nor enter the right path.

## Chapter V.
### The Chaos of the Philosophers.

**L**et the son of the Philosophers hear the Sages unanimously concluding that this Work is to be likened to the Creation of the Universe. In the beginning, therefore, **GOD** created the Heaven and the Earth, and the Earth was empty and void, and the Spirit of **GOD** moved over the face of the waters, and **GOD** said: Let there be Light, and there was Light. These words will be enough for the son of the Art. For indeed, Heaven must be joined with Earth upon the bed of friendship.

# Chapter VI.

## *The Air of the Sages.*

**T**he expanse or Firmament is called "Air" in the Sacred Scriptures. Likewise, our Chaos is named Air, and that not without a notable Secret, because just as the Firmamental Air is the Separator of the Waters, so also is our Air. Therefore, our Work is truly a system of the Greater World <note>term: Macrocosm; the universe as a whole, which the alchemist seeks to replicate in miniature.</note>. For just as the Waters beneath the Firmament are seen and appear to us who live upon the Earth, but the upper Waters escape our sight because they are so far distant from us; likewise also in our microcosm <note>term: Microcosm; the "small world" or the alchemical vessel, which mirrors the laws of the universe.</note> there are mineral waters outside the center, which are visible; but those which are shut up within escape our sight, and yet they truly exist. These are those of which the Author of the *New Light* <note>original: "Author Novi Luminis"; referring to Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a famous alchemist whose works Philalethes frequently cites.</note> speaks; which exist, but do not appear, until it pleases the Artist. Therefore, just as the Air distinguishes between the Waters, so also our air [distinguishes] all the extra-central [waters]—

...ble counsel <note>original: "nobili consilio"</note>, which prohibits the entrance to the waters located in the center. If you know how to water this dry Earth with water of its own kind, you will loosen the pores of the Earth, and this external thief, along with the workers of wickedness, will be cast out. The water will be purged by the addition of true Sulfur from the "leprous" filth <note>Base metals were often described as "leprous" or "sick," needing the Stone to "cure" them into gold.</note> and from the superfluous "dropsical" moisture. Then you will have in your power the small Fountain of the Count of Trevisan <note>Bernard Trevisan (1406–1490) was a famous alchemist who wrote of a fountain where the King must bathe to be transformed.</note>, whose waters are specifically dedicated to the Virgin Diana <note>The goddess Diana represents the "lunar" or silver stage of the process, characterized by a brilliant white color.</note>. This thief is a wicked creature armed with a poisonous, arsenical malice, from which the winged youth <note>Often a symbol for the volatile spirit or Mercury.</note> recoils and flees. And although the central water belongs to this Bride, he does not dare to show his most burning Love toward her because of the snares of the robber, whose tricks are truly inescapable. 

Let Diana be favorable to you here; she knows how to tame wild beasts. Her two doves will temper the malice of the air with their wings, so that the youth may easily enter through the paths <note>original: "odos"</note>; he strikes immediately through those paths and stirs up a gloomy cloud. You must bring the waves over it until it reaches the whiteness of the Moon, and thus the Darkness, which was upon the face of the abyss, will be dispersed by the spirit moving itself in the waters. Thus, by **GOD’S** command, Light will appear. Separate the Light from the Darkness for the seventh time, and this Sages’ creation of Mercury will be complete. The seventh Day will be your Sabbath of rest, from which time until the revolution of a year you may expect the birth of the supernatural Son of the Sun <note>The "Philosophers' Stone," often described as the "Son of the Sun."</note>, who will come into the world at the end of the ages to free all his brothers from their stain.

## CHAPTER VIII.

### *Concerning the labor and tedium of the first preparation.*

**S**ome ignorant <term>seekers of chemistry</term> <note>original: "Chemicolæ" — a derogatory term for those who practice the craft without the philosophical understanding.</note> dream that the whole work from beginning to end is mere recreation full of delight, and they believe labor to be outside the boundaries of this art; but let them safely enjoy their own opinion. In the Work, which they have so easily imagined for themselves, they will surely reap an empty harvest from their idle operation. We know, for instance, that after the divine Blessing and a good root <note>Meaning a correct starting material or fundamental principle.</note>, labor, industry, and diligence take the first place. Nor indeed will the "labor of the household" (which should rather be considered play or a recreation of the mind) grant what we so greatly desire according to our wishes; rather, as <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founding figure of alchemy.</note> says, one must not spare soul or labor. Otherwise, what the wise man predicted in parables will be verified: namely, that the desire of the idle man will kill him. Nor is it a wonder if so many men practicing **Alchemy** are reduced to poverty; for they flee from labor, and they do not endure the expenses. We, however, who know these things and have worked them out, have found for a certainty that no labor is more tedious than our first preparation. Therefore <term>Morienus</term> <note>A legendary 7th-century alchemist known for his dialogue with King Khalid.</note> seriously exhorts the King on this matter, saying: "Many of the Sages..."

# CHAPTER X.
## *Concerning the Sulfur which is in the Sophic Mercury.*

**M**ore than anything else, this is marvelous: that in our <term>Mercury</term> <note>Specifically "Sophic Mercury," the specialized solvent used by alchemists.</note> there exists not only an actual, but also an active <term>Sulfur</term>; and yet it retains all the proportions and the form of Mercury. For this reason, it is necessary to introduce "form" into it through our preparation; this form is the <term>metallic Sulfur</term>, which Sulfur is the fire that causes the compound <term>Sun</term> to putrefy. <note>In the alchemical process, "putrefaction" or breaking down the gold is a necessary first step toward transformation.</note> This sulfurous Fire is the spiritual seed which our virgin (nevertheless remaining undefiled) has contracted, because incorrupt Virginity can admit spiritual love, according to the author of the *Hermetic Secret* <note>original: "Arcani Hermetici Authorem" — likely referring to Jean d'Espagnet, a prominent alchemical writer.</note> and Experience itself. By reason of this Sulfur, it is a <term>Hermaphrodite</term>, because the same Mercury includes at the same time both the active and the passive principle, made visible through the same degree of digestion. <note>The "Hermaphrodite" symbol represents a substance that contains both the "male" active principle (Sulfur) and the "female" passive principle (Mercury) perfectly balanced.</note> Indeed, when joined with the Sun, it softens, liquefies, and dissolves it, with the heat tempered to the requirements of the compound. By the same Fire, it coagulates itself, and in its coagulation, it gives the Sun, and that according to the pleasure of the Operation. This will perhaps seem incredible to you, but it is true: namely, that the homogeneous Mercury, pure and clean, pregnant with internal Sulfur through our artifice, coagulates itself solely by the application of suitable heat, in the manner of the cream of milk <note>original: "floris lactis" — literally "the flower of milk."</note>, with a subtle earth floating, as it were, upon the waters. But when joined with the Sun, not only is it not coagulated, but the compound will be seen to grow softer every day, until, the bodies being nearly dissolved, the spirits begin to coagulate in a very black color and with a most foul odor. It is evident, therefore, that this spiritual metallic Sulfur is truly the "first mover" <note>original: "movens primum" — a philosophical term for the primary cause of motion or change.</note> which turns the wheel and spins the axis in a circle. This Sulfur is truly <term>volatile Gold</term>; it is not yet sufficiently digested, but it is pure enough, wherefore by simple digestion it passes into the Sun. But, if it be joined to the Sun...

## CHAPTER XI.
### *On the Discovery of the Perfect Mastery.*

**T**he Sages of old, as many as attained this Art <term>without the help of books</term> <note>This refers to the "Adepti" or Adepts, who were believed to have discovered the secrets of alchemy through nature and divine grace rather than written instructions.</note>, were led to its attainment in this way by the will of GOD. For I cannot persuade myself that it came to any by immediate revelation, unless perhaps Solomon possessed it, which I would rather leave to a Judge to decide than determine myself. And yet, even if he possessed it, what prevents him from having arrived at it by investigation, since he asked for Wisdom alone? GOD had given him Wisdom in such a way that with it he also possessed riches and peace. Because he searched out the nature of plants and trees, from the Cedar in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows on the wall <note>A reference to 1 Kings 4:33, emphasizing Solomon's total knowledge of the natural world.</note>, who of sound mind will deny that he likewise understood the natures of minerals? The knowledge of minerals is no less pleasant than that of plants. But to the matter at hand. We say that it is likely to be believed that the first <term>Adepts</term> <note>Those who have successfully completed the "Great Work" of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note> who possessed this <term>Mastery</term> <note>original: "Magisterio" — the "Great Work" or the process of alchemical transformation.</note>—among whom was **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure considered the father of alchemy.</note>—lacked a supply of books. They first sought not "more-than-perfection," but only the simple exaltation of imperfect metals to the royal state <note>The "royal state" refers to Gold, the "King" of metals.</note>. And when they perceived that all metallic things are of <term>Mercurial Origin</term> <note>The alchemical theory that all metals are composed of varying proportions of Mercury and Sulfur.</note>, and that **Mercury** is most similar to the most perfect gold in weight and homogeneity, they were thus prepared to <term>digest</term> <note>In alchemy, "digestion" refers to the application of steady, gentle heat over a long period to mature a substance.</note> this Mercury to the ripeness of Gold. However, they were able to accomplish it by no ordinary Fire. Wherefore they considered within themselves that, besides external heat, at least an internal fire is required to fulfill their wishes. And so they sought this in many things. First, they distilled extremely hot "Waters" from lesser minerals, and with these they corroded the Mercury; but they could achieve nothing by this way through any art that would cause the Mercury to change its internal properties, because all corrosive waters are external...

Therefore, seeking further for the active Sulfur, the **Magi** <note>The Sages or wise alchemists of antiquity.</note> finally searched for and found it most deeply hidden in the **House of Aries** <note>original: *Domo Arietis*; the astrological sign Aries is ruled by Mars, and thus refers here to the metal Iron.</note>. This was most greedily received by the Offspring of Saturn, which—being the purest and tenderest metallic matter and closest to the first metallic Being—is deprived of all actual Sulfur, yet possesses the potential to receive Sulfur. Therefore, like a **Magnet**, it draws this to itself, and absorbs and hides it in its belly; and the Almighty, to most highly adorn this **Work** <term>Opus</term> <note>The "Great Work" of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, impresses His **Royal Seal** <note>original: *Regium ſuum Sigillum*; a reference to the star-shaped crystalline pattern that forms on the surface of purified Antimony, known as the "Star Regulus."</note> upon it. Then the Magi immediately rejoiced when they saw the Sulfur not only discovered but also prepared. Finally, they attempted to purge Mercury by means of this, but the outcome did not correspond to their hopes, because the arsenical malignancy was still mixed with this Sulfur absorbed in the offspring of Saturn; although this was now scant compared to the quantity it had in its mineral nature, it nevertheless prohibited all entry. Therefore, they tried to temper this malignancy of the air by the **Doves of Diana** <note>original: *Columbas Dianæ*; an alchemical metaphor for silver or a specific refined metallic spirit used to purify the mixture.</note>, and the result answered their prayers. Then they mingled life with life, and moistened the dry by the liquid; they also sharpened the passive by the active, and quickened the dead by the living. Thus the sky was clouded for a time, but after heavy rains it became clear again. Here the **Hermaphroditic** Mercury <note>A substance containing both male (Sulfur/Fixed) and female (Mercury/Volatile) principles in balance.</note> emerged. Therefore, they placed this in the fire, and in a not very long time they coagulated it, and in its coagulation, they found the purest **Sun** <term>Sol</term> <note>Gold</note> and **Moon** <term>Luna</term> <note>Silver</note>. At last, returning to themselves, they reflected that...

This purified **Mercury**, being not yet coagulated, was not yet a metal, but having been made volatile, it would leave no residue in the bottom of the vessel during its distillation. For this reason, they wed these two to one another, enclosed them in glass, placed them in the fire, and directed the work according to the demands of nature for a long time. Thus the dead was made alive, and the living became dead; the body rotted, and the spirit rose again in glory, and the soul was finally exalted into the **Fifth Essence** <term>Quintessence</term> <note>The purest and most concentrated essence of a substance, believed to be the "fifth element."</note>, a supreme **Medicine** for animals, metals, and vegetables.

## C H A P T E R XII.

# On the Way to Making the Perfect Mastery in General.

**W**e must give immortal thanks to God that He has shown us these secrets of Nature, which He has hidden from the eyes of many. Therefore, those things which have been given to us freely by that Great Giver, we shall freely and faithfully reveal to other students. You should know, therefore, that the greatest Secret of our Operation is nothing other than the **Cohobation of Natures** <term>Cohobation</term> <note>original: *Cohobationem Naturarum*; the process of repeatedly distilling a liquid from its solid residue and pouring it back on, to concentrate the essence.</note>, of one upon the other, until the most digested Virtue is extracted from the digested substance by the crude. For this, however, several things are required: First, an exact comparison, preparation, and adaptation of the things entering the work. Second, a good disposition of external things. Third, a good **regimen** <note>The management of the heat and timing of the furnace.</note> is required for the things thus prepared. Fourth, a foreknowledge of the things appearing in the **Work** <term>Opus</term> is desired, lest one proceed blindly. Fifth, patience, lest the work be hurried or managed precipitously. ## CHAPTER XIII.
### On the Use of Mature Sulfur in the Work of the Elixir.

**W**e have spoken of the necessity of **Mercury**, and we have delivered many Secrets regarding **Mercury**, which before my time were quite barren in the world, because almost all Chemical books swarm either with obscure riddles, or deceptive operations, or finally with a heap of scurrilous <note>original: *scabiosorum*; literally "scabby" or "mangy," used here to describe low-quality or irritatingly confusing writing.</note> words. But I have not acted in this way, resigning my true will in this matter to the divine pleasure, as I believe that I am the one intended to unlock these treasures in this final period of the world; therefore, I no longer fear lest the art become cheapened—far be it! This cannot happen. For true **Wisdom** <note>original: *Sapientia*; often personified in alchemical texts as a divine guide.</note> guards herself in eternal honor. Would that **gold** and **silver**, that great idol worshipped until now by the whole world, might finally become as cheap as dung! Then we, who are skilled in these matters, would not study so hard to remain hidden—we who judge ourselves (mourning and sighing!) to have already received the very curse of Cain <note>A reference to Genesis 4:14; the author compares the life of a successful alchemist to Cain’s exile, being a "fugitive and a wanderer" to avoid being hunted for his wealth.</note>; namely, as if we were driven away from the face of the Lord and from the pleasant society which we once enjoyed with friends without fear. But now we are driven as if possessed by furies, nor can we believe ourselves safe in any place for long; often we also make the complaint of Cain to God, lamenting:

> Behold, whoever finds me will kill me.

Not daring to take on the care of a family, we wander as vagabonds through various nations, and we obtain no certain dwelling. And although we possess all things, yet we are permitted to use few; in what then are we happy? Except for contemplation alone, in which there is great satisfaction of the mind. Many believe—those who are strangers to the art—that if they possessed it, they would do this and that; and so we once believed, but having been made more cautious by dangers, we have chosen a more secret method. For he who has once escaped imminent danger to his life, for the rest—believe me—will be rendered wiser as long as he lives. As the proverb says: bachelors' wives and maidens' children are well managed and raised <note>original: *Uxores... cælibum, puerique virginum bene veniuntur ac educantur*; a common early modern proverb meaning it is easy for those without responsibilities to criticize how others handle them.</note>. I have found the world placed in a most malignant state, such that almost no one is found, however honest a face he wears or however much he speaks of public affairs, who does not propose some sordid and unworthy private aim for himself. ...he can accomplish anything, even in works of mercy, unless he is willing to risk his life. I experienced this recently in certain foreign lands, where I administered medicine to several dying people who were abandoned and afflicted with bodily miseries. They recovered their health to a miraculous degree, but immediately a rumor spread concerning the <term>Elixir of the Sages</term> <note>original: *Elixiri Sophorum*; the fabled philosopher's stone in liquid form, capable of healing all diseases and transmuting metals.</note>. This resulted in me fleeing by night more than once with the greatest difficulty—changing my clothes, shaving my head, wearing a wig, and adopting an assumed name. Otherwise, I would have fallen into the hands of most wicked men lying in wait for me, driven by mere suspicion joined with a most bitter thirst for Gold. I could recount many such tales which will seem ridiculous to some. For they will say, "If I knew this or that, I would act differently." Yet let them know that it is a burden for the ingenious to associate with the slow-witted. For the ingenious are crafty, subtle, perceptive—some are as sharp-eyed as **Argus** <note>In Greek mythology, Argus Panoptes was a giant with a hundred eyes, representing an all-seeing guardian.</note>, some are curious, and some are <term>Machiavellian</term> <note>Followers of the principles of Niccolò Machiavelli, implying those who are cunning, cynical, or calculating in social and political affairs.</note>, who inquire most deeply into the lives, habits, and actions of men. It is extremely difficult to remain hidden from such people, especially if any degree of personal familiarity exists.

If I were to speak to someone who believes these things about himself—namely, that he would act in this or that way if he possessed the stone—and said: "You are an acquaintance of a certain Adept," he would immediately think it over and reply: "That is impossible. Perhaps I might live to see one once, but to live familiarly with one is impossible without me smelling it out." You who believe this of yourself—do you not believe that others possess an equal perceptiveness to discern you? For one must associate with some people, otherwise you will appear as a <term>Cynic</term> or like <term>Diogenes</term> <note>A reference to Diogenes of Sinope, the Greek philosopher who lived in a tub and rejected all social conventions; the author suggests that complete isolation makes one look like a suspicious eccentric.</note>. 

If you consort with the common people, it is beneath your dignity. But if you form friendships among the prudent, you must be exceedingly cautious, lest others discern you with the same cleverness by which you believe you could fish out another <term>Adept</term> <note>original: *Adeptum*; one who has attained the secret of the Great Work.</note> (even if the secret is unknown to them), provided you could gain his familiar company. Furthermore, you will not easily recognize a suspicion once it is conceived, at least not without grave inconvenience. Even a slight conjecture will suffice for them to prepare snares for you. Such is the wickedness in men that we have not infrequently known certain people to be strangled by a noose, even though they were total strangers to the Art. It was enough that certain desperate men had heard a rumor about the art, in the skill of which those victims were said to be named. It would be tedious to recount everything,

...which things we ourselves have experienced, seen, and heard concerning this matter; even more so in this age of the world than in any prior one. Who does not lay claim to <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: *Alchimiam*; the art of transmuting base metals into gold and finding a universal cure.</note>, to the point that you would hardly dare to move a foot unless you wish to be betrayed, provided you have transacted anything in secret. Men’s minds are not so stupid; though like children playing, they might say, "Our eyes are closed, come, we do not see," yet if you approach, they will see enough from even one corner of an eye to create the greatest misery for you. Truly fine silver, produced by our art, is brought from no other place. The best that is brought from **Spain** is only slightly better in quality than <term>English Sterling</term> <note>original: *Sterling Anglicanum*; the high-standard silver used in English coinage.</note>, and that is in the form of crude coinage which is transported by theft, as the laws of those regions prohibit its export. If, therefore, you sell a bounty of pure silver, you have already betrayed yourself; but if you adulterate it (not being a <term>metallurgist</term> <note>original: *metallurgus*; a professional refiner or worker of metals licensed by the state.</note>), you are liable to the punishment of death according to the laws of **England** and **Holland** and nearly all nations. These laws provide that every debasement of Gold and Silver—even if it meets the weight—is judged a capital crime unless performed by a professed and licensed metal-worker. We know this because when we once attempted to sell as much as 600 pounds of the purest silver outside our own country, dressed like a merchant (for we did not dare to adulterate it, because nearly every region has its own standard for the quality of silver and gold which the metal-workers know easily, so much so that if we pretended it was brought from here or there, they would immediately recognize it by a test and seize the seller), those to whom we offered it immediately said to us that the silver was **made by art** <note>original: *arte factum*; meaning it was created through alchemical transmutation rather than mined from the earth.</note>. When we asked the reason why they asserted this, they replied nothing else than that silver which comes from England...

Whether it is brought from *Spain*, etc., we are no longer going to learn how to distinguish; but this is of no such kind. Hearing this, we secretly withdrew ourselves and left behind both the silver and its price, never to be reclaimed. Furthermore, if you pretend that a great weight of *Gold*—and especially *Silver*—was brought from elsewhere, this cannot happen without rumor. The *Shipmaster* will say, "Such a quantity of *Silver* was not brought by me, nor can it enter a ship without everyone's knowledge." And when others who usually trade there hear of it, they will laugh and say, "What? Thus, it will be publicized immediately, not just in one region, but in all those surrounding it.

We, having been taught by these dangers, have decided to remain hidden, and we shall communicate with you—who dreams of such an *Art*—so that we may see what you will devise for the public good once you have attained it. We say, therefore, that just as I previously taught that *Mercury* <term>Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the fluid, feminine, and transformative principle of matter.</note> is necessary in the work, and brought forth such things concerning *Mercury* as no antiquity before me has done; so now I make it known that *Sulphur* <term>Sulphur</term> <note>The masculine, active, and combustible principle that "fixes" or solidifies the fluid Mercury.</note> is required on the other hand, without which *Mercury* will never receive a profitable, supernatural congealing in the work. 

This *Sulphur* plays the part of the male <note>original: *maris*; meaning the masculine seed in the alchemical marriage of elements.</note> in our Work, and without it, whoever attempts the transmuting art attempts everything in vain. All the *Sages* <note>original: *Sophis*; referring to the "Philosophers" or master alchemists.</note> affirm that no *Tincture* <note>A substance capable of changing the color and nature of a base metal into gold.</note> can be made without its own "brass," which "brass" is, without any ambiguity, called gold. 

Hence the noble *Sendivogius* <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a renowned Polish alchemist whose works were highly influential on Isaac Newton and others.</note> says: *The wise man,* he says, *recognizes our stone even among dung, and the ignorant man does not believe it to be in gold even though it is there.* In gold, you must understand, which is the *Gold of the Sages*, the tincture of "goldness" lies hidden. Although this becomes a most perfected body, it is nevertheless "made raw" <note>original: *incrudatur*; a process of returning a metal to a "raw" or "primordial" state so it can be transformed.</note> in our Mercury alone, and from Mercury it receives the multiplication of its seed, not so much in weight as in virtue. 

And although many of the *Sages* seem to deny this *Sophic* <note>Refers to the "Philosophical" substances (like Sophic Gold) which are prepared by the alchemist, as opposed to common, "vulgar" materials.</note> truth, it is nonetheless exactly as I have said. They say, for instance, that common *Gold* is dead, while their own is living; in the same way, a grain of wheat is dead—that is, the activity germinating within it lies suppressed and yields—and thus it would remain forever if it were kept in the dry surrounding air. But let it be cast into the earth, and it soon receives a fermental life: it swells, softens, and germinates. So further...

The matter stands with **Our Gold** <note>original: *Auro nostro*; a term used to distinguish the alchemist's prepared material from common gold.</note> as it does with a grain of seed: it is "dead," which is to say that its life-giving power is sealed beneath a bodily husk, much like a grain—though there is a great difference between a vegetable grain and metallic gold. But just as a grain remains forever unchanged in dry air, is destroyed in fire, and can only be brought back to life in **our water**, so too is our grain "living." This is like *Wheat* <note>original: *Triticum*</note> sown in a field; it changes its name to "seed" for the farmer, whereas as long as it remained in the barn, it was "grain," suited for baking bread or other uses just as much as for sowing.

In the same way, **Gold**, as long as it is seen in the form of a ring, a vessel, or a coin, is common gold. In the first sense, it is called "dead" because it would remain unchanged until the end of the world. In the second sense, it is called "living" because it is then in *potential*—a potential that can be brought into action within a few days. Then, the gold will no longer be gold, but the **Chaos of the Sages** <term>Chaos of the Sages</term> <note>A term for the "Prime Matter" or the state of the substance when it has been broken down into its fundamental, unformed components before being rebuilt into the Philosopher's Stone.</note>.

Rightly, therefore, do the Philosophers say that **Philosophical Gold** differs from common gold, and this difference consists in its composition. For just as a man is called "dead" once he has received a sentence of death, so Gold is called "living" when it is mixed in such a composition and placed under such a fire that it must necessarily receive germinating life shortly—indeed, within a few days, it will demonstrate the actions of beginning life.

Therefore, those same Sages who say their Gold is "living" command you, the seeker of the Art, to **bring the dead back to life**. If you know this, and have prepared the active agent, and have correctly mixed your gold, it will quickly become living. In this **vivification** <gloss>enlivening</gloss>, your living solvent <note>original: *menstruum*; in alchemy, this refers to a solvent capable of dissolving metals, named after the monthly cycles of nature.</note> will die. 

Thus the Magi command to **bring the dead to life, and the living to death**, and yet they call their **Water** "living" at the very threshold. They say that the death of one principle and the life of the other occur in one and the same period. From this it is clear that their Gold is taken as "dead," while the Water is "living." Yet by composing these together, through a brief **boiling** <term>decoction</term> <note>The process of heating a substance in a liquid to extract its essence or facilitate a reaction.</note>, the dead Gold comes to life and the living **Mercury** is killed—that is, the spirit is thickened <gloss>coagulated</gloss> while the body is dissolved. Thus, they rot together in the form of slime, until all the members <margin>of the compound</margin>...

...of the compound are torn apart into atoms. This, then, is the natural process of our **Mastery** <term>Mastery</term> <note>original: *Magisterium*; refers to the complete alchemical process or the "Great Work" of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. The Mystery that we hide with such great effort is how to prepare the **Mercury**, truly spoken of here, which cannot be found upon the Earth ready for our hands—and that for specific reasons known to the *Adepts*. In this *Mercury*, this pure *Gold* is purified to the highest degree of purity; whether filed or rolled thin, we amalgamate it perfectly, and, enclosed in glass, we cook it persistently. The *Gold* is dissolved by the power of our *Water*, and returns to its most immediate matter, in which the life of the *Gold* that was enclosed becomes free, and it takes on the life of the dissolving *Mercury*, which is, in relation to the *Gold*, the same as good *Earth* is in relation to a grain of wheat. In this *Mercury*, therefore, the dissolved *Gold* rots, and so it must necessarily be, by the necessity of *Nature*. Wherefore, after the rot of death, a new *Body* rises again, of the same essence as the former, but of a nobler substance, which takes on degrees of power proportional to the difference between the qualities of the four *Elements*. This is the reasoning of our *Work*; this is our entire *Philosophy*. 

We have said, therefore, that nothing in our *Work* is secret except for the *Mercury* alone, the *Mastery* of which is to prepare it correctly, and to marry it with *Gold* in the proper proportion, and to guide it with fire according to the needs of the *Mercury*. Because *Gold* by itself does not fear fire, the task—the work—is to adjust the management of the heat to what the *Mercury* can endure. He who has not prepared his *Mercury* correctly, even if he joins *Gold* with it, his gold is still the gold of the common people, since it is joined with such a "foolish" agent <note>The author calls the unprepared agent "foolish" or "fatuitous" because it lacks the "intelligence" or chemical activity needed to transform the metal.</note>, in which it remains unchanged by the water, just as if it were sitting in a chest; and by no management of fire will it cast off its bodily nature. 

But our *Mercury* is not like that; therefore our gold is spermatic <note>original: *spermaticum*; in alchemy, this means the substance contains the "seed" or life-force necessary for growth and multiplication, unlike "dead" common metals.</note>, just as *Wheat* that has been sown is "seed," while that same wheat in the barn remains a crop or grain. And even if it were buried in a box beneath the earth, (just as the *West Indians* <note>A common 17th-century reference to the indigenous peoples of the Americas, likely referring to their methods of storing maize in dry pits.</note> are accustomed to hide their grain in pits in the *Earth* protected from watery vapor), yet unless it meets with the moist vapor of the earth, it is "dead"—that is, it remains without fruit, and is surely removed from growth. I know there are many who will criticize this teaching and say: Common *Gold* is the subject...

# An Open Entrance

[The common man] asserts the material of the **Stone** to be running Mercury <note>original: *Mercurium currentem*; this refers to common quicksilver found in shops, which the author considers useless for the Great Work.</note>: we, however, know the contrary. Come now, Philosophers, examine your purses; since you know such things, do you possess the Stone? I, certainly, possess it not by gift (except from my God), nor by theft; I have it, I made it, and I keep it daily under my command. Go on, then, treat your rainwaters, your May-dews, your Salts; prattle about your **sperm** <note>original: *spermate*; a technical term used by false alchemists to describe the "seed" of metals, which the author mocks here.</note>, more powerful than the Demon himself; provoke me with reproaches—do you believe I am affected with sadness by your foul talk? 

I say that **Gold** and **Mercury** alone are our materials, and I know what I write, and God, the searcher of hearts, knows that I write the truth. Nor is there reason to accuse me of envy, since I write with an undaunted pen and an unheard-of style, for the honor of God, the benefit of my neighbor, and out of contempt for the world and its riches. For **Elias the Artist** <term>Elias the Artist</term> <note>A legendary figure in alchemy, first predicted by Paracelsus, who was expected to appear in the "last days" to reveal all the hidden secrets of nature and alchemy.</note> is already born, and glorious things are now being preached concerning the **City of God**. 

I dare to assert that I possess more riches than the whole known world is worth; but I am not permitted to use them because of the snares of scoundrels. I rightly disdain and detest this **idol-madness** <note>original: *idolomania*</note> for Gold and Silver, with which the world celebrates price, pomp, and vanities. Ah, shameful crime! Ah, empty Nothingness! Do you believe I hide these things out of envy? Not at all; for I profess that I grieve from the bottom of my heart that we, as wanderers throughout the whole earth, are driven away as if from the face of the Lord. 

But there is no need for words; what we have seen, touched, and labored upon, what we have, possess, and know, these things we declare, moved only by compassion toward students and out of indignation for Gold, Silver, and precious stones—not insofar as they are God's creatures (far be it! for in that respect we honor them and judge them worthy of honor), but because people, both the Israelites of old and the worldly of today, worship them. Therefore, let it be ground into dust like the **brazen serpent** <note>A biblical reference to the Nehushtan (2 Kings 18:4); an object originally made for healing that was later destroyed because the people began to worship it as an idol.</note>. 

I hope and expect that after a few years, money will be as common as cattle <note>original: *pecus erit pecunia*; the author plays on the Latin etymology where *pecunia* (money) derives from *pecus* (cattle/livestock).</note>, and this pillar of the **Antichristian** beast will collapse into ruins. The people are delirious, the nations are insane; they hold a useless weight in place of God. Will these things accompany our long-awaited and soon-to-emerge **redemption**? When the **New Jerusalem** shall overflow with Gold in its streets, and its gates shall be made of whole and most precious stones, and the **tree of life** in the midst of Paradise shall give its leaves for the healing of the nations? I know, I know, that these my writings will be...

Therefore, I have not consulted with flesh and blood, nor have I sought the consensus of my brothers in writing this. May God grant, for the glory of His name, that I may achieve the end I expect; then at least those Adepts who know me will rejoice that I have published these things.

In dreams we have taught that the Art must be made from Gold and Mercury. It remains, furthermore, for us to describe the use and practice by which you may easily distinguish the goodness or the defects of Mercury, and having recognized them, you may alter and amend it according to your wish. Therefore, having obtained the animated Mercury <term>Animated Mercury</term> <note>original: *Mercurio animato*; mercury that has been "quickened" or prepared through specific alchemical processes to be ready for the Work.</note> and the Gold, there remains the accidental purgation of both the Mercury and the Gold, followed by the marriage, and thirdly, the governance.

## CHAPTER XV.

### *Concerning the accidental purgation of Mercury and Gold.*

**P**erfect Gold is found in the bowels of the Earth, where it is sometimes found in small fragments and sand. If you can obtain this sincere material, it is pure enough; if not, purge it either with Antimony <term>Antimony</term> <note>a semi-metal used in alchemy as a "wolf" to devour impurities in gold, leaving the gold refined.</note>, or through cupellation <note>original: *cineritium*; a refining process where ores are heated in a shallow porous cup (cupel) to separate noble metals from base metals.</note>, or by boiling it with aqua fortis <note>original: *aqua forti*; literally "strong water," referring to nitric acid.</note>, the gold having been first granulated. Afterward, melt it with the fire of fusion, and having filed it, it is ready. Mercury, however, requires an internal and essential purgation, which is the addition of true Sulphur <term>Sulphur</term> <note>In this context, not common brimstone, but a specific alchemical principle used to "fix" the Mercury.</note> step by step, according to the number of eagles <term>Eagles</term> <note>original: *aquilarum*; a technical term representing the number of times the mercury is distilled or purified; usually seven to nine "flights" or "eagles" were required.</note>, then it is purged to its very roots. But in addition, it requires an accidental cleansing to wash away the external filth ejected from the center. This labor is not absolutely necessary,

Though it is a labor, it nonetheless accelerates the work and is therefore suitable. For this reason, take your Mercury, which you have prepared through a suitable number of <term>Eagles</term> <note>original: *aquilarum*; a technical term referring to the repeated cycles of distillation used to "sublime" or purify the Mercury.</note>, and sublime it three times from common salt and the dross of <term>Mars</term> <note>the alchemical name for Iron.</note>, grinding it together with vinegar and a small amount of <term>Sal Ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride, used here as a cleaning agent.</note> until the Mercury disappears. Once dried, distill it through a glass <term>Retort</term> <note>a flask with a long, downward-bending neck used for distilling liquids or subliming solids.</note> with the heat gradually increased until all the Mercury has ascended. Repeat this four times. Afterward, boil the Mercury in spirit of vinegar for an hour in a <term>Cucurbit</term> <note>the lower, gourd-shaped vessel of a still.</note> or a glass with a wide bottom and a narrow neck, shaking it vigorously at times. Then decant the vinegar and wash away the acidity with spring water, poured on repeatedly. Then dry the Mercury, and you will marvel at its brightness. 

You could also wash it with urine or vinegar and salt and skip the sublimation; in that case, distill it at least four times after you have completed all the "eagles" without any further additions. Wash the steel retort each time with ash and water. Finally, boil it in distilled vinegar for half a day, shaking it vigorously at times; pour off the blackening vinegar and add new. Finally, wash it with hot water. You may also free the spirit of vinegar from its blackness by redistilling it, and it will retain its power. All of this is done to remove external filth which does not adhere to the center, yet is somewhat more stubborn upon the surface. You will perceive this impurity thus: if you amalgamate the Mercury with very pure Gold upon a very clean piece of paper, you will see that the <term>Amalgam</term> <note>a mixture of mercury and another metal, in this case, gold.</note> stains the paper with a dark blackness. You shall counteract this dross through the aforementioned distillation, boiling, and agitation; this preparation greatly promotes the work by accelerating it.

Note, indeed, that if the <term>amalgam</term> is allowed to rest, it hardens of its own accord. Therefore, the consistency must be judged while it is being stirred, and if it is then as pliable as <term>butter</term> and allows balls to be formed, and if those balls, placed on clean paper, thicken in rest without trouble so that the bottom is no more liquid than the top, the proportion is good.

This done, take <term>spirit of vinegar</term> <note>concentrated vinegar</note> and dissolve in it a third part of <term>Sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note>, and place the <term>Mercury</term> and <term>Sun</term> <note>the alchemical name for Gold</note> previously amalgamated into this liquid. Place it again in the previous liquid and boil it again in the same glass; grind it again vigorously and wash it. Repeat this until you can wipe away no further color from the <term>amalgam</term> with any labor,

## CHAPTER XVII.

### *On the proportion, shape, material, and sealing of the Vessel.*

**Y**ou shall have a glass, oval or round, large enough to hold at most one ounce of distilled water in its sphere, and certainly no less, if possible; but procure it as close to that measure as you carefully can. Let the glass have a neck the height of one palm <note>a "palm" was a traditional unit of measurement, roughly 3 to 4 inches</note>; let the glass be very clear and thick—the thicker the better, provided you can distinguish the actions within the hollow of the glass. Let it not be thicker in one place than another. Let the material adapted to this glass be half an ounce of Gold with one ounce of Mercury; and if you add triple the Mercury, the whole composition will still be within two ounces. And this proportion is precise. Furthermore, unless the glass is thick, it will not be able to endure in the fire, because the winds that are formed in the vessel by <term>our Embryo</term> <note>original: *Embryone nostro*; an alchemical term for the matter of the Stone while it is "gestating" in the heat of the furnace</note> will burst the vessel. Let the glass be sealed at the top, with caution that there be no crack, let alone a hole, otherwise the work would perish. Thus you will see that the work, in its material beginnings, does not exceed the price of three gold pieces. Indeed, in the manufacture of the water, the cost for one pound hardly exceeds two crowns. The instruments, I admit, are several; however, they are by no means expensive, and if you have my distilling instrument, you will be easily spared from fragile glasses. There are, however, some who dream that perhaps the price of a single imperial coin <note>original: *imperialis*; a high-value coin such as a Reichsthaler</note> will serve for the whole work, to whom it may be answered that they never [will finish] the work...

...to prove by experiment. For other things are necessary in the work which require expenses. Is it indeed to make the Stone? That is indeed the final goal. But the task is to find a humidity <note>original: *humiditatem*; a technical term for the secret solvent or "Mercury of the Sages"</note> in which gold dissolves like ice in warm water; to find this is our Work. On this many labor, that they might gain the Mercury of the Sun <note>gold-derived mercury</note>, others the Mercury of the Moon <note>silver-derived mercury</note>; but in vain. Truly I say, that so much of the material principle of this Water can be bought for the price of one florin as is enough to animate two whole pounds of mercury, so that it becomes the true **Mercury of the Sages**. Meanwhile, glass vessels, coals, earthen vessels, the furnace, and iron vessels and instruments cannot be obtained for nothing. Therefore, let the foul chatterings of the Sophisters <note>false alchemists or charlatans who tricked people with complex, expensive recipes</note> fall silent, who lie impudently and seduce many with their babbling. Without the perfect body, our bronze <note>original: *ære*; here referring to the metallic base</note>, namely Gold, no Tincture can ever be had; and our stone is on one side cheap, immature, and volatile, and on the other perfect, precious, and fixed. Which two species are the body, Gold, and the spirit, namely quicksilver <note>mercury</note>.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

## *On the Furnace, or the Sages' Athanor.*

**C**oncerning Mercury it has been said, and its preparation, proportion, and power; likewise concerning Sulphur, and its necessity and use in our work; how these things are to be prepared, I have advised; how they are to be mixed, I have taught; likewise concerning the vessel in which they are to be sealed, I have revealed much. All of which I warn must be understood with a grain of salt, lest by proceeding too literally, one might happen to err frequently. For we have woven the philosophical subtleties with such unusual clarity <note>original: *candore*; literally "whiteness" or "frankness," implying he is being unusually direct</note> that unless you have scented out the many metaphors in the preceding chapters, you will gather hardly any harvest except expense. For example, where without any ambiguity we called one of the principles Mercury, and the other the Sun; one saleable, the other to be fashioned by art...

# To the Closed Palace of the King

...so that: You should know that our Mercury <term>Mercurius</term> <note>In alchemy, "Mercury" usually refers to a secret solvent or the "animated" spirit of a metal, not merely the quicksilver found in a thermometer.</note> gives gold from itself; for if you did not know that this is the subject of our secrets, you would be forced to sell it as common Gold <term>Sol</term> <note>Latin: *Sol* (the Sun); the universal alchemical symbol for gold.</note>. Indeed, in every trial it is true Gold, and therefore it is "salable"—that is, it can be sold to anyone without any pangs of conscience. Therefore, our Gold is commonly salable, but it is not commonly to be bought, because for it to become *ours*, there is a need for our art. You might be able to find our Gold within common Gold and Silver <term>Luna</term> <note>Latin: *Luna* (the Moon); the alchemical symbol for silver.</note>; I myself have sought it in these and found it. But that task is by no means easy. The Stone itself is to be made with less effort than you will find the Stone’s nearest material by purchasing common gold. For this reason, our gold is the *proximate* <note>The most immediate or "ready" substance.</note> material of our Stone; the gold of the common people is the *near* material; other metals are *remote*; and those things which are not metallic are the *most remote*, or rather, entirely foreign.

Because our Gold is **Chaos**, whose soul has not been chased away by fire. The gold of the common people is that whose soul, in order to be safe from the fiery tyranny of Vulcan <note>The Roman god of fire; here representing the harsh heat of the smelting furnace.</note>, has withdrawn itself into a locked citadel. But if you seek our Gold in any "middle" thing—between the perfect and the imperfect—search and you shall find it; if not, then dissolve the bars of common gold. This is called the "first preparation," by which the enchantment of its body is dissolved, without which it cannot perform the work of the husband <note>The "marriage" of substances is a common metaphor for chemical combination.</note>.

If you enter upon the former path, you are bound to proceed with a most gentle fire; but if the latter, then you must implore the aid of parched Vulcan. You must apply such a fire, for instance, as we provide during "multiplication," when the physical Gold and Silver of the common people are used as a ferment to complete the Elixir. This will indeed be a **Labyrinth**, unless you know how to extricate yourself. Nevertheless, in any progression, you require an equal and continuous heat, whether you have worked with common Gold or with ours. 

Know this regarding both: that our Gold will give you a Work completed two or three months sooner than common Gold, and in its first perfection, the Elixir will have a thousand-fold virtue, whereas in the other work it will scarcely have a hundred-fold. Furthermore, if you complete the Work with our Gold, you must "feed" it, soak it, and ferment it, etc., by which its power will grow immensely; but in the other Work, you must "illuminate" and "wax" <note>original: *incerare*; a process of softening a solid to a wax-like consistency to help it merge with other substances.</note> it, as is taught abundantly in the *Great Rosary* <note>The *Rosarium Philosophorum*, a famous 16th-century alchemical text.</note>. Moreover, if you have worked with our Gold, you can calcine, putrefy, and whiten it, with the help of a gentle internal fire acting alongside a dewy warmth applied from without. If you have worked with common gold, by subliming and boiling...

The materials must be prepared by boiling, so that afterwards you may be able to unite them with the Virgin's Milk <term>Lacte Virginis</term> <note>A symbolic term for the mercurial solvent used to dissolve the philosophical gold.</note>. However much progress you have made, you will be able to accomplish nothing whatsoever without fire. Therefore, not without reason did the truth-telling Hermes <note>Refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of alchemy.</note> establish fire as the governor of the work, second only to the Sun <note>Gold</note> and Moon <note>Silver</note>. I would wish this fire, however, to be understood as coming from our truly secret furnace, which the common eye has never seen.

Yet there is also another furnace, which we call "common," which will be constructed either of brick, or of potter's clay, or of iron and copper plates well-coated with clay. This furnace we call the **Athanor** <term>Athanor</term> <note>A self-feeding furnace designed to maintain a constant temperature for long periods without constant attention.</note>, the shape of which pleases me best is the "Tower with a nest." Therefore, let there be a Tower of about three feet in height and nine fingers (or a common span) wide. After the base or foundational layer, let there be a small door for cleaning out the ashes, of three or four fingers' size, fitted all around with a stone; immediately above this, let a grate be placed. A little above the grate, let there be two holes of about two fingers, through which the heat may be emitted into the attached Athanor. 

Furthermore, let the Tower be exactly sealed from cracks; coals are to be put in from the top—first those that are already lit, then others may be thrown in—and finally let the mouth be exactly blocked. With such a furnace, you can complete the work according to your heart's desire. Moreover, if you are diligent, you may find various ways of administering the required fire. Therefore, let the Athanor be made in such a way that after the matter is placed inside, you can apply any degree of heat you wish without removing the glass vessel, from a fever-heat up to the fire of a lesser reverberation <term>ignis reverberii</term> <note>A high-intensity heat where flames are "reflected" or "reverberated" off the roof of the furnace onto the material.</note>, and in its most intense degree, the heat should last by itself for at least ten or twelve hours. 

Then the Door of the Work lies open to you. But once you have obtained the Stone, you can more usefully fashion a portable furnace, because the Stone, once made, is multiplied in less time and by a gentler fire of Nature.

Our Mercury is our way, and without it, nothing will be done. Our Sun also is not common Gold, and yet it is within it. And if you have worked in our Mercury with common Gold, with the proper regulation, after those one hundred and fifty days you will have our Gold, because our Sun comes from our Mercury. ...[once] common gold <note>original: "vulgi"; refers to gold found in the world as currency or jewelry.</note> has been broken down into its elements by our Mercury and joined together again, the whole mixture, by the benefit of fire, will be **Our Gold**. If this Gold is then boiled again by Mercury, it will certainly produce all the signs described by the Philosophers, using the kind of fire that they themselves have described. 

Now truly, if you apply the "regimen of the stone" <note>the specific sequence of heat and timing</note> to the boiling of common gold, however pure it may be, with our Mercury, you are certainly on the path of error. Therefore, those who write about common Gold <term>Sole vulgi</term>, as we do in this little treatise—and as Artephius, Flamel, Ripley, and many others also do—we are not to be understood in any other way than this: that **Philosophical Gold** is made from common gold and our Mercury. This product, through repeated melting, will then yield **Sulfur** and a fixed, incombustible **Quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum</term> which, upon every trial, has the power to "tinge" <note>to transform base metals into gold or silver.</note>. 

Likewise, by this way of understanding, our Stone is in every metal and mineral, because common gold can be extracted from them, and from that common gold our "nearer" Philosophical Gold can be sought. In all common metals, our Gold is present; but in Gold and Silver, it is contained more closely. 

Therefore, Flamel says: "Some have worked in Jupiter <note>Tin</note>, others in Saturn <note>Lead</note>, but I," he says, "have worked in the Sun <note>Gold</note> and found it." Yet there is one thing in the Metallic Kingdom, of a wondrous origin, in which our Sun is more "nearly" present than in common Gold or the common Moon <note>Silver</note>. If you seek it in the hour of its birth, it melts in our Mercury just like ice in lukewarm water, and yet it is in some way similar to Gold. 

You will not find this immediately in common gold. However, by digesting common gold with our Mercury for one hundred and fifty days, you will find this same true matter, which is **Our Gold**. This is the "longer way," and it is not yet as powerful as that substance which Nature has left ready at hand. And yet, by "turning the wheel" <note>repeating the alchemical cycle of dissolution and coagulation</note> a third time, you will find the same thing in both. The only difference is the time: in the former [the shorter way], it takes seven months; in the latter [the longer way], a space of a year and a half. 

I am skilled in both ways, and I praise the easier way; however, I have described the more difficult one, lest I draw the curse <term>anathema</term> of all the Sages <term>Sophorum</term> <note>The "Wise Ones" or experienced alchemists who swore to keep the "short way" secret.</note> upon my head. In reading the books of more sincere men, one finds that they all vary in their instructions for the regimen. And while they speak of one *Work*, they teach the regimen of another, a snare in which I remained entangled for a long time before I could free my feet from the trap. I therefore declare that the heat in our *Work* is most gentle to nature, provided you understand our work correctly. But if you work with the **Common Sun** <note>Common gold used as a starting material.</note>, that work is not strictly our work; yet, it will lead directly to our work at its determined time. In that path, you truly require a strong decoction <note>A long-term boiling or heating process.</note> and a proportionate fire; afterward, however, you will proceed with a most gentle fire in our tower-like **Athanor** <term>Athanore</term> <note>A self-feeding alchemical furnace designed to maintain a constant, steady heat over many days.</note>, which I must praise most highly. 

Therefore, if you have worked with the *Common Sun*, take care to carefully arrange the marriages of **Venus** <note>In alchemy, Venus represents copper, but here it likely refers to a specific metallic quality or "green" acidity needed to dissolve the gold.</note>; then place them in their bed, and with the proper fire, you will see the **Emblem of the Great Work**—namely the black, the **peacock's tail** <note>A stage in the process where many colors appear on the surface of the matter, like the feathers of a peacock.</note>, the white, the yellow, and the red. Then repeat this *Work* with **Mercury**, which is called the **Virgin’s milk** <term>lac Virginis</term> <note>A name for the purified mercurial solvent that nourishes the "Stone."</note>, by applying the fire of the **Dew-bath** <term>Balnei roris</term> <note>A gentle heating method, similar to a modern double-boiler or steam bath.</note>, and at most a heat of sand tempered with ashes. You will then see not only black, but a "black blacker than black" and every kind of blackness; likewise, the complete white and red. This occurs by the will of God in a "gentle breeze," like the one that called Elijah with a still, small voice. 

Therefore, if you know the art, extract **Our Sun** from **Our Mercury**; then from one single thing you will perfect the *Work*, which, believe me, is more perfect than all worldly perfection, according to the **Philosopher** <note>Likely referring to Aristotle or Hermes Trismegistus.</note>: "If," he says, "you can perfect the work from *Mercury* alone, you will surely be the seeker of a most precious work." In this *Work*, there are no superfluities <note>Waste or unnecessary byproducts.</note>; instead, by the living GOD, the whole is converted into purity, because the action takes place in one thing alone. But if you begin the process in the *Work of the Common Sun*, the action and the "passion" <note>The reaction or "suffering" of the matter being changed.</note> then occur in two things, from both of which only the middle substance is taken, and the dregs are rejected. 

If you meditate deeply on these things which I have explained briefly, you hold the key to unlocking all the apparent contradictions among the **Philosophers**. This is why **Ripley** <note>George Ripley (c. 1415–1490), a famous English alchemist and author of *The Compound of Alchemy*.</note> teaches to turn the wheel a third time in the chapter on **Calcination**, where he speaks expressly of the *Common Sun*, and he must be understood in this way. In the doctrine of his proportions he is very obscure, because those three proportions serve three [different] works. One work is most secret, pure, and natural, and takes place in **Our Mercury** with **Our Sun**, to which work [it must be] ascribed...

...[to be] observed <note>The text begins mid-word, likely "observanda," meaning "must be observed."</note> are all the signs described by the Sages <term>Sophis</term> <note>original: "Sophis"; the wise masters or historical adepts of alchemy.</note>. For I swear in good faith that I have revealed the truth. If you work with the Mercury I have described and the purest common Gold with the proper fire, you will find our **Sun** <note>Philosophical Gold.</note> within seven or nine months at the most, and our **Moon** <note>Philosophical Silver.</note> within five months. And these are the true timeframes <note>original: "Termini"</note> for completing these Sulfurs; if you then believe them to be our Stones, you are still mistaken. But from these, through repeated labor and at least a sensible fire, you will have the true **Elixir**, and all this within a year and a half, **GOD WILLING** <note>original: "DEO DANTe"</note>, to whom be glory forever.

## CHAPTER XXI.

### Concerning the Burning of the Flowers and the Caution thereof.

It is no small error, and yet easily committed: the <term>burning of the flowers</term> <note>original: "florum combustio"; refers to the overheating of the delicate chemical vapors or precipitates before they have matured</note> before the tender natures are well extracted from their depth. This error must be especially avoided after the third week. For in the beginning, the abundance of moisture is so great that if you direct the work with a fire stronger than is fitting, the fragile vessel will not bear the abundance of vapors and will immediately burst—unless perhaps your vessel is too large. And in that case, the moisture will be scattered so far that it will no longer return to its body, at least not enough to revive it. But when the Earth begins to retain part of its water, then indeed, as the vapors fail, the fire can be intensified beyond measure without any harm to the vessel; but the work will be ruined thereby, and it will give the color of the <term>wild poppy</term> <note>original: "papaveris sylvestris"; a reddish color indicating the matter has been scorched or "burnt" by excessive heat rather than ripening naturally</note>, and the whole compound will finally become a dry powder, uselessly reddened. You shall judge by this sign that the fire was stronger than just—namely, so strong that it was an enemy to the true union. For you should know that <term>our Work</term> <note>The Great Work (Magnum Opus) of alchemical transformation</note> requires a true transformation of natures, which cannot

...[this] cannot happen, unless the final union of both natures takes place; but they cannot be united, unless in the form of water. For there is no union of bodies, but only a crushing; much less can there be a union of a body with a spirit <term>at the level of the smallest parts</term> <note>original: "per minima"; a technical term in natural philosophy referring to a union where every tiny particle of one substance is joined to a particle of another</note>, but spirits can very well be united among themselves. Therefore, a homogeneous metallic water is required, for which the way is prepared through a prior <term>calcination</term> <note>The process of heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to a powder or "ash," used here to prepare the metal for dissolution</note>. 

This drying, therefore, is not truly a drying, but a reduction of water with the earth through the sieve of nature into atoms finer than the requirement of the water allows, so that the earth may receive the transmutative ferment of the water. But if the heat is more vehement than is proper, this spiritual nature, struck as if by the hammer of death, turns from active to passive, and from spiritual to corporeal—namely, a useless <term>red precipitate</term> <note>A chemical solid that forms out of a solution; here, the author warns that if the heat is too high, the matter "burns" into a useless solid prematurely</note>, because by its undue heat, the color becomes that of a raven’s blackness; although this is dark, it is a highly desirable color <note>The author suggests that while blackness is usually the goal, a premature "burnt" blackness caused by too much heat is a failure</note>. 

Nevertheless, redness is conspicuous and remarkable at the beginning of the true Work; yet when this concurs with a proper abundance of moisture, it shows that <term>heaven has lain with earth</term> <note>A symbolic description of the union of spiritual/volatile principles (the "heaven") and material/fixed principles (the "earth")</note> and has conceived the fire of nature; therefore, the whole hollow of the glass will be tinged with a golden color. But this color will not last; rather, it will shortly give birth to green, and then expect black within a short time; and if you are patient, you will see your wish fulfilled. At least <term>make haste slowly</term> <note>original: "festina lente"; a classical adage advising a balance between speed and caution</note>, and yet continue a sufficiently strong fire, and steer your ship between <term>Scylla and Charybdis</term> <note>A metaphor for navigating between two dangerous extremes—here, too much or too little heat—referenced from the hazards in Homer’s Odyssey</note> like a skilled pilot, if you desire to gain the riches of both the Indies <note>A 17th-century idiom meaning immense wealth, referring to the East and West Indies</note>. 

At times you will see tiny islands, as it were, and multicolored spirals and umbrellas emerging in the waves and at the sides, which will shortly dissolve while others arise. For the earth, eager for germinating, is always fashioning something; sometimes you will imagine you see birds or beasts and reptiles in the glass, and the colors are of slight importance to the sight. The whole secret is that you continually maintain the proper fire, and all these things will finish in a jet-black color, a discontinuous powder, before fifty days have passed.
