# CHAPTER VI.

## On the mode and means of extracting this Seed.

**T**he most beautiful things are always the most difficult, as the experience of all ages can be a rich witness. Therefore, it is no wonder if such great difficulty is found in a subject so noble above others. For I have not easily known any work in the nature of things beset with more difficulties [than this is]. Therefore, if anyone has entered this path, and yet spares his soul from study and labor, it is necessary that he turn back, for he has strayed at this very threshold. For the terrible evils that will appear in the work will be the greatest cause of despondency. 

But if the **Father of Lights** <note>original: *Pater Luminum*. A reference to God as the source of all knowledge and revelation, common in hermetic texts.</note> should grant the key of the art to anyone, nothing more remains for him than **women's work** and **child's play** <note>original: *opus mulierum, ludusque puerorum*. A famous alchemical aphorism meaning that once the secret 'Key' is found, the process requires only patience and gentle heat rather than strenuous labor.</note>; namely, that he may delight his eyes with the most beautiful signs appearing during the labor, until he is ready to reap the harvest. 

Let him possess the most precious treasure of the whole world; without this, truly, error and expense, care and anxiety, will be the fruits of this frustrated **Philosophy**. Therefore, every wise man, before he enters the path, will first and most greatly be anxious to know it [along with its signs], so that if by chance any difficulties might appear in it, being armed against them, he may not be forced to return with sorrow and grief after the journey has begun. Therefore, let all **Sons of the Art** <note>A traditional term for alchemists who considered themselves part of a spiritual and intellectual lineage.</note> know that to attain our secret, it is necessary to manifest the most hidden **seed of Gold**, which is not done except by the full and total **volatilization** <term>volatilization<gloss>The process of turning a solid substance into a vapor or spirit, often seen as 'spiritualizing' the matter.</gloss></term> of the fixed, and therefore of that form...

corruption. Moreover, to destroy gold in this way is the most secret work of the entire world. For this divine science is not completed in the corrosive defilement <note>The author warns against using harsh, "vulgar" acids (like aqua regia) which he believes ruin the metal's internal spirit rather than refining it.</note> of the metal; rather, all such corrosions are false and erroneous. Our work requires not just any dissolution, but a **Philosophical** one—that is, a reduction into Mercurial water. This is achieved through a prior calcination <term>calcination<gloss>In alchemy, the process of heating a substance to reduce it to a powder or "ash," symbolizing the death of the old form.</gloss></term> performed by the **Agent Mercury** <term>☿<gloss>The symbol for Mercury, representing the "Philosophical Mercury" or the transformative solvent used by alchemists.</gloss></term>. This is produced through a subtle rotation and conversion of the Elements. 

This calcination is the mortification <note>original: *mortificatio*. An alchemical stage where the substance is "killed" or broken down into its base components so it can be reborn.</note> of the homogeneous moisture with the dry [part] of its own nature, so that afterward, through that same dry moisture, it may be revivified. This happens to such an extent that the most "digested" virtue, extracted from the substance to be dissolved by the solvent, becomes the very cause of this calcination and dissolution. 

What does this have in common with the corrosive crushing of bodies [by means of mineral waters/acids]? Indeed, these operations are rather opposed by a **diametric opposition**. If anyone observes this correctly, he will very easily perceive the difficulty of the work. Consider Gold: it is the most solid of all bodies, the most fixed, and of the strongest composition. It is the most patient of fire and least liable to corruption; it does not easily pass into a nature so contrary to its own. Therefore, if anyone attempts this by force, he will profit nothing. 

Thus, an **Agent** of prepotent virtue is required for this to happen. This agent must be homogeneous, friendly, and spiritual, so that it is akin to the body, yet able to overcome it and penetrate to its very roots, through its innermost parts. Since the recesses of Gold are so widely extended, and yet the smallest bit of Gold remains true Gold, it follows that the agent must be no ordinary one. Furthermore, Gold will not easily lay aside its form; rather, it will fight until, utterly conquered, it succumbs and dies. It follows that our Agent must also possess the power of revivifying, so that from the dead corpses it can raise up a new, pure body.

## CHAPTER VII.

**I**t remains for us to seek such an Agent with which we may accomplish all the aforementioned things. In this Agent, it is required first that it be a <term>homogeneous water</term> <note>original: *aqua homogenea*; a substance that is uniform in nature and shares a common origin with the metal being treated.</note>, and this by the law of necessity. For I have taught above that the <term>Golden seed</term> <note>original: *semen Aureum*; the essential life-spark within gold that allows it to grow or be transformed.</note> lies hidden, and obtains its powers, in water alone. But it is shut up within the body of <term>Gold</term>, under the thickest coverings, which are clearly the opposite of that hidden thing we seek. Therefore, this water remains to be drawn out by a subtle artifice, as it does not enter of its own accord; hence, this must be accomplished through something else, which must indeed be of the same nature as that which we seek to draw out. For every like generates its like—that is, every agent exercising a generative action upon something transforms that which it acts upon into its own nature (as nearly as possible). Next, it is necessary that this water be kindred to the body to be dissolved, and accordingly pure, clean, and most exquisitely cleansed and purged of all filth.

But even this is not enough; rather, it is required to be the opposite of <term>Gold</term> in all those qualities in which it differs from the water (in which the seed lies hidden) that we seek. The former [gold] is supremely fixed, while this is supremely volatile; the former is a most solid body, while this is a most penetrating spirit. The one is coarse, the other subtle; the one dead, the other alive and life-giving—in a word, all other conditions are required in this [agent] which we seek in the gold after its dissolution, but which are lacking in its coagulated, dead body. 

It is concluded, therefore, that <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> alone is the true <term>key of the Alchemical art</term>, which is in truth that <term>dry water</term> so often described by the Philosophers: flowing, slipping, and yet not wetting the hand of the one touching it, nor anything else that is not of the unity of its own matter; and not this alone, but it is further endowed with the virtues described above. This is our gate-keeping guardian, <term>our balsam</term>, **oil**, **honey**, <term>our urine</term>, **May dew**, **female**, **mother**, **egg**, **secret furnace**, **Oven**, **Sieve**, **Marble**, **true fire**, **venomous Dragon**, <term>our theriac</term> <note>original: *Theriaca*; a reference to a universal medicinal antidote, here used to describe the transformative power of Mercury.</note>, **burning wine**, <term>Green Lion</term>, <term>Bird of Hermes</term>, <term>Goose of Hermogenes</term>, <term>this two-edged sword in the hand of the Cherub</term> <note>A biblical allusion to the sword guarding Eden; here it represents the power that guards the secrets of nature.</note>, which guards the way to the <term>tree of life</term>; it is distinguished by infinite other names. It is <term>our vessel</term>, the true and hidden one, as well as the **Philosophical garden** in which <term>our Sun</term> <note>Gold</note> will rise and stand up. It is the royal and triumphant mineral

## On the Transformation of Metals

<term>Vegetable Saturnia</term> <note>original: *Saturnia vegetabilis*; a symbolic name for a specific alchemical substance, likely a derivative of lead or a particular solvent</note>, and likewise the <term>Caduceus of Mercury</term> <note>original: *Mercurii caduceus*; the staff of Hermes, symbolizing the power to unite opposites and the transformative nature of the solvent</note>, perform wonders through her, and she transforms herself according to her own pleasure, assuming various masks. Regarding this Water, the *Philosopher* says: "Let the *Alchemists* boast however they wish," he says, "but without this, the *transmutation of metals* is impossible." What shall I say? What shall I discuss, that I might proclaim her praises? She is not the same in her own nature as we make her through our Artifice; thus, she is a lowly thing, and yet the most precious treasure of the entire world. O perfection of Nature! O the <term>pinnacle</term> <note>original: *colophon*; a finishing touch or crowning achievement</note> of metallic works! Therefore, Son of Learning, attend diligently to the art, so that you may achieve your desire. Take that which is most filthy in itself—that is, <term>our prostitute woman</term> <note>original: *mulier nostra meretrix*; a common alchemical metaphor for raw, unrefined matter or "crude" substance that readily reacts with others</note>—purge away all filth entirely, and extract from there that which is most pure, which is our <term>menstruum</term> <note>original: *menstruum*; a solvent used to extract the essence of a substance</note>, a royal Diadem. Behold, I have completed in few words what ennobles the Philosopher, frees him from errors, and leads him directly to the most beautiful field of delights.

Therefore, to conclude this chapter, I shall briefly and succinctly repeat everything that has been said before. There is a certain noble science, true and certain, called *Alchemy*, by which any imperfect metals are perfected into *Gold or Silver* by the projection of the triumphant, penetrating, and tinting <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: *Arcanum*; a secret, potent substance or "inner mystery" of a material</note> upon them. This secret is nothing other than *Gold* exalted to the highest degree of its perfection, and this is achieved through the wise Art administering to Nature. For indeed, all imperfect metals are of the same material composition as Gold, and they differ only by bare accidents, as well as by the modes and degrees of incomplete <term>decoction</term> <note>original: *decoctionis*; the process of "cooking" or maturing metals within the earth through natural heat</note>. Whatever is imperfect and mixed with them is clearly heterogeneous; and although it may cling to the pure part externally, it is not inwardly united, and therefore can be rejected by a prevailing Agent, such as <term>our complete Elixir</term>. 

To obtain this Arcanum, one must draw out the seed [which lies hidden in the body of Gold], which is enclosed under the deepest valleys and yields to no strength, but is manifested only by wise art. When this seed appears [having previously been hidden], it comes forth under a <term>Mercurial form</term>, from which it is exalted into the <term>fifth essence</term> <note>original: *essentiam quintam*; the Quintessence, or the purest, most concentrated medicinal and transformative power of a substance</note>—first white, then red—through the continuous heat of the fire. And all of this is accomplished through a homogeneous Agent: the <term>Pontic Mercurial</term> <note>original: *Mercuriale Ponticum*; a "sharp" or "sea-like" mercury often described as the "universal solvent" in alchemical texts</note>, which is pure, clean, and crystalline.

### On the Metamorphosis of Metals

...honey <note>original: *mel*; here likely used as a metaphor for the crude or "sweet" starting material</note> has shed its own form, it may put on its true Philosophical form. It would be tedious to review labors of this sort; therefore, since truth is the indicator of itself and of the false—and the right is likewise the indicator of itself and the crooked—I shall pass on to the matter itself. I have taught above that all metals share the same material principle, namely **mercury** <term>☿</term> <note>the symbol for Mercury, often representing the "mother" or "soul" of metals in alchemy</note>. It follows, therefore, that **mercury** is truly a metallic thing, and consequently [even if it is common mercury] it nevertheless originally possesses a matter that is homogeneous with all metals. 

If, therefore, Philosophical Mercury is to be a homogeneous metallic water, it follows that materially and fundamentally it is not distinguished from other mercury, except insofar as one is purer and hotter than the other, and yet both are a "dry mineral water." Let the **sons of doctrine** <note>a traditional term for students of alchemy or those initiated into the art’s secrets</note> know, therefore, that the matter of common mercury can and must enter into the matter of Philosophical Mercury, although not all of the substance seen in that common form remains. 

For let ingenious **chemists** <term>Chemicolæ</term> know for certain that no other Mercury is given from which all metals are made than the common one [at least in respect to its origin]. This mercury, generated within the veins of the earth, was destined to produce metal as long as it remained safe from raw air in a place fit and suited for generation; it retained its own motion and internal stirring so that it might be excited toward perfect generation. 

But if, by some accident, the suitability of the location is violated or corrupted, this matter—as if struck by the **Hammer of Death** <note>original: *Mortis Malleo*; a striking metaphor for the moment the "living" mineral process is halted, making the metal "dead" or stagnant</note>—immediately loses all motion entirely. It is no longer able to be moved further forward, just as an egg [over which a hen has sat for some time] is rendered thereafter unfit to produce an offspring once it has cooled. The life—that is, the internal altering heat—has vanished because the external heat failed. Thus, what previously tended toward perfection every day is now hindered by chance and becomes an "abortion," with no hope left for future spontaneous motion. 

This is the reason why, when some have tried to digest **mercury** <term>☿</term> above the ground with artificially devised heat, they have brought back only a mockery as the reward of their labor. Therefore, the "form" is taken away, or rather hindered in its arrival. This form [as was said above] is a particle of ineffable light that is ready at hand, illuminating its lodging, provided all things have been aptly disposed from the outside; thus, it leaves its impression upon things. This impression, once received by the matter, produces a **ferment**, which is the true author of all transmutation.

### CHAPTER VIII.

...through its fermentative odor, altering the very things in which it resides, exciting them toward a motion that is both corruptive and generative. However, when the external accidents required for these processes are lacking, all these things collapse of their own accord, and this ruin is not easily repaired by any art. Therefore, there remains to us a crude, metallic, undigested, and cold matter, not purified by decoction <note>the process of heating a substance in a liquid to extract its essence or purify it</note>, which [with respect to minerals] emulates the nature of spring water [with respect to plants and animals]. This is the ***True Matter*** <note>original: *Materia vera*</note>, which lacks the form of the ***Philosophical Mercury*** <note>original: *Mercurii Philosophici*</note>, for which it is bound to exchange its own form so that what we seek may be produced from it.

The superfluity is twofold: an earthly leprosy and a watery dropsy <note>In alchemical terms, "leprosy" refers to the dull, crusty impurities that "infect" metals, while "dropsy" refers to an excess of unstable, phlegmatic moisture.</note>. Therefore, add and supply to the **Mercury** what is missing—namely, a fiery power for burning—and all the dregs will fall away from the **Mercury** of their own accord, which you shall then carefully separate. 

If you achieve this, you have perfected the work of a most insightful and skilled ***Philosopher*** <note>meaning a true master of alchemy</note>. ***Jupiter*** <term>♃</term> <note>Representing the stage of the work where the matter turns white and pure.</note> has then obtained the Empire; having dispelled the most foul clouds of ***Saturn*** <term>♄</term> <note>Representing the dark, leaden, and "corrupt" initial state of the matter.</note>, he has caused a clear and sparkling fountain to emerge for you. You will marvel at the uncommon brilliance of this water. Its virtues are uncommon—which it receives not from its matter, but from its form—and they are to be found in no other thing in the whole world. For instance, it naturally dissolves ***Gold*** <note>original: *Aurum*</note> with a true Philosophical solution, not as the laboring **Sophists** <note>A term of contempt used by true Adepts for amateur alchemists who used "corrosive waters" or acids that destroyed the "soul" of the metal.</note> dissolve it through defiling corrosive waters, attempting to alienate it from its metallic matter as much as they can. This ***Mercury*** naturally produces from itself the ***Secret*** <term>Arcanum</term> of ***Gold*** and ***Silver*** <note>original: *Argentum*</note>, and likewise the ***Potable Gold*** <note>original: *Auri potabilis*; a legendary medicinal elixir of liquid gold believed to grant longevity.</note>; I write this with knowledge, and the **Adepts** <note>those who have successfully completed the Great Work</note> likewise know and testify to it.

I shall therefore conclude this little treatise, because whatever remains to be said is candidly handed down by me in a specific treatise written elsewhere. In the meantime, farewell, enjoy these things, and expect a blessing from God.

# A BRIEF INTRODUCTION
#### TO THE
## CELESTIAL RUBY.
### *Concerning the Philosopher's Stone and its Secret.*

The **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: *Lapis Philosophorum*</note> is a certain Celestial, Spiritual, penetrating, and fixed Substance, perfecting all **Metals** into true **Gold** and **Silver** [according to the quality of the Medicine] and capable of passing every test; and this is done through the imitation of Nature and its operations, as closely as possible.

The **Art of Chemistry** <note>original: *Ars Chemia*; in this context, it refers to the "Great Art" of alchemy</note> is concerned with this substance, treating and teaching the manner and path of perfecting it. However, this is not achieved through diverse things, but through one single thing alone, to which nothing is to be added and nothing taken away, but from which only the superfluous must be removed.

As for the validity <note>original: *jus*, literally "right" or "law"</note> of this art, experience would be the most effective way to convince men in this matter: if it were proven that true **Gold** could be made by this art, then there would be no doubt whatsoever regarding either the validity or the utility of the Art. It is evident that imperfect metals are transmutable <note>capable of being changed from one form or substance into another</note> in this way because all were destined for perfection as one; however, some remained imperfect due to a defect in digestion <note>In alchemical thought, metals "grow" in the earth like plants; "digestion" refers to the natural heat of the earth that matures base metals into gold over centuries.</note>. Therefore, if they could be properly cooked <note>original: *coqui*; refers to alchemical decoction or the application of laboratory heat</note>, they too would be perfected, since there is no impediment in the matter itself to prevent this. Indeed, all metals originate from a single source, namely a crude, cold, and moist **Mercury** <note>represented by the symbol ☿; here referring to the "First Matter" or root principle of metals rather than common quicksilver</note>, in which there was originally no differen- <margin>tientia</margin> <note>differentiation or distinction</note> between the **Sun** <note>the alchemical symbol for Gold</note> and **Saturn** <note>the alchemical symbol for Lead</note>...

<summary>This page introduces the "Celestial Ruby" or Philosopher's Stone, defining it as a spiritual substance that perfects base metals into gold. The author argues that transmutation is possible because all metals share a common "mercurial" origin and only differ due to incomplete natural heating.</summary>

...ence. Nevertheless, what Nature has subsequently worked in this matter—namely, by cooking <note>original: *decoquendo*; the alchemical process of heating a substance to mature or "ripen" it</note> it more or less—has alone created this diversity. Therefore, all other Metals can be perfected into the Sun <note>original: *Solem*; the alchemical name for Gold</note> by the work of our divine and most perfect Mastery <note>original: *Magisterii*; refers to the completed alchemical process or the Stone itself</note>, which, when cast upon imperfect Metals, is able to perfect them by cooking them to such a degree, insofar as the Mastery itself possesses more than the required perfection [which is needed in Gold].

Here, therefore, one may observe how great the power is, and of how Spiritual a Nature this our Divine Stone is, which by mere projection <note>The act of "throwing" a small amount of the Stone onto a larger mass of molten base metal to transform it</note> can accomplish above the ground in one hour what Nature, through her subterranean operations, would by no means have perfected. How much Nature can do when aided by Art will thus be clear to see. 

For as long as our Stone was perfected by Nature without the aid of art, its power <note>original: *virtutis*; often translated as "virtue" or "potency"</note> was only singular; but the power acquired through art, with Nature cooperating and managing, is tenfold <note>original: *denaria*</note> for each treatment—that is, in a certain way, infinite, since it cannot be calculated. For first, by dissolving it, and again by coagulating and cooking it, one part of the Medicine <note>term for the Stone in its healing/transformative capacity</note> falls upon 1,000 parts of imperfect Metal, penetrating and perfectly tinting <note>original: *tingens*; the alchemical transformation of the "color" or inner essence of a metal</note> it. 

Truly, if you attempt to advance this medicine further by repeated dissolution and coagulation, behold, it is now extended to infinity: for your intellect will fail you for calculating sooner than the power of the Elixir will fail for penetrating and tinting. It is not that a tiny amount of such a multiplied Elixir touches the whole mass immediately with its physical touch, but rather it permeates the whole by its power and influence; for even the smallest particle of the imperfect body is touched and tinted immediately by the medicine. 

Yet the matter stands thus: every tinted part is to the adjacent part like a ferment <note>original: *fermenti*; similar to how yeast or a "starter" transforms a whole batch of dough</note>; therefore, the Elixir tints that which it touches most closely with a tint slightly weaker than it was itself endowed and imbued with, and this in turn ferments that which is closest to it by communicating the tint; and this continues until the entire mass is finally brought to the perfection of true Gold. This happens in a short space of time due to the spirituality of our agent; which, since it is a true Metallic Fire, no different from elemental fire, imperceptibly penetrates and heats any of the hardest bodies, even those...

### A Brief Introduction ###
<note>original: *Brevis Manuductio*</note>

...I mean not only those who are common or illiterate and unlearned, but even some—indeed, very many—men who are otherwise most learned, and perhaps even pious. It is thought to be dry, and yet it is oily, flowing easily upon a metal plate and tinting it. Wherefore it is rightly called the "Father of all wonders." ## Regarding the Celestial Ruby.

->Regarding the Celestial Ruby.<-

It has a certain name specific to itself, and yet there is nothing in the whole world whose name it cannot take on under some consideration. For its nature is so wonderful that if we say it is Spiritual, it is true; but if we call it corporal, we speak correctly. For it is **Gold**, and not that of the common people <note>original: *non vulgi*; referring to alchemical gold versus physical bullion</note>, but spiritual gold—that is, it is made subtle, penetrative, and noble. Therefore it is the spirit or the **fifth essence** <term>quinta essentia</term> <note>Also known as the quintessence, the purest element that transcends the four physical elements of earth, air, fire, and water.</note>, the most noble of all Creatures after the rational soul, reducing all diseases and all imperfections, both in Animals and in Metals [according to the quality of the medicine], to a most exact and perfect balance. And this is truly our **Microcosm** <term>Microcosmus</term> <note>Literally "little world"; the idea that the Stone contains the entire universe in miniature.</note>, which we value so highly. Having this stone, whether as a powder or a fifth essence, neither riches nor health will be lacking, God granting, to whom be glory forever.

But to come to the final part of the task I have undertaken—namely, to show by what means this stone of ours may be obtained—for it is not to be sought as something manufactured by Nature, but is to be composed by the art and ingenuity of the craftsman, with Nature nevertheless assisting and providing the labor. For as has been declared quite abundantly, the matter of this stone is to be sought from nowhere else but metals; nevertheless, these metals are not our stone, which is very easy to understand, for they have another form different from our stone. Yet, I do not deny that our **medicine** <gloss>remedy or tincture</gloss> is to be drawn from them; however, so that it may be drawn out, the prior form of the metal must necessarily be removed. This must be done while preserving the species, although through the destruction of that particular and individual metal. Now, the metallic species lives and is preserved in the spirit, which spirit resides in nothing else but a water of its own kind that is homogeneous <note>original: *homogenea*; meaning a substance of the same nature or origin</note>. For water is the dwelling place of the spirit, which must be retained above all in the preservation of the species. Therefore, **Gold** must be changed from its form, and that into a water of its own kind, in which water the spirit of Gold is preserved. This spirit afterwards re-thickens its own Water and brings in—after **putrefaction** <term>putrefactionem</term> <note>The stage of alchemical decay, often called the "Black Crow," necessary for the birth of the new form.</note>—a new form, a thousand times more perfect than the form of Gold [which it lost by **returning it to a raw state** <note>original: *reincrudando*; the process of reducing a processed metal back into its primary, "crude" matter</note>].

Metallic bodies must therefore be reduced into a homogeneous water that does not wet the hands <note>A classic alchemical description of "Philosophical Mercury," which behaves like water but does not dampen surfaces.</note>; so that from this water a new species...

# Brief Introduction

...of metal may result, far nobler than any metal. This is our most precious medicine and the **Celestial Ruby**.

Now, this entire work corresponds perfectly to that natural operation occurring underground, which is why the work is rightly called "natural." For Nature, from Mercury <term>☿</term> alone, which is cold and moist, produces metals according to their species by constant digesting and cooking within the veins of the earth. Art <note>In this context, "Art" refers to the skill and technology of Alchemy.</note>, however, to shorten the work, has discovered a far more subtle operation, yet similar to the natural one: for it joins mature Gold to crude, cold, and moist Mercury so that the gold may be dissolved. From both of these, through mixing and a secret joining, it produces a single Mercury, which they call the **water of life** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*; here referring to a potent solvent or "mercurial water" rather than brandy.</note>. This Mercury they finally boil down into Gold—not the common kind <note>original: *non vulgi*</note>, but something far nobler, which falls upon any imperfect metals and tints them into proven Gold that can withstand every test.

You understand therefore, I believe, that although our stone is made from Gold alone, it is nonetheless not the gold of the common people. So, in order that our Gold may be drawn out from common Gold, it must be dissolved into a water—not an elementary water <note>Common water found in nature.</note>, but one that "does not wet the hands," which is to say, a mineral water. This water is the **Mercury**, which, drawn from the **red servant** <note>original: *servo rubeo*; a common alchemical code name for matter that has reached a certain stage of heat or maturity.</note>, contains within itself everything to complete the work without any further human intervention. And this is finally that unique, true, and Natural principle, to which nothing must be added, and from which nothing must be removed or diminished, except for certain superfluities; the substance itself will complete the task by its own power and natural instinct without any human assistance. Therefore, once you have this Mercury, care for nothing else.

Not without reason, therefore, did the Philosopher <note>Commonly referring to Aristotle or a high-ranking alchemical authority like Hermes Trismegistus.</note> say: *Let your whole study be directed toward boiling down the Mercury;* but I say to you: *Let your whole study be directed toward preparing this Mercury—that is, in whitening our red **Laton** <term>Latone</term> <note>Laton refers to the impure "body" of the metal or the dross that must be purified during the "whitening" stage of the Great Work.</note>.* Once that is done, you have done your part; what remains is nothing but **women's work and children's play** <note>A famous alchemical phrase meaning that once the initial difficult stages are over, the process continues easily on its own with gentle heat.</note>: for Nature will be ready at hand to manage the rest. Meanwhile, the most desired rest is granted to you, as the Philosopher said, which is indeed more desirable than any labor.

For know that this work of our whitening [<gloss>namely, the radical whitening</gloss>] is no light task; for this will certainly be of the altered and reduced body...

...evidence, nor will Gold so whitened ever return to its former shape: for a spirit has been made from a body, and a volatile thing has been made from a fixed thing by this operation. Therefore, you should focus all your strength on the **whitening of the Laton** <note>original: *Latone*; in alchemy, "Laton" refers to the base metal or "black" stage of the matter that must be purified and whitened during the Great Work.</note>. For it is easier to make Gold than to destroy it in this way: for he who dissolves in this manner actually congeals; indeed, the **dissolution of the body** and the **congealing of the spirit** happen at the same time.

Consider truly, little sons of wisdom, and mark these mysteries: whatever dissolves is spirit, but whatever coagulates is body. If you wish therefore your bodies to be dissolved, you have need first of all of a spiritual substance, because a body does not enter a body to dissolve it; rather, spirit enters it, thins it, and makes it porous. And since you seek a water, you therefore need a water to make this manifest: for every agent performing some act upon something assimilates that upon which it acts to itself [as much as possible], and every natural effect is shaped to the nature of its cause; therefore, to draw water out of the earth, water will be needed.

I do not [as some wrongly think] understand "water" here to mean ***aqua fortis*** <note>Nitric acid; literally "strong water."</note>, ***aqua regia*** <note>A mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids; literally "royal water," named for its ability to dissolve gold.</note>, or other corrosives, which the common sort of alchemists <note>original: *Alchemistarum vulgus*</note> artificially compose for themselves. They place metallic species into these to be dissolved, yet they do not dissolve them, but rather corrode, defile, and corrupt them. For who would believe that those waters could destroy the old form of a metal while preserving its metallic nature, when they themselves are utterly alien to the nature of metals? Indeed, they are not effective enough to destroy the species <note>The essential "form" or identity of the metal.</note> entirely—otherwise, they would convert them into their own nature; instead, as much as they are able, they transform them into something filthy: for the more bodies are corroded, the more they are alienated from their metallic species. 

But our water is the **water of Mercury**, and it dissolves bodies into Mercury <term>☿</term> <note>The symbol for Mercury or Quicksilver.</note>, and it is inseparably joined with them when they are dissolved, dwelling with them and being cooked together, so that from them may be made that one spiritual whole which is sought. For everything that naturally dissolves something, so that in this way the species of the dissolved thing is preserved, remains with the dissolved thing both materially and formally; it grows together with it and is thickened by it, and nourishes it, as can be seen in gra- <note>The text cuts off mid-word, likely "grain" (*granis*).</note>

### Brevis Manuductio
->A Brief Guidance<-

...of wheat; since this is dissolved by a moist earthly vapor, this vapor remains after the dissolution of this grain as its <term>radical moisture</term> <note>original: *humido radicali*; in medieval and early modern thought, this was the fundamental life-sustaining fluid found in all living things.</note>, and grows together with it into a plant. Another point must also be observed in every natural dissolution: that since such a dissolution is the <term>quickening</term> <note>original: *vivificatio*; the act of bringing a "dead" or dormant substance back to life.</note> of the dead, this can be achieved by nothing other than that living thing which was of the essence of this dead thing before it died. Just as in a grain there is a dead life (so to speak) which we wish to quicken, this can be achieved by nothing other than the vapor of the earth and the warm moisture of the sky. For the grain itself was extracted from the earth, and was once nothing other than such a vapor, which was afterwards made dead by <term>decoction</term> <note>original: *decoctione*; a process of heating or boiling to concentrate or "ripen" a substance.</note>; therefore, it must be naturally quickened by this vapor alone, while the species is preserved.

I write this because so many men, and so learned, have been greatly deceived by that common <term>mercury</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿; the author is warning against using ordinary quicksilver bought from a merchant.</note>: for although it is a mineral water, it is nonetheless not similar to the <term>Gold of Nature</term> or its essence. For who will not admit that if a grain of wheat is thrown into a watery marsh [where reeds are nonetheless accustomed to grow], it will not germinate nor grow? Why is this, I ask, except that that watery moisture was not essential to it, nor similar to the nature of wheat? For this reason, it does not dissolve naturally, but rather destroys. 

In the same way, <term>Gold</term>, if it is mixed with common <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: *argento vivo*; literally "living silver," the common name for mercury.</note> for boiling, or with any other <term>mercury</term> except its own unique moisture, does not undergo dissolution in them. This is because these waters are too crude, cold, and impure, and are far dissimilar from the <term>Gold of Nature</term>; therefore, the gold is not improved in them, nor does it retain them, nor is it ripened with them into a perfection far nobler [than that nature]. Finally, therefore, our <term>mercury</term> is not the <term>mercury</term> of the common people; for it is a water pure, clean, clear, bright, and shining, and worthy of much admiration. It is crude, cold, and immature if compared to the <term>Sun</term> <note>original: *Solem*; the alchemical symbol for Gold, representing the most "mature" and "hot" state of matter.</note>; but it is mature, warm, and digested with respect to common <term>mercury</term>, which has no qualities similar to this one, except for the color of whiteness alone and the form of its flow—yet even in these things there is a very great difference.

So that you may finally and properly understand what our water is by its circumstances, I tell you [moved by charity] that it is alive,

<header>Toward the Celestial Ruby.</header>

### Toward the Celestial Ruby.

Running, clear, shining, whitest like snow, hot and moist, airy, vaporous, and digesting; in which **Gold** <note>original: *Aurum*</note> melts like ice in lukewarm water. In this is contained the whole rule of fire and **Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*</note>, which exists in this water but does not dominate it. That water is indeed that gate-keeping guardian, the bath of the **King** <note>original: *Regis*; a common alchemical code for gold or the masculine principle.</note> and his **Queen** <note>original: *Reginæ*; representing silver or the feminine principle.</note>, heating them assiduously and incessantly. And yet, this heat is taken from elsewhere than the matter itself, and is distinct from the substance of the whitening water, though joined to it and appearing under the same form of flow and the same color. 

This is that heat of the lamp which, if it be tempered, will daily circulate the matter until the moisture is dried out through <term>Calcination</term> <note>original: *Calcinationem*; the process of reducing a substance to a dry powder by heat.</note>, and a second fire of ashes is produced, in which the vessel or water is hermetically closed and sealed, according to the **Philosopher’s** <note>original: *Philoſophi*; likely referring to Hermes Trismegistus or Geber.</note> saying: *Take the vessel, strike it with the sword, take its soul; this is the sealing.* Therefore, this water of ours is our **Vessel** <note>original: *Vas*</note>, and within it our furnace <note>original: *furnus*</note> dwells secretly. Its ignition must be moderate, lest the whole work be destroyed, yet strong enough so that the spirit does not lose heart for lack of heat. 

Thus, the whole secret of our vessel consists in this water; the structure of the secret furnace is also founded in the composition of this water. In the knowledge of this, all our fires, all weights, and all rules of governance lie hidden. This water is that clear, transparent fountain in which our **King** must be washed so that he may be able to conquer all his enemies. Be diligent concerning this water and its preparation, because certainly without any other aid—except for the application of a perfected, purified, and filed body—**Nature** <note>original: *Natura*</note> will make from this our most secret stone.

And I say to you in truth, that this water is mineral, pure and clean, nor can it be extracted from anywhere except from those things only in which it is naturally present. And that thing from which it is most nearly extracted is the most hidden of all; the way of extracting it is most wonderful, and its power is stupendous. For it dissolves the **Sun** <note>original: *Solem*; the alchemical term for gold.</note> with no trouble and is befriended by it, washing it of all its filth: it is white, lukewarm, and clear. Therefore, let the Most High be praised, who created this **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurium*</note> and gave it a nature surpassing all others. For certainly, without this water, the work would be vain and useless.

Alchemical matters. You, however, must pay attention to what this water is, and learn from the work itself, just as I have done. Consider, therefore, and weigh deeply the possibilities of **Nature**, and do not introduce anything "heterogeneous" <note>foreign or unrelated to the matter</note>: for **Nature** is only improved by its own **Nature**, and by no other. But if you still do not understand, do not blame me; for I have sincerely—insofar as it is lawful for a man to speak—exposed the whole matter to you. Therefore, so that you may understand the conclusion of this matter, be as attentive as possible. **Our Stone** <note>original: *Lapis noster*; the Philosophers' Stone.</note> is made from one thing, and from four mercurial substances [of which one is mature, the others crude and pure; two of these are drawn from a mineral by a third in a wondrous way] joined by a tempered, not violent, fire, and thus cooked daily until one thing is made from them all by a natural, most secret conjunction, not by manual labor.

Afterward, the quality of the fire having been changed, let it be digested by a fire that increases day by day—weaker at the first threshold, and thus daily increased—until these volatile things are fixed. This is done through a **Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*; the active, "masculine" principle of stability and heat.</note> of its own kind, fixed and incombustible, until the entire compound attains the same nature, fixity, and color. For then it securely resists the fire, and this is "the strength of all strengths," <note>original: *fortitudo fortis*; a famous phrase from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, describing the Stone's power.</note> overcoming every subtle thing and penetrating every solid thing; its full power appears when it is turned toward the earth.

To describe the matter in specific terms, there are multiple steps of this process of ours, twelve in number, all of which I shall briefly run through; the first of these is called <term>Calcination</term> <note>original: *Calcinatio*; the reduction of a substance to a powder through heat.</note>.

# ON CALCINATION.

**Calcination** is the first purging of the **Stone**, the drying out of moisture through the power of natural heat, excited by the external heat of the water; whereby the compound is turned into a lime or powder of a black color, which is nevertheless unctuous <note>oily or greasy</note> and retains its radical humidity.

### To the Celestial Ruby <note>original: *Ad Rubin. Cœlestem*; likely a reference to the title of the treatise or the "Heavenly Ruby," a name for the Philosophers' Stone.</note>

...let it be introduced, which cannot be held without this: for **Gold** <note>original: *Aurum*</note> is a very fixed <note>in alchemy, "fixed" refers to a substance that is stable in fire and does not evaporate</note> body, and it cannot be immediately dissolved by our water, unless it is only in part—that is, it must be soft, raw, and made white. In this whitening, two Natures appear, the volatile and the fixed, which we liken to **Dragons** or **Serpents**. Therefore, so that a full dissolution may occur, there is a need for crushing by calcining <note>original: *calcinando*; the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder</note> the Body, so that it becomes spongy and viscous, because only then is it fit for solution.

The second final cause <note>the purpose or ultimate goal of the action</note> is this: that we reconcile contrary qualities; for while they fight, they are useless to us. In the first conjunction, our water distinguishes between *Sulphur* and volatile and fixed *Mercury* <note>original: *☿*</note>; and these are mutual enemies to one another, being different things. It is our task to recall them to unity. However, contrary qualities are not reconciled except through a medium <note>a middle substance or state that shares characteristics with both extremes</note>. Therefore, in our first operation there are four contrary qualities: heat, cold, dryness, and moisture. Two of these—heat and dryness—are attributed to *Sulphur*; cold and moisture are attributed to *Mercury*. They are thus opposed in diametric contrariety: the heat of *Sulphur* and the cold of *Mercury*, as well as the moisture of the *Mercury* and the dryness of the *Sulphur*. To bring these contraries back to friendship, it cannot be done without a medium; the medium will therefore be a participant in both, and suited to both. Thus, if we wish to reconcile heat and cold, the medium through which this is done will be dryness, which can be joined to both heat and cold. By turning the compound into earth, heat and cold now agree in this third state so that they can live together, albeit in a lessened degree. Afterward, by dissolving it into water, the other two enemies—dryness and moisture—are reconciled through the coldness of the water, so that now one thing is made from two by a conjunction performed after a natural separation.

The efficient cause <note>the agent or force that produces the effect</note> of this Calcination is the operation of heat upon the moisture; converting everything that resists it into a most subtle powder. The moving instrument, however, is the fire, enclosed against the nature of our dissolving water; it excites the heat in the body and digests the moisture into a viscous or oily powder.

...right; First, because a certain dissolution, so to speak, has already been performed through our divine water. Truly, the woman retains all her power in water; therefore, the first work of the man exerting his strength will be to overcome that in which the woman possesses both her qualities; once this is done, he will easily subject to himself that in which she has only one quality. <note>In alchemical allegory, the "Woman" represents the moist, cool Mercury, while the "Man" represents the hot, dry Sulfur. Calcination is therefore the head of the work; for without this, there will be neither mixing nor union. This must be done in the first days of your stone, for in the first **whitening** <note>original: *dealbatione*; a stage where the matter turns white, signaling a degree of purification</note> the body is reduced into its two principles: <term>Sulfur</term> <note>the active, "male," or combustible principle of matter</note> and <term>Quicksilver</term> <note>original: *Argentum vivum*; the fluid, "female," or metallic principle</note>. They are therefore compared to two **Serpents** or **Dragons**: one winged, signifying its volatile <note>tending to evaporate or fly away in fire</note> nature, and the other without wings, denoting fixity <note>stability and resistance to fire</note>. Both of these, proceeding from a single source, tend toward one goal; therefore, it is likened to a **Serpent catching its tail in its mouth** <note>the Ouroboros, a symbol of the unity of matter and the cyclic nature of the universe</note>. This is to show that Sulfur is nothing outside the substance of Mercury, nor is Mercury outside the substance of Sulfur, but that this Mercurial Sulfur and Sulfurous <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: *☿*</note> complete the entire art. 

It is rightly called a single compound, which even if it appears double at the very threshold of the work—whence it is called <term>Rebis</term> <note>from the Latin *res bina*, meaning "a double thing"; the hermaphroditic union of opposites</note>—can nevertheless become one and the same through Conjunction. This "one" is called the <term>Elixir</term> <note>the perfected substance or medicine of the Stone</note>, which would never be possible unless they were of the exact same Nature. Therefore, the nature of Sulfur and Mercury must be diligently observed, and errors avoided: for these two are not different things, but one and the same: Sulfur is mature and digested Mercury, and Mercury is crude and immature Sulfur.

We must therefore observe that divine work of generation <note>original: *genesis opus*; the process of creation or birth</note>—specifically, how Nature has worked in the procreation of metallic bodies beneath the earth in the mines. In our work, we perform everything in imitation of her as closely as possible; for this reason, we choose the same material which she used, although Art has discovered for itself a far more subtle way of preparation to shorten the work and achieve a more-than-perfect **exaltation** <note>the process of raising a substance to a higher state of purity or power</note> of the stone.

For in the metallic veins, only one thing is found, namely Mercury, which is quite crude and cold, and in which the Sulfurous quality is utterly overwhelmed. Almost no digestive heat is found there; however, by an imperceptible motion over a long period of time, this metallic principle is changed little by little until it is finally converted into **fixed Sulfur**. <note>Sulfur that has become resistant to the power of fire and no longer evaporates</note> Thus, while it remained cold and moist, it was called Mercury; in this state of elevation or excitation, it is named Sulfur.

But the matter is different in this work of ours: for besides the crude and cold Mercury, we have something else—namely, mature **Gold**, in which the active qualities exist in actuality. Therefore, we join this Gold to our Mercury (in which the passive qualities are found) so that one may assist the other. That which Nature digested in the mines without the aid of any heat, we—possessing a **double fire**—digest; from this it happens that we produce not simply Gold, but something much more noble and excellent than Gold.

You see, then, what Sulfur is and what Mercury is, and how we also have a double Mercury and a double Sulfur in our art. ...until finally the whole is dissolved into a kind of oily and sticky water; for our operations are so linked together that one is the cause and the beginning of the other, and without one, the other can neither be held nor understood. **First**, that you obtain our <term>Mercury</term> <note>This refers to "Philosophical Mercury," a specialized substance, not the common quicksilver found in a pharmacy.</note>, without which nothing happens in this art: see to it, therefore, that you are not deceived by that common **Mercury**, which is utterly useless for our work; for if you work with it until the very last day, you will find nothing in it.

**Second**, care must be taken that the fire of the furnace is not too intense, but that its measure be that of an oven: so that you may fully understand this, know that the <term>Sulphur</term> <note>In alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, masculine, and "fiery" principle of a substance.</note> which does not dominate in the **Mercury** or water—that is what digests the matter—which [Sulphur] and <term>Azoth</term> <note>The universal solvent or the essential "mercury" of the metals.</note> are abundantly sufficient for you. Hold these things regarding the internal fire as opposed to the natural fire; I call it "internal" because it increases the work at the end.

...lest you drown the moisture of your stone, but rather temper it skillfully and gently according to the requirements of Nature, so that the strength of the stone is not diminished. **Fourthly**, you must attend to the sealing of the vessel, lest the spirits fly away and the work be destroyed. Guard the vessel and its binding, and do not think this is of little importance. Consider, then, with what great care Nature closed the womb of the pregnant woman, so that nothing could enter, otherwise the fetus would perish. With no less industry should you also be cautious in this matter while perfecting this Philosophical work, lest your labor be in vain. Listen, therefore, to the Philosopher <note>Likely referring to a specific authority such as Aristotle or an alchemical master.</note> saying: "Take the vessel and strike the fires with a sword, receive the soul; this is the closure." <note>original: "Accipe vas & ignes percute gladio, animam recipe, hæc est clausura." For this error is irreparable, leading to most certain loss.

They cannot satisfy themselves without either moving the vessel, opening it, or adding and taking something away; or at least they increase the fire to hasten the work. In this way, they hinder the **work of nature** and consequently do not reach the desired ends.

# To the Celestial Ruby

After the silver color of the <term>amalgamated</term> <note>A mixture of metals, typically involving mercury to soften or dissolve them.</note> body, a perfect blackness will appear. This color does not arrive by a momentary entry, but daily; as the whiteness is diminished, the blackness more and more supervenes, until it is finally completed. For blackness is the sign of the dissolved body, which does not happen in a single hour, but little by little, yet unceasingly. For the <term>tincture</term> <note>The spiritual essence or "soul" of the material that carries its color and transformative power.</note> emerging from the reins <note>The "kidneys" or innermost core.</note> of the <term>Sun and Moon</term> <note>Original: "Solis & Lunae." Alchemical code for gold and silver.</note> shows itself as black to the eyes, but it is drawn out from the senses, and imperceptibly. Therefore, the arrival of the blackness and the exit of the tincture from the viscera of the body to be dissolved follow the same manner and timing; for as soon as the tincture has totally emerged, the blackness will be perfect and absolute.

On this matter, hear what the *Children’s Game* <note>Original: "Ludus puerorum," a famous 14th-century alchemical treatise that emphasizes the simplicity of the work.</note> says: *First, the more you cook it, the more you refine what is coarse and blacken the compound.* And *Bernard of Trevisan* <note>A legendary alchemist previously mentioned as a model of patience.</note> says: when the Earth begins to dominate the rest of the elements, blackness appears; yet it does not obtain its dominion except gradually. To conclude in a word, there are only four principal colors; the first of which is blackness, and it is the slowest in its arrival and the longest in its duration. If it were made perfect in a momentary entry, the work would certainly be very swift, for it would perish no more slowly than it arrived, and it would not remain at the peak of blackness for even an hour. 

For there is no pause in these operations; rather, it grows to the peak of one degree, which it no sooner reaches than it begins to decrease again. Therefore, one ascends slowly toward blackness, and one also descends slowly from it; there is not even a moment in which it neither ascends nor descends, for nothing rests except at its end, and blackness is not the end of our <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone.</note>, therefore it does not rest in it.

How then will the blackness appear? In this way, surely: just as night arrives. First comes twilight, then finally the black night, and this happens through imperceptible degrees, with less light existing in the air at each moment than the one before, until finally nothing at all illuminates it; then deep night is seen. Now, all of this usually happens within an hour, yet the movement is imperceptible; since our work requires a longer space of time, this movement will necessarily be even more unperceivable. ### A Brief Guide

Therefore, you who seek this, consider the example brought before you, and you will have your answer.

**Objection:** But after the first excitation <note>The initial application of heat or the beginning of the chemical reaction.</note> of the matter, the <term>tincture</term> <note>The spiritual essence or coloring principle of the stone.</note> emerges at every hour and moment; the color of the emerging tincture is truly the blackest black. Therefore, within an hour after the first excitation of the matter, the blackest blackness should appear.

But **it is answered** that the blackest blackness belongs to the tincture once it has *emerged*, not while it is still *emerging*. Or if it is so, it nevertheless exits imperceptibly—truly an imperceptible blackness. Although the blackest substance has emerged, when it is mixed into a great deal of white, it will not manifest the blackest blackness in the whole compound, but rather an off-white color—provided that the subject of the whiteness is not subtle and well-purified, just as this white material is now. Indeed, the tincture in its first exit is not completely black, but obtains this through <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The alchemical "rotting" or breakdown of matter, necessary for rebirth.</note>. This is not a bare exiting of the tincture, but arises from that strife and resistance between the emerged tincture and the extracting water; that is, between <term>Sulphur</term> and <term>Mercury</term> <note>The two primary "parents" of metals in alchemical theory.</note>. On this matter, hear **Morienus** <note>Morienus Romanus, a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemical teacher.</note> saying:

> *Our operation is nothing other than the extraction of water from its earth, and not only that, but the returning of the water upon the earth, until the earth putrefies.*

The <term>tincture</term>, therefore, is not entirely black of itself; rather, it is most white. Yet it emerges with the sign of blackness because the more the <term>tincture</term> (which is the <term>soul</term>) emerges, the more the earth (which is the <term>body</term>) is deprived of life <note>Original: "exanimatur," meaning to be stripped of the "anima" or soul.</note>, and thus it <term>putrefies</term> and turns black.

How much time, then, must one wait before it blackens perfectly? On this point, pay attention to what **Flamel** <note>Nicolas Flamel (c. 1330–1418), the famous French scrivener who reportedly discovered the Philosopher's Stone.</note> says:

> *The color you must see first is blackness—and not just any blackness, but the blackest [aterrima]—and that within the space of forty days.*

**Ripley** <note>Sir George Ripley (c. 1415–1490), an influential English alchemist and Augustinian canon.</note> says the same:

> *Permit the mixed and leveled natures to lie together for six weeks to conceive; wait for that time with a slow fire.*

When the colors die, they will demonstrate it; for at that time they will boil like liquid pitch and putrefy. And **Bernard** <note>Bernard of Trevisan, a frequent source for the author regarding patience and the stages of the work.</note> says in his parable:

> *The King, stripping off his splendid robes, hands over his silks to <term>Saturn</term> <note>Saturn is the planetary symbol for Lead and the color black; here, it represents the onset of the Nigredo.</note>, and is clothed in black, which he retains for forty days.*

Understand all of this, however, as referring to blackness in its highest degree, which is clear from Flamel’s words repeated above; but the faint blackness... <note>The text continues onto the next page.</note>

[the blackness] will appear more quickly: thus the *Scale of the Philosophers* <note>original: "scala Philosophorum," a famous alchemical treatise detailing the steps of the Great Work.</note> says regarding the stage of <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The chemical breakdown or "rotting" of the substance, considered the first essential step in alchemy.</note>, *within sixteen days, he says, while maintaining a light fire*, the matter will be continuously covered in blackness: and this happens either later or sooner according to the skill of the operator in the preparation of the materials.

Truly, do intermediate colors appear in the progress from white to black, just as they do in the progress from black to white? For it seems that they do, because a transition is not given from one extreme to another except through intermediaries. And we answer that they do indeed appear, though certainly in a confused manner; and some colors will appear in a particular work during the progress toward the height of <term>blackness</term> <note>original: "nigredinis," the Nigredo stage.</note> which perhaps will not appear in another, namely because they are nothing but accidental colors. 

Truly, these are not exactly the same colors between the first whiteness and the blackness as those between this blackness and the final <term>whiteness</term> <note>original: "albedinem," the Albedo stage.</note>; because the nature of the matter is not the same. In the former, the matter was thick and more earthy, needing to be burned and purified; but in this [later] work, the matter is more spiritual and purer. Therefore, in a pure or cleansed subject, in the progress from the extreme of blackness to the extreme of whiteness, the intermediate colors will be much brighter and more wonderful than those which appeared in the earthy subject. 

Truly, they will appear in both progressions: in the first transition between extremes, they are darker, fewer, and uglier; in the later transition, they are more numerous, more brilliant, and more splendid. As the Philosopher witnesses, after the height of blackness and before the whiteness, in the hour of the greatest conjunction, wonders will appear: for however many colors can be imagined in the whole world, they will then be visible. And <term>Ripley</term> <note>George Ripley (c. 1415–1490), a famous English alchemist known for his "Twelve Gates."</note> says, in our work there will appear colors than which no more beautiful have ever appeared. 

Likewise, before the perfect blackness, intermediate colors will show themselves, as witnessed by the Philosopher, who, depicting the colors of the <term>Dragons</term> <note>In alchemical symbolism, "Dragons" often represent the volatile and fixed principles (like Mercury and Sulphur) or the raw, unrefined matter undergoing change.</note>, says they are black, yellow, and azure. These intermediate colors, he says, denote that your concoctions are not yet perfectly putrefied; in a word, during the "dying" [of the matter], various darker colors will be seen, but they are rare and few, and this is before the dark night clouds over the whole Horizon. 

During the "resurrection," however, many and most splendid colors will arise, as the body now begins to be glorified, and light begins to predominate over the darkness; and this occurs in a cleansed and spiritual subject.

Truly, in what order will these aforementioned colors appear? This certainly cannot be determined, because they vary in many ways; however, the better the essence of the <term>water of life</term> <note>original: "aquæ vitæ," referring here to the "mercurial water" or alchemical solvent used to break down the materials.</note> is, the better the signs will appear. The order of the four principal colors is described by everyone; however, no one can determine the order of the accidental colors. Let it be enough for you if you have complete <term>blackness</term> <note>original: "nigredinem," the Nigredo stage, symbolizing death and putrefaction of the matter.</note> within forty days; do not care much for the rest. But it is good to pay attention, for blackness is the first and most desirable color, and although others may appear, unless you see this one, you have undoubtedly strayed. 

But as has been said, other colors are not to be despised, except for the <term>venereal color</term> <note>original: "venereo colore," typically referring to a greenish hue associated with the planet Venus and copper.</note> or an imperfect red. If these appear before the blackness, they are to be viewed with suspicion, especially when dryness of the compound and a separation of the parts accompanies them; this premature rush, I say, is a fatal sign to the operator of wasted time.

The Philosopher <note>A common title for an authoritative source, often Aristotle or a legendary alchemical figure.</note> testifies to this same thing, saying, *excessive fire prevents the union and tints the white with the color of the wild poppy.* And Flamel <note>Nicolas Flamel (c. 1330–1418), a French scribe who became a legendary figure in alchemy.</note> says in his *Hieroglyphic Figures*: *unless you have seen the blackest black of the black, whatever other color you see, you are on the path of error; but the reddening color is especially to be suspected, for if you have seen that, you have burned—or are even now burning—the life-giving power of the stone.*

But one must not linger longer on these matters, since one water does all of this, provided the compound is governed with a continuous external heat assisting the internal one; nor is anything in the whole work more marvelous than this water of ours, which I have fully described above, to which place I refer you.

# ON DISSOLUTION.

The Dissolution of our Stone is its reduction into its first matter, the manifestation of the moisture, and the extraction of the Natures from their depth, which is accomplished by leading them into a mineral water.

This operation is not of light work or significance, for those who have sweated over it can attest to how difficult it is.

# THE SOURCE

## OF CHEMICAL PHILO-
## SOPHY.

**I** shall divide the whole of the art into these parts: the first will contain the things constituting the work substantially and essentially; the second will cover their arrangement. The things essentially constituting the stone are the body, or <term>mature sulfur</term> <note>original: "sulphur maturum"; the active, masculine principle of the work, often identified with gold or a fixed metallic core.</note>, also called <term>red bronze</term> <note>original: "æs rubrum"; a symbolic name for the solar substance.</note>; and the water, or immature mercury, also called <term>white bronze</term> <note>original: "æs album"; the lunar or feminine substance.</note>. To these are added the vessel, the furnace, and the <term>triple fire</term> <note>original: "ignis triplex"; usually referring to the distinct grades of heat—such as the lamp, the bath, and the sand—used during different stages of the process.</note>. The arrangement of these things considers both weight and "regimen" <note>the management or governance of the process over time.</note>. The weight is twofold, and the regimen is twofold. These complete the following operations: <term>Calcination</term>, <term>Dissolution</term>, <term>Separation</term>, <term>Conjunction</term>, <term>Putrefaction</term>, <term>Distillation</term>, <term>Coagulation</term>, <term>Sublimation</term>, <term>Fixation</term>, and <term>Exaltation</term>.

The first two of these operations are performed chiefly by the temperate, non-burning, and altering heat of the "first fire," which warms <term>the King’s bath</term> <note>original: "balneum Regis"; the mercurial solvent or liquid medium used to dissolve the metallic "King."</note>. This changes the material first into a subtle, viscous, fragmented, black, and foul-smelling earth, and then into a multi-colored mineral water; this is called the <term>fire against Nature</term> <note>original: "ignis contra Naturam"; a technical term for the chemical solvent that performs the work of "burning" or dissolving without literal flames.</note>. The three operations that follow are performed by the union of the first and third fires—that is, the "natural" fire and the "fire against nature." When joined in this way, they create an "unnatural fire" by circulating the matter daily and separating the subtle from the thick, until the whole becomes of the same temperament; then, by joining the separated parts and impregnating them, they bring about putrefaction.

The final five operations are performed by the <term>Fire of Nature</term> <note>original: "igne Naturæ"; the internal, life-giving heat inherent in the matter itself.</note>, which grows and predominates day by day, and which first [acts upon] the putrefied matter daily

it circulates it, and purges it from dregs, by frequent ascent and descent, which is therefore called **Distillation**, **Volatilization**, **Washing**, **Purification**, **Cohobation** <note>original: "Cohobatio"; the process of redistilling a liquid by pouring it back onto the solid matter left in the vessel to extract more essence.</note>, **Imbibition** <note>original: "Imbibitio"; the soaking of a solid in a liquid until it is saturated.</note>, **Feeding** <note>original: "Cibatio"; the gradual addition of liquid to "feed" the growing matter.</note>, the **Moistening of the earth**, and this is done by heat for so long, until at last dryness begins to coagulate, which is called **thickening** <note>original: "inspissatio"</note>, which through longer concoction or sublimation induces **fixity**, the goal of which is **exaltation** <note>the process of raising a substance to its highest state of dignity and potency</note>; this is not a local change from a lower place to a higher one, but making something most noble from a vile thing.

These are all our operations, and successive arrangements, which by some are called as many "regimens": which name if anyone prefers to apply, he is allowed to do so; however, know that there is only a twofold fire, the **Natural** and **against nature**: of which the latter acts first, because only through this is the former brought out into the light, and it is necessary for <term>putrefaction</term> <note>the symbolic "death" or decomposition of the substance, usually indicated by a black color</note> to precede regeneration; and when these two fight with each other, they produce the **unnatural fire**, and from this struggle arises putrefaction: after which, however, there is a glorious regeneration, in which the **Sulfur** and **water** become one, and together they receive congealment from no fire except the natural one.

Therefore our **Body**, which is commonly called **Lemnian earth** <note>original: "terra Lemnia"; historically a medicinal clay from the island of Lemnos, used here as an alchemical code for the solid "earthy" base of the work</note>, completes the whole work, but by no means unless it is watered with its own water: which is truly **rain water**, not that which the common people know how to prepare; but ours, which no one except the true philosopher has ever seen—believe me, for I speak the truth—fools know how to extract many waters, namely those that wet the hands, but our water is the life of all things, over which you must sweat; then neither the **Sun** <note>Gold</note> nor the **Moon** <note>Silver</note> will be lacking for the gaining of riches. I will say, and that from a faithful heart, what kind of water this is: it is the water of **Saltpeter** <note>original: "Salis petræ"; literally "salt of stone"</note>, which in its outward appearance is like <term>Mercury</term>, but in its heart is pure **hellish fire** <note>original: "ignis infernus"; in alchemy, this refers to a deep, central, and potent transformative heat, rather than a place of punishment</note>: beware, however, that you are not deceived by **quicksilver** <note>original: "Argento vivo"; common liquid mercury</note>, but understand that Mercury which the **Sun**, returning in the month of March, pours out through all places; this you shall collect in the month of October, because then it is certainly found mature, and the most precious treasure of the whole world.

But so that I may describe our <term>Mercury</term> <note>symbol: ☿</note>, our rain water, to you in such a way that you can find it, know that it is before the eyes of the whole world, which...

...but [it is] a composite, namely of the vessel and the fire of the Philosophers, to which a third is added, namely the bond <note>original: "vinculum"; refers to the unifying principle that holds the elements together during the alchemical process.</note>. When therefore we speak of our vessel, understand it to be our water; when we speak of the fire, likewise understand the water; and when we discuss the furnace, we mean nothing diverse or divided from the water. There is therefore one vessel, one furnace, one fire, and all these things are one, namely the water. The fire therefore digests, the vessel whitens and penetrates, and the furnace or bond surrounds and includes all things; and the fire is <term>Mercury</term> <note>The text uses the symbol ☿, representing Mercury, which in alchemy is the "universal spirit" or "First Matter" rather than just the common metal.</note>, the vessel is also <term>Mercury</term>, and the furnace finally is the same <term>Mercury</term>. And note well: there is no fire in the whole work except Mercury, though it may appear in many forms of fire and many forms of water. Therefore, both the fire and the water are diversified in their power within the work, as they are in number, but in their genus they agree in one and the same thing: namely, Mercury. Thus our fire is living, the water living, the vessel living, the furnace living, and all these things are one.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Know also, most dear [reader], that there is only one thing in the whole world in which this Mercury of ours is to be found. It is similar to Gold in essence, but dissimilar in substance; by converting its elements, you will find what you seek. Join Heaven with Earth upon the fire of friendship, and in the midst of the firmament you will see the bird of Hermes <note>original: "avem Hermetis"; a famous alchemical symbol for the rising spirit or the process of sublimation where a substance is purified by being turned into vapor.</note>. Do not confound the Natures, but divide and then rejoin them, and you shall reign in honor through your whole life. Hear, therefore, this greatest secret.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;From the Southern region toward the West, a very high mountain is found, closest to the Sun, which is one of the seven, and second in height from the highest. This mountain, of which we now speak, is of an exceedingly hot temperature because it is not far distant from the Sun; and in this mountain a vapor is enclosed, or a spirit, which is primarily necessary for our work. However, it does not ascend unless it is vivified, and it is not vivified unless the earth is dug to the knees at the summit of the mountain. But if this is done, the spirit ascends—or a very thin exhalation—which, being congealed by the air, runs down drop by drop into a most clear water, heated like a bath, which is immediately collected. For it is the true Caduceus <note>The staff of Mercury, usually depicted with two snakes; here it represents the power of the alchemical solvent.</note> of Mercury, with which he performs wonders. This is our water, our vessel, our fire, and our furnace; and it is our Mercury, not that of the common people, but a liquor of the purest Salt, hot and moist, which we call Mercury.

...ed. Hold this secret. <meta>This page continues the technical explanation of how Mercury acts as a "water" for metals. It follows from the previous page's discussion on how the art of alchemy shortens the natural process of gold-making by mixing Mercury with Sulphur. <page-num>807</page-num>

-> ## The Source of Chemical Philosophy. <-

[It] is by its own nature cold and moist; nonetheless, if it is mixed with any vegetable in a <term>decoction</term> <note>The process of boiling a substance in a liquid to extract its essence.</note>, it takes on and clothes itself in the qualities of the thing mixed with it—namely, that which was blended in. Its force and spirit, or life, which resides in the water, comes out into the water through the boiling process, and the water reciprocally receives its nature. However, the thick and bodily earthy part of the boiled substance is not that spirit which changes the water’s qualities, but is separable from the moisture after the boiling is complete.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the same way, one must understand **Quicksilver** <note>original: "Argento vivo"</note> and its various forms, though with a difference: for whatever Metal or Mineral is so familiar to **Mercury** that it can be mixed with it at the most minute level <note>original: "per minima"</note> and be boiled together, that Mercury takes on other qualities according to the species of the metal thus joined to it, and it will cast off its own dross <note>original: "feces"</note>. Therefore, metallic and mineral species are to be boiled in it subordinately and alternately; [Mercury] itself is their "water," into which the mineral spirits are released through boiling. They alter that water, not unlike vegetables boiled in their own simple water. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Yet two differences are to be noted between the aforementioned boilings. First, that water does not become <term>fixed</term> <note>In alchemy, a substance is "fixed" when it is made solid and can withstand the heat of fire without evaporating.</note> with vegetables during <term>coagulation</term> <note>The process of a liquid becoming solid or semi-solid.</note>, whereas Mercury does become fixed with metals; for these [metallic] compositions are stronger than those [vegetable ones]. Second, in the boiling of vegetables or animals, the water—since it is a transparent liquid—receives not only a new virtue and new qualities, but also a different color from the one it previously had. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;This, however, is not the case with Mercury. For its nature is altered, but not its color nor the form of its flow; rather, the color of the dissolved metal lies hidden under the form of the liquid quicksilver, and by its own power it does not appear. Therefore, first Mercury acts by dissolving the Metal, and afterwards the Metal acts by coagulating the Mercury. And just as in the <term>dissolution</term> <note>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid.</note> the form and color of the Metal lay hidden under the form and color of the Mercury, so also in the coagulation the form and color of the Mercury are hidden under the color and form of the Metal. Thus, neither do the qualities of the Metal prevent the flow of the Mercury during dissolution, nor do the qualities of the Mercury hinder the stability of the metal during coagulation. Do you not observe here a certain wonderful harmony <note>original: "concordantiam"</note> between **Mercury** and the Metals? For they love one another like a mother and a son,
