...sister and brother, male and female; for which reason bodies are improved through "water," and they receive in it and through it a breadth of subtlety—that is, a spiritual and volatile nature. The water, in turn, is amended by the bodies, is retained by them, and takes on a bodily nature. Thus the whole compound is ripened together once the active agents have become passive, and vice-versa. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The reason why the color of **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurii"</note> is not changed by a dissolved body during the boiling process <note>original: "decoctione"</note> is this: earth and water are so perfectly uniform <note>original: "homogenea"</note> in Mercury, and so well-tempered, that neither can be separated from the other. They are so powerfully mixed that, despite the wondrous thinness of the matter, the substance is so dense that it hides the colors. Hence, if any part of the Mercury is corrupted—whether destructively by defiling things, or productively when joined with a body suited to its nature—it will immediately manifest the color instilled into the substance. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;There are, moreover, specific proportions of Mercury regarding earth and water: in respect to the latter [water], it flows and is liquid; in respect to the former [earth], it moistens nothing it touches, except for that which shares the unity of its own nature. From these very facts, all the errors of those working with Mercury are revealed. Some block or divide its uniformity by drying it out through various <term>sublimations</term> <note>The process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, used for purification.</note>; others corrupt the "earth" within it, creating an imbalance by trying to make it transparent. Whoever these people may be, they never achieve anything except a **Sophistical work** <note>In alchemy, a "sophistical" result is a "fool's gold"—something that looks like the goal but lacks the true medicinal or transformative properties.</note>. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For Mercury is the **seed of metals** <note>original: "Metallorum sperma"</note>, which Nature, with great wisdom, formed in the veins of the earth to become metal. It lacks nothing except a pure "digestion" <note>A slow, steady heating process mimicking the warmth of the earth.</note>; however, it cannot be digested except by a pure, non-burning metallic **Sulphur**. Mercury indeed possesses this Sulphur at its own center, through which Nature, over a long period of time, would form **Gold** from it. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Yet how Nature performs this by its own skill is unknown to man. To be sure, while Gold could be made from Mercury alone without any additions, it would only be completed over a vast amount of time and with such great expense that it would be foolish to attempt it for the sake of making simple Gold. There is, therefore, a unique Sulphur in the world that Nature has already perfected, which is most "intimate" or familiar to Mercury. This Sulphur is mixed with Mercury at the very root <note>original: "radicaliter"</note>; through this, the Mercury is boiled down, and the Mercury—because of the opposition of their qualities—causes that Sulphur to undergo <term>putrefaction</term> <note>A stage of breakdown and blackening (the nigredo) considered essential before a substance can be reborn in a higher form.</note>, and so through...

...[by a due heat] it is cherished, and fed with its own food, then indeed from **Gold** will be had that which will abundantly fulfill our work. In this way, a man, insofar as he is a man, cannot be called a **Father**, nor can he be called the matter of an embryo: but he has within himself such matter from which—through the joining of unlike spermatic matter of the same kind and through a fit arrangement—an infant is formed. I believe that **Gold** must be understood in exactly the same way. Gold is certainly the most perfect of all Metals, and the father of our **stone** <note>The "Philosopher's Stone," the goal of the alchemical Great Work</note>, yet it is not the *matter* of it. Rather, the **sperm** which is in the Gold, which it emits—if only it be treated by the art—this surely will be the masculine matter of our stone itself. It is nothing other than the most "digested" <note>In alchemy, digestion refers to a slow, steady heating process that matures a substance</note> virtue of Gold, which is extracted from it by skillful art; then it is called our **living Gold**, and not the common kind, which is **dead**. So too in the procreation of a man: a man can be called "dead" [with respect to the act of generation] until he has poured forth the proper matter which he has within himself into a fit place; it happens no differently in our art. 

Therefore, our **Gold** is not the **gold of the common people** <note>original: "Aurum vulgi," referring to the metal used for coins and jewelry</note>: for they differ just as a father differs from his [own] sperm. The first <note>The alchemical "sperm"</note> is useful and living for our work; but the other <note>Common gold</note> is dead and useless, until it is quickened—that is, until it emits its own sperm [which is the active virtue of our stone]. 

Thus, therefore, proceed with the greatest caution: take this **body** which I have shown, and gently extract the **seed** from it. Then indeed [and not before], this **Gold** [which was previously dead, idle, and useless] having been made living, active, and suitable for our work by this art, will supply you with the **first matter** of our stone—the masculine kind, namely. Thus, we no longer call this "Gold," but rather **bronze**, **magnesia**, **lead**, or **dung** <note>original: "æs, magnesia, plumbum, fimus"; alchemists used these "low" names for their secret substance to hide its value and nature from the uninitiated</note>. Nor indeed can it properly be called Gold anymore; for Gold is a **body**, but this is **chaos**—that is, **spirit**. Nor by any art will it return to the former appearance of Gold, because the body has been converted into spirit.

Leaving aside all common operations, I follow the intention of the Philosophers, and I desire that sublimation which they call the first preparation of the subtle matter. Through this, the **Eclipse** of the earthly obstacle is removed from the **Moon** <note>The lunar or feminine principle, often associated with silver or purified mercury</note>, so that it may receive illumination from the **Sun** <note>The solar or masculine principle, associated with gold</note>. This dew softens the earth and excites great winds in its belly or bosom, which carry our **stone** upward, where it is imbued with celestial virtue. Having fallen back again to the earth, which is its nurse <note>A direct reference to the "Emerald Tablet," a foundational alchemical text: "The wind carried it in its belly; the earth is its nurse."</note>, it puts on an earthly and corporeal nature; thus it receives the power of the things above and the things below. 

We conclude, therefore, that in no way can either **Gold** or **Mercury** provide us the first matter of our **stone** until the tincture is extracted from the **Gold** by dissolving it through the dissolving **Mercury**. This tincture is a living, active virtue, not a dead one, just as **Gold** was dead before its dissolution. This is the matter of the ancient Philosophers, which, as the **Author of the New Light** <note>original: "Auctor novi luminis," referring to Michael Sendivogius, a famous 17th-century alchemist</note> says, *exists, but does not appear until it pleases the artist, and in the knowledge of which lies all perfection.*

Hence a certain Philosopher, writing of this fire, says: *Behold, the fire I show you is water* <note>original: *Ecce ignis quem tibi oſtendam eſt aqua*</note>. Therefore, my brother, let it not be a cause of doubt to you that I previously numbered our furnace, fire, and vessel among the things essentially constituting the **Stone**: for in this I follow the intention of all Philosophers writing on this art. *even transformed an impure mass of Lead <note>original: "Plumbi"</note>, which is volatile in fire, into fixed Gold <note>original: "Aurum"</note> through the application of a small amount of transmutatory powder, in a mere moment; and it stood the test of any Fire so persistently that no one can doubt it any longer. This includes those who, until now, have persuaded themselves and others that this Secret <note>original: "Arcanum"</note> is to be found nowhere on earth. On the contrary, let us be most thoroughly persuaded that there exists in the Nature of things that First-Material Mercury of the Philosophers <term>Mercury of the Philosophers: Not common quicksilver, but a theoretical primordial substance that alchemists believed was the "root" of all metals and the key to the Philosopher's Stone.</term>, which is like a Fountain overflowing with wondrous effects. These effects escape even the sharpest and most critical human reason, as will become clear from this little Work of mine, which I wished to name for and consecrate to You, my primary Patrons, as my most wise Defenders and Lords. In the meantime, however, I pray you know that I did not write this with the goal of teaching anyone an Art unknown to myself, but only to recount the true Process of this Secret. For what, indeed, sails further or protects the Truth better than the true Light of Truth itself? It is, after all, the way of brute beasts to pass through life in silence, especially regarding those things which are most looked for and required to propagate the glory of the most wise and powerful God the Creator. Therefore, since it would be unworthy and ungrateful to the Divine Majesty for a man—who ought to be a partner in the Divine Nature—to become as dull as the beasts, I have brought it into my mind to offer this most rare history to you, my most faithful Friends and Patrons of this Science, and to recount everything in good faith, as far as the strengths of my mind have allowed at the time. Thus, setting aside all the charms and ribbons of flowery words, I shall immediately prepare myself to relate whatever I have seen and heard concerning this Elias the Artist <term>Elias the Artist: A legendary figure in alchemical prophecy, a "chemical messiah" expected to appear and reveal the ultimate secrets of nature and medicine.</term>. To be sure, I was not in such intimate familiarity with Him that he might instruct me in the Manner of preparing the Universal Medicine <note>The "Universal Medicine" or Elixir was believed to cure all diseases and prolong life.</note> by the Method of Physico-artificial Chemistry; yet, he provided me with such reasons in the Method of Healing that I am never able to extol him enough with his well-deserved praises. Therefore, most Curious Lords, Patrons, and Lovers of the true Chemical art, receive this slight little gift with fair minds; or, if you prefer, read it through merely for the sake of refreshing the mind. In it, I am about to relate everything that took place between us on various occasions, and indeed in the form of a dialogue. I most humbly pray that you receive this new little book with the same benevolence with which you have received others of my Treatises, for I humbly dedicate and dutifully give it to You for the sake of moving and increasing your wonder. Fare well, greetings, and be favorable.*

->**Most Excellent and Most Experienced Lords,**<-

*Before I begin to write concerning the Philosophical Pygmy conquering and binding the Giants in this Theater of Secrets, please grant, I pray, that with your permission I may use the words of Van Helmont excerpted from his book on the <term>Tree of Life</term> <note>original: "Arbore Vitæ"</note> page 630, which I shall transcribe here.*

I am forced to believe that there is a **Gold-making and Silver-making Stone**; but, friends of the <term>Spagyric Art</term> <note>The "Spagyric Art" refers to the alchemical process of separating and recombining the constituents of bodies to produce more potent medicines or metals.</note>, I am not unaware that many among the wisest—even among those who are considered the most exquisite of <term>Chemists</term>—have consumed not only their own goods, but also those of others alongside them in this great Vulcanian Secret <note>A "Vulcanian" secret refers to Vulcan, the Roman god of fire, signifying the intense heat and metallurgical skill required in alchemy.</note>, which experience proves more than enough to this very day. For we see, alas! daily, how these incautious <term>Chemists</term>—indeed, those more worthily called **ALL-CHEMISTS** <note>original: "ALGEMISTÆ," likely a pun by Van Helmont mocking those who claim to do everything or who lose "all" their wealth.</note>, and simply *Laborers*—are deluded by the cunning of such diabolical "Gold-making" and "Silver-making" flies. I also know that many foolish men will rise up and contradict the truth of my genuine experience [regarding the True <term>Philosopher's Stone</term>]. Specifically, one claims it is the work of the Devil; another, that it is hocus-pocus <note>original: "OKOSBOKOS"</note>; that one claims it is merely the Soul of Gold—namely that with one ounce of Gold one might be able to tinge <note>In alchemy, to "tinge" is to transform a base metal into a noble one by applying a small amount of the transmuting agent.</note> one ounce of Lead, and no more—but this contradicts the testimony of Kuffler <note>original: "Kiffleri"; referring to Johann Sibertus Kuffler, a 17th-century chemist and inventor.</note>, as I shall briefly mention: yet another person in that same place believes in the truth and possibility—

->**Things whose reasoning we do not understand, we marvel at;**<-
->**But things which it is a pleasure to know thoroughly, we search into.**<-

But in the realm of Nature, what can a man desire who has fallen from the fountain of Light into the Abyss of Darkness? Especially one whose wisdom in this study of natural Philosophy is sterile and sophisticated. It is characteristic of most of these foolish and inept men to immediately despise a thing once it is understood; but they do not know that perhaps more things are yet to be sought than are already possessed. Therefore, Seneca rightly said in his book *On Morals*:
> You are not yet happy, if the crowd has not mocked you. <note>original: "Nondum felix es, si non te Turba deriserit."</note>

But it matters not to me whether they believe or contradict whatever I write concerning the **Transmutation of Metals**. Meanwhile, I rest well enough content with this one thing: what I have seen with these eyes of mine and done with these hands. Indeed, as the <term>Philosophers</term> <note>In this context, "Philosophers" refers specifically to alchemists or "natural philosophers" who studied the hidden laws of nature.</note> proclaim of themselves, I too have handled with my own hands this spark of eternal Wisdom—namely, the <term>Universal Saturnine Magnesia of the Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>original: "Lapidis Philosophorum Magnesiam Saturninam Catholicam." In alchemy, "Saturnine Magnesia" refers to a primary lead-based substance believed to be the "mother" or "magnet" of the Stone, containing the universal spirit.</note>, as well as the **Fire that pierces rocks**—indeed, a treasure of such great value that it might equal the price of twenty tons of gold. What more do you ask? I believe what I have seen with the "eyes in the fingers" of a <term>Thomas</term> <note>A reference to "Doubting Thomas" from the Bible, who needed to touch physical wounds to believe; Helvetius asserts his belief is based on physical touch and observation.</note>. Namely, that in the nature of things, among the <term>Adepts</term> <note>An "Adept" is a master alchemist who has successfully discovered or received the secret of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> even now in this decrepit age of the world, that most secret **Hyperphysical-Magical Saturn** is possessed, and it is known to none but some <term>Christian Cabalist</term> <note>A "Christian Cabalist" refers to a practitioner who combined Christian theology with Jewish mystical traditions to uncover hidden secrets of nature.</note>. 

And we judge that Physician most blessed to whom this nourishing medical potion of our **Mercury** <note>In alchemy, "Mercury" is not just the liquid metal, but a vital spiritual essence or "First Matter" used for both transmutation and healing.</note> becomes known—the medicine of our son **Aesculapius** <note>The ancient Greek god of healing; here used to signify a perfect medical remedy.</note> against the power of Death, against which no other <term>Panacea</term> <note>A "Panacea" is a legendary universal remedy capable of curing all diseases.</note> grows in gardens. (Deus Optimus Maximus).</note> does not reveal his **Gifts of Solomon** <note>A reference to the wisdom and wealth granted to King Solomon, often associated in alchemy with the mastery over nature’s hidden forces.</note> indiscriminately to all mortals. Furthermore, I might not unreasonably ask, how many of the wisest **philosophers** are so keen-sighted that even with the sharpest edge of their most skilled wit they can grasp by what hidden shadow the **imaginative faculty** <term>imaginative faculty</term> <note>The "imaginative faculty" refers to a 17th-century belief in "maternal imagination," where a pregnant woman’s intense thoughts, fears, or sights could physically mark or "stain" the child in her womb.</note> of a certain pregnant woman, staining things poisonous or monstrous, can perfect its work in a single moment, provided it is triggered into action by some external object?

Moreover, the **stars** are a cause of the matter at hand not to be despised, even if **I** or **You** do not know how to grasp their celestial influences with the mind. Nor even are the **plants** which the earth provides for us to be cast aside, even if **I** or **You** do not know how to judge correctly from their external **signature** <term>signature</term> <note>The "Doctrine of Signatures" was the belief that God marked plants with physical features—like a shape resembling a heart or a liver—to indicate their medicinal use.</note> concerning the effect of the powers ingrained in them, which they remarkably exert by their own potency to heal and preserve human bodies. Is it for that reason that everyone else, to a man, is damaged in their internal **light** and ignorant of all hidden things, just because **I** or **You** lack the knowledge of how the powers created for that same end are to be brought into action, and a thousand other things of that sort?

Although you are ignorant of the splendor in **angels**, the brilliance in the **heavens**, the clarity in the **air**, the transparency in the **waters**, the variety of colors in flowers, the hardness in **stones** and **metals**, the proportion in **animals**, the **Image of God** <note>original: "Imaginem Dei"</note> in regenerated men, **Faith** in believers, and **Reason** in the **Soul**, yet there is a beauty within them such as is perceived and clearly known by very few mortals, etc.

Why indeed should there not be such a wonderful virtue in the **Philosopher's Stone**, which I have indeed seen? Yet I would not wish for anyone to believe that this is my primary goal, as if I wanted to persuade the sons of this age—the worthy as well as the unworthy—to labor in this work; not in the least! ...I warn each and every curious seeker of this **Art** <term>Art</term> <note>In this context, "The Art" refers specifically to Alchemy, the sacred and practical pursuit of transforming matter.</note> to holy abstain from a secret of this kind, which is as dangerous as a **Holy of Holies** <note>original: "Sancto Sanctorum"</note>. Indeed, the student of this **Secret** must carefully beware the reading of, and fellowship with, **Pseudo-philosophers**. But I hope that I have satisfied the curious **Naturalists** or investigators of **Physical Secrets**, provided that for the present I share and make public this description of everything that took place between **ELIAS THE ARTIST** <note>Elias the Artist was a legendary figure in alchemy, a predicted "messiah" of the craft who would appear to reveal the final secrets of the Stone. This **Light** and **Divinity**—so refreshing and lovely—which I have beheld, is something that can never be extinguished or erased from my mind by any forgetfulness, even if it is believed by none of the foolish scholars or the ignorant, illiterate "asses" who do nothing but puff themselves up with a boastful crown of eloquence.

For in this most ulcerated old age of a malignant world, nothing is so safe or secure from the slanders of mockers that it will not be unworthily received and maligned by the ignorance of raging, envious fanatics. However, all such "shadow-dwellers" wander so far from the right path of **Truth** that, in the progress of time, they shall miserably waste away and vanish, entangled in their own errors. Nevertheless, our assertion stands—and shall stand until the very consummation of all ages—built upon the eternal foundation of **Triumphant Truth**, even if this **Art** <term>Art</term> is not yet known to all mortals.

For the **Adepts** <note>In alchemy, an "Adept" is someone who has successfully performed the "Great Work" and created the Philosopher's Stone.</note> assert, by the ancient faith of their experience, that this natural **Mystery** [which many anxious people have sought and requested in the wrong way] is only to be found with **JEHOVAH**, placed "Saturninely" <note>The term "Saturnine" refers to Saturn, which in alchemy represents lead, gravity, and the deep, hidden foundations of the material world. Meanwhile, we declare those men happy who, by the help of the **Art**, take care to learn how they might wash this **Philosophical Queen** <term>Philosophical Queen</term> <note>Alchemical imagery often uses royal figures to represent materials. For it is the nature of good things to be useful to others.*

# Read a true extract from a letter written by Dr. Kuffler. <note>Johannes Sibertus Kuffler (1595–1677) was a prominent chemist and inventor who moved in the circles of the Royal Society.</note>

Kuffler: First, I found in my laboratory a certain *Aqua Fortis* <term>Aqua Fortis: Literally 'strong water,' this is nitric acid, used by alchemists to dissolve and separate metals.</term>. Secondly, I found another in the laboratory of *Charles de Roy*. I poured this *Aqua Fortis* over the calx of the Sun—that is, gold prepared in the common way <note>original: "Solis calcem"; 'Sun' is the alchemical symbol for gold, and 'calx' refers to the fine powder produced when a metal is heated or dissolved and then precipitated.</note>—and after the third cohobation <term>cohobation: A process where a liquid is repeatedly distilled from a solid substance to concentrate its medicinal or transformative power.</term>, it carried up with it the Tincture of Gold into the neck of the retort <note>retort: A glass vessel with a long, curved neck used for distilling chemicals.</note>. I mixed this with silver that had been precipitated in the common way, and I saw that one ounce of this sublimated Tincture of Gold, when placed in a crucible with an ordinary flux <term>flux: A substance added to metal to help it melt and flow more easily.</term>, transmuted one and a half ounces of the two ounces of precipitated silver into the finest gold. A third part of the remaining silver was indeed gold, but it was white and fixed <note>fixed gold: Metal that remains stable and does not evaporate or degrade under the most intense heat of a furnace.</note>; the other two parts were the finest silver, remaining stable through every trial by fire. This is my experience, though afterward we could never find such *Aqua Fortis* again: and I, **HELVETIUS**, saw this gold which was without the usual yellow color—the White Gold.

->*Likewise*<-

Yet another rare example occurred in the year 1664 at The Hague, performed by a certain silversmith <term>Argenti-faber: A worker in silver or a silversmith.</term> named **GRIL**. He used a Spirit of Salt <term>Spirit of Salt: Hydrochloric acid.</term> prepared in an uncommon way to "ripen" **LEAD**, so that from one pound of lead he obtained three parts of the finest silver and two ounces of the most fixed gold.

A certain silversmith at The Hague, a man much practiced as a student of alchemy but (as is the nature of alchemy) a very poor man, requested from a very good friend of mine—the cloth-dyer *Johann Caspar Knöttner*—some Spirit of Salt prepared in an uncommon way. When Knöttner gave it to him, he asked: *Whether he intended to use that Spirit of Salt on metals, or not?* Grill responded: *For metals.* Afterward, he poured this Spirit of Salt over lead which he had placed in a glass dish of the kind normally used for preserves or confections. When a period of two weeks had passed, there appeared to him, floating on the surface, a most curious and splendid silver star, as if it had been drawn with a compass by a most ingenious craftsman. Whereupon Grill, filled with great joy, signaled to us that he

...had already seen the **Signet Star of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Stellam signatam Philosophorum"; this refers to a star-shaped crystalline pattern that forms on the surface of certain metals—especially antimony—during cooling, which alchemists saw as a sign of successful purification.</note>, about which he had perhaps read in the works of **Basil** <note>referring to Basil Valentine, a legendary 15th-century alchemist and author of *The Triumphant Chariot of Antimony*.</note>. I and many other honorable men watched with the greatest wonder as this star floated upon the **Spirit of Salt** <term>Spirit of Salt: An old name for hydrochloric acid.</term>, while in the meantime the lead remained at the bottom, ash-gray in color and swollen like a sponge. However, after seven or nine days had passed in the month of July, the moisture of that Spirit of Salt was consumed and vanished by the intense heat of the air; the star then sank to the bottom and placed itself again upon that spongy, earthy lead. This was a sight worthy of wonder, witnessed by many spectators. 

Finally, that man **Grillus** took a portion of that ashen lead with the adhering star and **cupelled** <term>cupelled: A refining process where metals are heated in a shallow porous cup (a cupel) to separate precious metals like gold and silver from base metals like lead.</term> it under a muffle-test. From one pound of this lead, he found twelve ounces of cupelled **Moon** <note>original: "Lunae"; the alchemical name for silver.</note>, and from these twelve ounces, he further obtained two ounces of the finest **Gold**. 

And I, **Helvetius**, can still show some of this spongy lead with the star still adhering to it, as well as the Silver and Gold made from it, alongside the "leaves" of the star. Because that man Grillus—who was as cunning as he was stubborn—refused to tell **Knôttner** whether he had used his own Spirit of Salt, but instead repeatedly tried to see if he could learn the art of making it from Knôttner himself. After some time had passed, the praised Knôttner forgot which specific kind of Spirit of Salt he had provided (since he was equipped with many different varieties of it), not knowing that Grillus would find the result so quickly. 

In the meantime, Knôttner and his entire family were eventually seized by the plague and died, while the other man [Grillus] drowned in water, exchanging life for death. After the death of both men, no investigator has been able to discover the art of making it as those two had done. 

Certainly, it moves one to wonder that the internal nature of Lead can appear in such a noble external form through the simple maturation by the Spirit of Salt; nor does it soothe the mind with any less wonder that the marvelous **Philosophers' Stone** can transmute metals so swiftly, inasmuch as its power is potentially implanted within it—just as the power in iron is brought into action by the contact of a magnet. But enough of these things for the **Sons of the Art** <note>A traditional term for initiated alchemists or dedicated students of the "Great Work."</note>.

## CHAPTER III.

*Since promises are held to be all the more pleasing the sooner they are fulfilled, I shall return without any delay or detour to the goal I promised for the reporting of my History; of which, let it be understood as follows:*

**A**t The Hague <note>original: "Hagæ Comitis"; the seat of government in the Netherlands.</note>, in my own house, at some hour of the afternoon on the 27th of December <note>original: "VI. Calend. Januar. seu XXVII. Decembris"; Helvetius provides both the Roman calendar and the standard date.</note> in the year of the 1666th year from the salvific birth of Christ, there arrived a certain man. To me, he was entirely unknown, yet he was accompanied by an honest gravity and a serious authority. He was dressed in the simple clothing of the common people, much like a **Mennonite** <note>A member of a Protestant group known for their simple dress and rejection of finery, similar to the Quakers.</note>. He was of medium height, with a somewhat long face that was speckled with several pockmarks <note>original: "morbillorum puncturis"; scars left by smallpox.</note>. His hair was very black, but not at all curly; his chin was beardless, and he appeared to be in about his forty-third or forty-fourth year of age. As far as I could gather by conjecture, he originated from North Holland <note>original: "Batavia Septentrionali, vulgo dicta Nord-Hollandia".</note>.

When the courtesy of our greeting was finished, this new guest, with the greatest reverence, requested that I grant him free access to me. He explained that he had neither wished nor been able to pass by my home, for the sake of the **Art of Fire** <term>Art of Fire: original "Artis Pyrotechnicæ"; a common 17th-century term for chemistry and alchemy, focusing on the transformative power of heat.</term>. He added that he had not only long intended to visit me, perhaps through the helpful service of a friend, but had also read through some of my small Treatises—specifically the one I had published against Sir **DIGBY’S** **Powder of Sympathy** <note>Sir Kenelm Digby (1603–1665) was a famous English courtier and natural philosopher who promoted a "sympathetic powder" said to heal wounds by being applied to the weapon that caused them rather than the wound itself.</note>, and in which I had betrayed my own doubt regarding the **True Philosophical Mystery**. Having seized this "hairy opportunity" <note>An idiom referring to *Occasio*, the goddess of opportunity, who was depicted with a forelock of hair that must be grabbed before she passes.</note>, he then asked me whether I could believe that there still existed in the Nature of Things such a **Great Mystery**, by whose benefit a Physician might be able to universally cure all diseases—unless the patient already suffered from the failure of the lungs, or the liver, or some similar noble and principal organ. To this I responded: "Such a remedy is, for every Physician, especially...

...necessary, but no man knows what and how great the Secrets are that still remain hidden in Nature; nor in my whole life have I ever seen such an <term>Adept</term> <note>A master alchemist who has successfully performed the "Great Work" of creating the Philosophers' Stone.</note>, even though I have read and re-read much in the writings of the **Philosophers** concerning the truth of the matter or the Art. Moreover, I asked him whether he himself, speaking as he did of the **Universal Medicine**, was a physician; but he answered with a denial, declaring that he was nothing but a brass-founder, and that from his youth he had learned many rare sights from a friend. Among these, he specifically learned the method of drawing out medicinal secrets from metals through the torture of fire, and for this reason, he remained even now a lover of that most noble Medicinal Science. 

Furthermore, after many other discourses concerning experiments of fire upon metals, this **ELIAS ARTISTA** <note>Elias the Artist was a legendary figure in alchemy, predicted by Paracelsus to appear and reveal the final secrets of the art.</note> interrupted me, saying: "If you were to see this Supreme Secret [namely the **Philosophers' Stone**] anywhere, would you not recognize it, seeing as you have poured over the writings of various most excellent **Chemists** concerning its substance, color, and wondrous effect?" To which I replied: "Not at all." For although I have read of it in the works of **Paracelsus**, **Helmont**, **Basilius**, **Sendivogius**, and similar existing literary monuments of the <term>Adepts</term>, I nevertheless did not think that the **Philosophical Matter** could be recognized by me—even if I saw it present before my eyes—as to whether it were true or not. 

In the meantime, he drew from his pouch an ivory box most skillfully crafted, in which he possessed three heavy fragments of a good size, almost equal to a small walnut; they were of a glassy color, like pale-yellow Sulfur, to which internal scales of the crucible still adhered, in which this most noble substance had been melted. Its value might perhaps have amounted to twenty tons of gold. 

After I had held that entrusted <term>treasure</term> <note>original: "κειμήλιον" (keimēlion); a precious object or heirloom.</note> of the Stone in these hands of mine for almost a quarter of an hour, and had drunk in from the philosophical mouth of its owner many things worth knowing regarding its wondrous effect upon human and metallic bodies, I returned this **Treasure of Treasures** to the master who possessed it—who had given it to me to handle for such a brief time—with a heart truly most sad and desperately afflicted,

Also, how within a quarter of an hour he could prepare <term>Saffron of Mars</term><note>original Latin: "crocum Martis." A term for iron oxide, used in alchemy both as a pigment and a medicinal remedy for blood-related ailments.</note>, a single dose of which infallibly cures pestilential dysentery; and furthermore a Metallic Liquor, by the help of which within four days he could most certainly cure every kind of <term>Dropsy</term><note>An archaic term for edema, or the accumulation of fluid in the body's tissues.</note>: and also a certain clear Water sweeter than honey, with the aid of which he could extract the Tincture of Garnets, Corals, and all glasses fused by craftsmen within the space of two hours, using only warm sand, and many similar things. I did not observe these nor commit them to memory, because my intention was carried "further beyond" <note>original Latin: "plus ultra."</note>, namely toward the Art of extracting such a noble juice from Metals for the sake of the Metals themselves; but "the shadow in the water snatched the morsel of meat from the dog." <note>This is an allusion to Aesop’s fable; Helvetius is admitting that by focusing on the "greater" goal of making gold, he foolishly overlooked the valuable medical secrets the stranger was sharing.</note> Furthermore, the **ARTIST** told me that his own Master of the Art had asked him to bring a glass full of rainwater, into which he mixed a tiny amount of a very white powder, ordering that I [the disciple of that master continues the story here] should seek from the silversmith one ounce of <term>cupelled silver</term><note>Silver that has been refined and purified of lead and other base metals through intense heating.</note> in thin sheets, which within a quarter of an hour was liquefied like ice in warm water. Then he immediately offered me half of this little draft he had prepared, a kind of drink that tasted not unlike sweet milk, from which I seemed to become very cheerful.

Having related these things, I immediately asked him to what end the other man had done this? Was it perhaps a <term>Philosophical Potion</term><note>Helvetius is asking if the drink was the "Universal Medicine" or "Potable Gold," a substance believed to grant health and longevity.</note>? To which he answered me: "It is not necessary for you to be so curious."

Next, he told me how, by the order of the praised Artist, he had taken down a leaden rainwater box from the wall; and when the lead was newly melted in a pot, that Artist took out a small box full of sulfurous powder from his pouch, a tiny bit of which—as much as would fit on the tip of a knife—he threw into that melted lead. He immediately ordered that the fire be strongly blown by two bellows to stir up a vigorous flame; shortly after, he poured from the pot the finest gold onto the red stones that were in the kitchen.

For if you had at least wrapped your prey in yellow wax, so that it might have been protected from the lead smoke, then it could have penetrated into the depth of the Lead in such a way that it would have transmuted it into Gold. But as it was, a <term>Sympathetic Operation</term><note>original: "Operatio Sympathetica." An alchemical principle where substances react based on natural "sympathies" or attractions; here, the medicine was "attracted" to the rising fumes because it wasn't protected.</note> was performed in the smoke, and so the Medicine, mixed with the smoke, flew away. Indeed, all Gold, Silver, Tin, Mercury, and similar Metals are corrupted by leaden vapors and are likewise rendered into fragile glass." 

During this part of the conversation, I showed him my crucible. While looking at the remaining substance, he discovered a most beautiful saffron-colored Tincture adhering to the walls of the crucible, saying: "Returning to you tomorrow at the ninth hour, I will show you that your Medicine must transmute lead into Gold." In this promise of his, I rested secure. Meanwhile, however...

I earnestly and repeatedly sought information from him as to whether this <term>Philosophical Work</term><note>original: "Opus Philosophicum." Regarding the Matter from which our <term>Secret</term><note>original: "Arcanum." In alchemy, a hidden or miraculous substance or process.</note> is perfected, I wish you to know that only two metals and minerals are given from which it may be prepared; but because the <term>Sulfur</term><note>original: "Sulphur." One of the three primary alchemical principles (with Mercury and Salt), representing the active, masculine, and combustible spirit of a substance.</note> of the Philosophers is found much more abundantly in those minerals, it is therefore fashioned from minerals."

In turn, I asked him: what kind of <term>Solvent</term><note>original: "Menstruum." A technical term for a solvent, derived from the Latin for "monthly," suggesting a natural or rhythmic cycle of dissolution.</note> it was, and whether the operation was performed in glass vessels or in crucibles. He replied: the <term>Solvent</term> is a certain celestial <term>Salt</term><note>original: "Sal." The third alchemical principle, representing the body, stability, and the medium between Sulfur and Mercury.</note>, or one of celestial virtue, by whose benefit the Philosophers dissolve only the earthy metallic body; and by dissolving it, the noble <term>Elixir of the Philosophers</term> is soon drawn out. The operation is perfected in a crucible from start to finish in an open fire: indeed, the whole <term>Work</term> is both begun and fully completed in no longer than four days, and for this whole <term>Work</term>, no more expenses than three florins are spent. And he added that neither the mineral *from which*, nor the salt *through which* it is made, is of great price.

But when I retorted: "My Lord, this is a wonder, for it contradicts the writings of various philosophers, who write that at least seven or nine months must be spent in elaborating this Work"; he replied: "The true writings of the philosophers are understood only by true <term>Adepts</term><note>original: "Adeptis." A person who has successfully discovered the secret of the Philosopher's Stone and mastered the Great Work.</note>. Therefore, they wished to write nothing certain regarding the Time; indeed, no lover of the Art will ever find the art of preparing this <term>Mystery</term><note>original: "Mysterium."</note> without the communication of some true <term>Adept</term>. In respect and regard of which I also ask of you, Friend, that—since you have seen the Matter of the true Work—you do not forget yourself and lose your goods in the fire by gasping after the investigation of this Art; for you will never find it." To which I said: "My Lord, since—although he was as unknown to you as you are unknown to me—he nevertheless showed you the way of finding the operation of this <term>Secret</term>, perhaps you also could notify me of a little something regarding this secret, if you were willing, so that having overcome...

I could perhaps add that once the most difficult basics of all have been discovered—*as the saying goes*—it is perhaps not equally difficult to find one thing based on the occasion of another discovery. But the Artist replied: "In this Work, however, things do not stand thus. For unless you know the matter from the head of the work to its very heel <note>original: "à capite operis ad calcem." An idiom meaning from beginning to end.</note>, you know nothing of it. I have indeed told you enough, yet you are still ignorant of how the glass **Seal of Hermes** <term>Seal of Hermes</term><note>original: "Sigillum Hermetis." A method of hermetically sealing a glass vessel by melting and twisting its neck to make it airtight, essential for containing the volatile "spirits" of the work.</note> of the Philosophers is fashioned and broken open again, in which the **Sun** emits splendor with its wonderfully colored metallic rays, and in which mirror the transmutable **Metals** behold themselves with the eyes of **Narcissus** <note>In alchemical allegory, Narcissus looking into the water represents the metals reflecting their own inner, hidden nature or the "soul" of the metal being revealed in the liquid solvent.</note>, and from what kind of rays the **Adepts** collect their **Fire**, by whose help volatile metals are fixed into the most stable state, whether **Gold** or **Silver**. But for this time, it is enough: because [*God willing*] tomorrow once again there will be an opportunity for meeting, so that we may speak of this **Philosophical Matter**, and as I said, I will come to your house at nine o'clock to show you the **Method of Projection** <term>Method of Projection</term><note>original: "projiciendi Modum." The final stage of the alchemical process where a tiny amount of the Philosopher's Stone is "projected" or cast into a crucible of molten base metal to transform it into gold.</note>." 

But with a farewell for a favorable night, that **ELIAS THE ARTIST** <note>Elias Artista was a legendary figure in 17th-century alchemy, prophesied by Paracelsus as a master who would reveal all secrets of the universe in the final age.</note> left me until today’s dawn, waiting most sadly; indeed, the **Mercury of the Philosophers** flew away with him into the air, for I have heard not even a single word spoken about him since. However, because he [*had promised that he would return to me the following morning or at daybreak*], he sent another unknown man to me at half-past nine, signifying to me that the friend who had promised me on the previous evening that he would see me again had been unable to come because of other distracting business, but that I would be visited by him at three o'clock in the afternoon. 

Furthermore, after I had waited in vain with the most intense longing until half-past seven, I began to doubt the truth of the matter. Moreover, my wife also came to me—a very curious investigator of the praised man's art—vexing me concerning the **Philosophical Art** possessed by that mentioned stern and honest man, saying: "Come now, I beg you, let us test the truth of the Work according to what that man said. For otherwise, I would certainly spend this entire coming night sleepless." To which I replied: "Let us wait, I pray, until tomorrow, to see if perhaps he is yet to return." Meanwhile, however, I ordered my son to light a fire, thinking: "That man, surely, during his discussions at other times..."

by his own divine [works], he is now found guilty of a lie for the first time. For a second time, when I wished to make an experiment using a stolen bit of the material hidden under my thumbnail, it was in vain, because the lead was not transmuted into Gold. Finally, for the third time, he gave such a tiny fragment of the material to touch so large a mass of lead; truly, he led me into a trap <note>original: "in transennam induxit." An idiom meaning to be enticed into a snare or deceived by appearances.</note>. In the meantime, however, I ordered yellow wax to be brought, in which I could wrap the material, and I sought out lead, intending to cut off half an ounce <note>original: "z ß." The symbol for an ounce ($ \mathcal{z} $) with the symbol for half ($ \ss $). Helvetius equates this to 6 drachmas.</note> or 6 drachmas. My wife wrapped the material of the **Stone** in the wax, and as soon as the lead was melted, she herself threw in the pellet. That pellet, with a hissing and bubbling <note>original: "flatuositate." This refers to the release of gases or "spirits" during the chemical reaction.</note> in a well-closed crucible, completed the operation in such a way that within a quarter of an hour the entire mass of lead was transmuted into the best Gold. 

Certainly, even if I had lived in the age of Ovid, I would not have believed in a rarer **METAMORPHOSIS** of the Chemical Art; indeed, if I had inspected it with the hundred eyes of **Argus** <note>In Greek mythology, Argus Panoptes was a giant with a hundred eyes, symbolizing perfect watchfulness.</note>, I would hardly have seen any more admirable Work of Nature. For this Lead, mixed with the **Stone of the Wise** <term>Stone of the Wise</term><note>original: "Lapide Sophorum." A common synonym for the Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold.</note> and melted in the Fire, certainly showed us a most beautiful color—indeed, a most brilliant green. As soon as I poured it into a casting-cup <note>original: "poculum fusorium." A mold used to receive molten metal.</note>, it had taken on a color like blood, but after it had cooled, it glittered with the color of the best Gold. Truly, I and all those standing with me were utterly astonished; immediately, while the gold-made lead was still hot, we hurried away to a **Goldsmith**. After a preliminary examination, he judged it to be the finest Gold of all, better than which none could be found in the whole world, promising that he would pay fifty florins for each of its ounces.

On the day following that event, the rumor of this wonderful Metallic Transmutation was spread and scattered through the whole of our **The Hague**. Wherefore many illustrious men and lovers of the Art came to see me; specifically, among those great names, the General Examiner of the Mints of this Province of Holland, **Lord Porelius**, came to me with several other most illustrious men, earnestly requesting that I share with them at least a minute fragment of my artificial Gold for testing...

...while [testing] it through the legitimate examinations, which I more than willingly performed for the sake of my own curiosity. Together we went to the house of a certain very curious goldsmith named Brechtelius. In his laboratory, the metal was tested through that form of proof which skilled artisans call *Quartation* <term>Quartation: A refining method where gold is alloyed with three parts silver so that acids can better reach and dissolve the impurities.</term>, which is to say, when three or four parts of silver are melted in a crucible with one part of gold, and then this mixture is reduced into thin foils by frequent strikes of the hammer. Over these foils is poured a sufficient quantity of *Strong Water* <note>original: "Aquæ Fortis." This is nitric acid, which dissolves silver but leaves gold untouched.</note>, by which *Strong Water* the silver is dissolved, while the gold seeks the bottom like a black powder; and afterward the *Strong Water* is poured off, and the golden powder is in turn melted in the crucible back into gold.

However, once this work was finished, we thought at the beginning that half of the gold had flown away <note>The researchers initially feared the gold had evaporated or been lost in the chemical reaction.</note>, but in reality, it was the opposite of what we had thought. For we discovered that the gold had additionally transmuted some of the silver into gold; specifically, two drachmas <term>Drachma: A unit of weight; in the apothecaries' system, one drachma is 1/8 of an ounce.</term> of gold had transmuted two scruples <term>Scruple: A small unit of weight; three scruples make one drachma.</term> of silver into gold identical or similar to itself, owing to the abundance of the *Tincture* <note>The 'Tincture' refers to the transformative energy of the Philosopher's Stone, which was thought to be so powerful it could "infect" nearby base metals with the nature of gold.</note>.

Since we doubted whether the silver had perhaps been insufficiently separated from the gold, we immediately made a mixture with seven times as much Antimony <note>Antimony was used in the "Stibium" process to further purify gold, as it consumes all other metals except gold.</note>. After this test in the antimony, we lost eight grains of gold, but when I caused the antimony to evaporate again, I found nine grains of gold again, though of a slightly pale color, so that in the best *Fire Test* <note>original: "Proba Ignis." This likely refers to cupellation, a high-heat process to test the purity of precious metals.</note> we lost nothing of this gold. I performed this infallible kind of testing three times, and in the presence of most noble and illustrious men, I found that every drachma of gold had acquired for itself a scruple of gold as an increase, while the silver remained excellent and very flexible. Thus, five drachmas of gold had further attracted five scruples to themselves from the silver; and [to wrap up all the remaining details at once] the total weight of the quantity of that praised, tiny powder transmuted six drachmas and two scruples of the viler metal into gold so "fixed" <note>In alchemy, a "fixed" metal is one that is stable and does not evaporate or degrade when exposed to intense heat.</note> that it was able to endure even the most intense torture of the fire with perseverance. *Behold!* Thus have I recounted the entire history to you so far, from the very beginning <note>original: "ab ovis." Literally "from the eggs," a Latin idiom meaning from the very start of the story.</note>.

## CHAPTER IV.

->*So that I may now fulfill the duty of my promise, I will turn immediately to the Dialogue or Colloquy between ELIAS THE ARTIST and the DOCTOR.*<-

### ELIAS THE ARTIST.

**G**reetings, Master Helvetius! Unless my presence proves a nuisance to you, a desire has come upon me to converse with you for a little while, for I have heard that you are a curious investigator of natural things. Indeed, I have read through your little books, and above all the entire small Treatise written against the effect of Mr. Digby's Sympathetic Powder <term>Sympathetic Powder: A form of "magical" medicine popularized by Sir Kenelm Digby, which was claimed to heal wounds when applied to the blood-stained clothing of the injured person rather than the wound itself.</term>, where he boasts that he wishes to heal all wounds without regard to distance. Certainly, I am incredibly delighted by those things which are seen in this "Mirror of Creatures" <note>Elias refers to the natural world as a mirror reflecting God's work.</note> implanted by nature, whether they be sympathetic <term>Sympathetic: In 17th-century science, "sympathy" referred to a natural attraction or connection between objects.</term> or antipathetic <term>Antipathetic: A natural repulsion or opposition between substances.</term>. Indeed, we are best able to know the inexhaustible treasures of the divine Light and Spirit—conceded to us no less abundantly than liberally—from all the Creatures which are produced for this same end, whether they are born under the ethereal sky, in the belly of the Earth, or in the womb of the sea: namely, that by their own potentially indwelling benefits, they may restore health to the mortal body of men.

### T H E  P H Y S I C I A N.

Oh Sir! The presence of such a new and visiting guest will never be a bothersome shadow to me, but rather the most welcome of friends. For philosophical conversation about the Secrets of Nature is the unique recreation of my mind, as well as such a suitable, life-giving nourishment that no man can worthily taste it before he has been properly prepared for that banquet. Please, friend, enter the chamber.

### T H E  A R T I S T  E L I A S.

Is it so, Sir! Here, as it seems to me, you have an entire workshop of Vulcan <note>original: "Vulcaniam officinam," referring to Vulcan, the Roman god of fire and metalworking; here, it means an alchemical or chemical laboratory</note>, and perhaps all these things have been drawn forth spagyrically <term>spagyrically: related to spagyrics, a branch of alchemy focused on medicine, emphasizing the separation and recombination of "pure" essences</term> and precisely through the torture of Fire <note>original: "Ignis tortura," a common alchemical term for the intense, prolonged heat used to break down mineral substances</note> from the Mineral Kingdom: but for what purpose, I ask, are so many medicines? I believe that God, in the nature of things, naturally provides such medicines that we might be able to restore the weakened and prostrate health of man much more quickly and safely with very few of them—unless the disease is either lethal due to a defect of Nature, or there is a putrefaction of some injured noble internal organ, or a total consumption of the radical moisture <term>radical moisture: "humidum radicale," a historical physiological concept of a vital, innate fluid that fuels the body's life-force</term>. In such desperate cases, no Galenic cure <note>referring to the traditional medicine of Galen, which relied on balancing the four bodily humors</note> or Paracelsian tincture <note>referring to the chemically-based medicine of Paracelsus, which used minerals and "essences"</note> can provide a remedy. Yet in ordinary diseases it is not so; where, nonetheless, not infrequently most men—may there be no retribution for the saying <note>original: "absit Nemesis dicto," a Latin idiom used to ward off bad luck or divine anger when making a bold statement</note>—must of necessity migrate from the bountiful Kingdom of this sweetest Light into the shadowy land of the dead before their destined end of life, while they either neglect the health of their body or commit it to the trust of Physicians who are unskilled in the most immediate remedy.

As far as I understand from your Lordship's discourse, you yourself, unless I am mistaken in my reasoning, are either a Physician or skilled in Chemistry. Indeed, just as you said, Sir, I believe that in the Nature of Things other more excellent medicines are given—just as several other Philosophers assert—that there is something given, although known to few,

## T H E  P H Y S I C I A N.

My friend, I would willingly grant this: that God sells that praised Good, just like all other gifts, to His sons for nothing; however, you rarely hear that He has sold, or does sell, this medicinal wine of Nectar to His sons for nothing. ...in short, to ascend the summits of those same mountains, where one may feed upon the Ambrosia and Nectar of the Great Sages <note>original: "Macrosophorum," a term combining Greek roots for 'great' and 'wise,' referring to the legendary masters of alchemy</note>.

In the meantime, it is the duty of a good Physician—if he ever finds himself lacking such a Universal Elixir <term>Universal Elixir: the supreme alchemical medicine, or Philosopher's Stone in liquid form, believed to cure all ailments</term>—that he, not without a constant endeavor to preserve a pure and sound conscience, should apply to the diseases of the sick entrusted to his care such treatments or remedies for restoring health as he has certainly discovered, by reason of their effect, to possess the power of healing.

Therefore, in even the most desperate diseases, I, along with most Practitioners, have always used such very simple Medicaments so that the suffering might quickly recover or be restored to their former state of health, or even a better one.

For indeed, various and diverse types of Salts <note>In 17th-century medicine, "salts" were seen as one of the three primary building blocks of matter (alongside sulfur and mercury) that could cause disease if they became imbalanced or "corrosive"</note> are produced in the glands and lymphatic vessels after the putrefaction of this or that ingested food; these later bloom in various humors <term>humors: the four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) believed to control health and temperament</term>, leading to different diseases, whether internal or external. For as experience teaches, there are as many varieties of diseases as there are constitutions or temperaments of human bodies; they are subject to these diversities even if the disease is of one and the same kind. This is proven to us by daily interaction with those drinking Wine together, from which clearly diverse effects manifest themselves.

For instance, **P E T E R**, as soon as he drinks Wine, is prone to a wrathful—not to say furious—spirit.

Conversely, **P A U L**, when drinking wine, seems to have imbibed a lamb-like <note>original: "agninam," meaning sheep-like or gentle</note> timidity of soul.

**M A T T H I A S** truly sings, and **L U K E** weeps.

Concerning the Scurvy Contagion <note>original: "Contagio Veneno Scorbutico." In this era, scurvy was often viewed as a "poison" or "acid" in the blood rather than a nutritional deficiency</note>: specifically, **P E T E R's** radical juice <note>original: "succus radicalis," the fundamental life-sustaining fluid or "radical moisture" of the body</note> in the lymphatic vessels and glands is converted into an obstructing Acid <note>original: "Acidum oppilans," an acid that clogs or blocks the body's internal passages</note> that blocks all the passages and organs of the entire body. From this, blue and discolored spots arise under the skin of the arms and feet; during a time of plague, however, these swellings appear like peppercorns.

->*The same of*<-

The juice of **Paul's** parts <note>These "parts" or categories named after Apostles likely refer to a specific diagnostic system used by the author to classify different metabolic temperaments or "signatures" of disease.</note> is changed into a **Bitter** aperitive <term>aperitive: a substance used in 17th-century medicine to "open" the pores or vessels to clear obstructions</term>: from which there arise under the skin red spots on the arms and feet, mimicking the bites of fleas; but in the plague, they become Carbuncles <note>original: "Anthraces," referring to the dark, ulcerated sores characteristic of the plague</note>.

The juice of **Matthias's** parts is converted into something slightly sweet and easily putrefied: from which there sprout under the skin watery tumors of the arms and feet, almost such as you might see in those suffering from Dropsy <note>original: "Hydropicis," a condition of swelling caused by excess fluid</note>; but in the Pestilence, these become pestilential tumors.

The juice of **Luke's** parts is changed into a Sharp, Salty, and drying substance; from which there come about under the skin of the arms and feet precipitations of the ordinary ferment of the flesh, and drying-outs, just as usually happens in Atrophy <term>Atrophy: a wasting away of the body or its tissues</term>, indeed most often in true Atrophy; but in the plague, the most burning Buboes <note>original: "Bubones," the swollen lymph nodes associated with bubonic plague</note> arise, accompanied by madness even unto death.

Behold, Friend, no physician can cure the evil of this Scorbutic <term>Scorbutic: relating to scurvy, which in this era was viewed as a broad category of diseases caused by "salt" imbalances in the blood</term>, Pestilential, or Febrile poison through a single Universal Medicine, but rather through the mediation of a certain Particular vegetable or Mineral remedy granted to us by God in Nature. For indeed, with a single scorbutic herb such as Scurvy-grass <note>original: "Cochlearia"</note> or Sorrel <note>original: "Acetosa"</note>, or Fumitory <note>original: "Fumaria"</note> or Brooklime <note>original: "Beccabungia"</note>—and much less with a remedy fused into one from these different species—can I helpfully relieve or treat all those suffering from scurvy; because between the herbs Scurvy-grass and Sorrel there exists an Antipathy <note>original: "Antipathia," a concept in early medicine where certain substances or forces naturally oppose and cancel each other out</note>, just as between Fire and Water: and so the same Antipathy flashes between the herb Fumitory and Brooklime. Therefore:

The corrective for **Peter's** variety of the staining, salty-acid Scorbutic poison is made with the Bitter volatile Salt of the herb Scurvy-grass.

The corrective for **Paul's** variety of the staining, salty-bitter Scorbutic poison is made with the fixed acid Salt of the herb Sorrel.

The corrective for **Matthias's** variety of the slightly sweet and moistening salty-staining Scorbutic poison is made with the help of the bitter, drying fixed sulfur of the herb Fumitory.

## ELIAS THE ARTIST.

Everything you have discussed, I would easily concede; however, very few Physicians use this method of healing. Yet, in the meantime, it is not impossible that in the **Mineral Kingdom** <note>Alchemists divided the world into the Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral Kingdoms; the Mineral was considered the most potent and "fixed"</note> there is also a supreme **Universal Medicine**, by the benefit of which alone we might be able to prepare and administer everything that you have related to me regarding the many various remedies from the lowly **Vegetable Kingdom**. And yet, God, the Best and Greatest, for several weighty reasons, has not granted this most magnificent gift of superior knowledge to all philosophers indiscriminately, but has revealed it to only a very few—so much so that the **Adepts** <term>Adepts: those who have successfully discovered the secret of the Philosopher's Stone</term> to a man all confess with one voice that the Science is true, and its truth is in no way to be doubted.

## THE PHYSICIAN.

These are based partly on the age and strength of the person, and partly on their sex and other circumstances. One must distinguish between the delicate and the robust (whether by nature or upbringing), between male and female, between a young man and a maiden, or between the beginning, middle, or end of a disease. One must also discern whether the disease is deep-seated and old, or whether it has only very recently attacked the patient; or finally, whether the **Ferment** <note>original: *Fermentum*; early medicine viewed disease as a process of "fermentation" or souring of the body's humors</note> is being promoted in this disease, or is being cast down in another. And unless these corrupt humors are immediately expelled from the body without any delay through Nature’s ordinary drainage channels <term>emunctoria: the organs or pathways, such as the skin, kidneys, or bowels, that carry waste out of the body</term>—whether by the bowels, the urine of the bladder, the sweating pores, the saliva of the mouth, or the nostrils—surely the corruption of one thing will become the generation of another; namely, a disease. For from any spark, unless you extinguish it in time, a great fire will arise. Moreover, if a failure in the movement of the vital Spirits occurs, it is impossible for this [healing] to happen. Therefore, the conscientious Physician must take care of one thing above all: how he might promote the Spirit-

### THE ARTIST.

Not in the least, sir. Indeed, such great power has never been granted to any Medicine that it might be able to change the nature of man. For truly, intoxicating wine taken by various individuals does not change the nature of man in the drunkard, but only provokes that which is naturally and potentially within him, and brings into action what was as if dead within him. The operation of the **Universal Medicine** <term>Universal Medicine: Also known as the Philosopher's Stone or the Elixir, believed by alchemists to cure all diseases and prolong life</term> functions in the same way, for by the refreshing of the **Vital Spirits** <term>Vital Spirits: In the medical theory of the time, these were subtle substances that carried life and sensation through the body</term> it provokes health that was only suppressed for a time in the man—health that had previously existed there naturally. It is just as the heat of the Sun does not change herbs or flowers, but at least provokes them, and calls them back into action out of their own potential nature. For a man of a **melancholic** <note>Associated with black bile; a temperament characterized by being somber, analytical, or prone to sadness</note> temperament is restored again to his melancholic affairs, while a **Jovial** <note>Associated with the planet Jupiter; a temperament characterized by cheerfulness and optimism</note> and merry man is refreshed in his joyful actions, and so on. 

And it is a most immediate or excellent preservative in all desperate diseases. Hence, one who senses that some adversity is about to happen to him <note>Referring to the onset of illness</note> prefers to prevent it rather than be prevented by it. Furthermore, if any prolongation of life were granted through some **Philosophical Medicine** <note>The alchemical Elixir of Life</note> against the fated predestination of Almighty God, then certainly **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>original: "Mercurius Trismegistus"; the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the founder of alchemy</note>, nor **Paracelsus** <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a famous Swiss physician and alchemist</note>, nor **Ramon Llull** <note>original: "Raymundus Lullius"; a 13th-century polymath to whom many alchemical texts were attributed</note>, nor **Count Bernard** <note>original: "Comes Bernhardus"; likely Bernard Trevisan (1406–1490), a famous Italian alchemist</note>, nor many similar illustrious possessors of this **Great Mystery** <term>Great Mystery: Latin "Mysterium Magnum," a term used to describe the ultimate secret of the alchemical art</term> would have met the common death of all other mortals; but perhaps they would have prolonged their lives even to this very day. Therefore, it would be the mark of a fanatic or a madman to write this—and indeed the mark of the most foolish person to believe and feel the same—concerning any single one of the medicines in the whole nature of things.

# THE PHYSICIAN.

Whatever you have said, my friend, concerning the operation of the **Universal Medicine** <term>Universal Medicine: The highest goal of alchemy, also known as the Philosopher's Stone, capable of curing all illness and transmuting base metals into gold</term>—and you have spoken no less regally than fundamentally—I would joyfully and willingly concede. However, as long as I labor in ignorance of the correct way to prepare it, I am doing nothing more than one who, wishing to play with a small boat on a tiny pond, is cast out into the vast Ocean; he will certainly be driven back to the shore without any fruit for his efforts. For although many illustrious men have written something about that praised Preparation, they have nevertheless wrapped it in such a sail of shadowy caution, so to speak, that their tracks (though hiddenly demonstrated) have become known to very few diligent readers—tracks which were to be followed only until one reached the destination they desired. Furthermore, how few people are equipped with such funds that they can buy for themselves all those books in which this sort of **Hypothesis** <note>In this context, the theoretical framework or secret formula of alchemy</note> is treated in such a scattered way? One would consume the greatest part of a short life in reading them before gathering sufficient knowledge and practical experience. Let us remain, therefore, in our Laboratory, which is also blessed by God, according to the saying:

> Pray and Work; and God gives in every hour.
> <note>original Latin: "Ora ac Labora; & Deus dat omni hora." This was a famous motto of the Benedictine monks and later adopted by alchemists to show that success required both spiritual devotion and physical labor.</note>

You argue correctly enough, sir; for this **Art of Arts** <note>Alchemy</note> is very rarely learned from the writings of the Philosophers alone. But let us move on from this topic to the Metallic Transmutative Effect of this most noble **Tincture** <term>Tincture: A potent alchemical substance used to "tinge" or transform the internal nature of a metal</term>. Regarding this, many Partners or Adepts have written many, many books. Most of their genuine disciples, laboring long in the **Fire** <note>The physical work at the alchemical furnace</note>, have reached the desired end of their **Secret** <note>original: "Arcani"</note> with, as they say, **white birds**. <note>original: "albis avibus." An ancient Latin proverb meaning "under a lucky star" or with great success and good omens.</note>

# THE PHYSICIAN.

Now what shall I do, my Lord? If perhaps, because of your solemn Philosophical Oath, it is not permitted for you to give me that small piece of the wonderful **Tincture** <term>Tincture: In alchemy, a potent substance or "medicine" capable of transforming base metals into gold or curing all diseases.</term>, you should certainly know that—just as you suspect—I am anxious in spirit and earnestly eager to drink in this most noble Science. Indeed, I believe that even the first Patriarch of the world, Adam himself—who was once banished from Paradise for eating the apple of dual wisdom <note>original: "utriusque Sophiæ malum"; a reference to the fruit of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.</note>—if he were still alive in our age, would not hesitate to want to eat once more of this golden apple from the garden of **ATLAS** <term>Atlas: In mythology, Atlas guarded the Garden of the Hesperides which grew golden apples; alchemists used this as a metaphor for the secret "apples" or stages of the Great Work.</term>.

Your Lordship says, *“That many Princes have not been able to see what I have seen.”* I have indeed seen the Matter about which you preach such rare things, yet in the meantime, I have not witnessed the Transmutative Effect, except by placing my faith in your words. Since your Lordship comforts me by saying that you will now depart, but will return to me after an interval of three weeks to demonstrate the most beautiful **Chemical Arts** as well as the **projection** <term>Projection: The final step in alchemy where the Philosopher's Stone is "projected" or cast onto molten base metal (like lead) to instantly turn it into gold.</term>, if it be permitted, I shall acquiesce for now in the enjoyment of this good hope. Meanwhile, I give you my greatest thanks for the immense friendship you have shown me, and for your singular care in warning me so that I might not pour out and squander my reputation and all my fortunes upon Chemical Labors, only to lose them.

Certainly, I have never yet made trial of such difficult things, nor am I about to attempt them, unless your Lordship first wishes to show me the way and method of preparation freely and out of pure benevolent friendship. Meanwhile, I truly admire the Truth of the Art, and I congratulate myself on the account of your proven friendship toward me, since you have revealed this to me: that you are an **ADEPT** <term>Adept: A person who has successfully achieved the "Great Work" and discovered the secret of the Philosopher's Stone.</term>.

For if a King, or a Prince, or any of the other Great Lords should know or find out that you are the possessor of this Art, and should therefore [which God forbid!] seize you for interrogation,

## THE ARTIST.

I have never shown the **Philosophers' Stone** <term>Philosophers' Stone: The legendary substance of alchemy capable of transmuting base metals into gold and acting as a universal medicine.</term> to anyone else, nor revealed myself as its possessor, except to one certain honest and just old man, as well as to you; but no human being must ever see or hear of such a thing hereafter. Indeed, even if any King or Prince were to cast me into chains (which I truly hope my God will not easily permit), I would by no means be willing to betray the **Art** to them, whether directly or indirectly—unlike those street-peddling doctors, druggists, vagabond impostors, or impoverished alchemists. Instead, I would prefer to be flayed, tortured, and put to death by the most savage torment of the rack and live coals.

## THE PHYSICIAN.

Good friend, are there any authors who write more clearly about the truth of this **Art** than all those many others, who belch out such obscure words about it? Perhaps they do not even understand those words themselves, unless they use the commentaries and notes of more obvious paraphrasers; just as you, perhaps, have read through them after the fact, and therefore know best of all who the true **Adepts** <term>Adepts: Those who have successfully mastered the Great Work of alchemy and produced the Stone.</term> are.

## THE ARTIST.

Lord Doctor, I do not read many books, nor have I read through many; yet among other authors, I have not found one more diligent than **SENDIVOGIUS** <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636) was a famous Polish alchemist and courtier.</note>, specifically in the book titled *Cosmopolita* <note>original: "Cosmopolita"; a widely read alchemical treatise titled "The Cosmopolitan."</note>, or in Dutch, **CITIZEN OF THE WORLD**. Likewise, Brother **BASILIUS** in his **Twelve Keys** <note>Referring to Basil Valentine, a legendary figure whose "Twelve Keys" describe the stages of the alchemical process.</note>. As far as **SENDIVOGIUS** is concerned, you shall have the use of this author as soon as I return, just as I said: for within his obscure words the truth lies hidden, just as...

### THE PHYSICIAN.

I give you the greatest thanks, Lord, for such great friendship. In the meantime, I will wait for whatever you have promised; and I easily agree with and grant what your Lordship has explained regarding the Objects of the Tincture, as one who believes that wonderful and effective Essences of Metals are hidden beneath the external rinds and husks of Bodies, although I find very few so practiced and experienced in Fire that they know how to shell the nut according to the dictate of the **Art**. Indeed, every external and robust Body of any Animal, Vegetable, or Mineral is like such a terrestrial Province into which—as *Isaac Hollandus* <note>Johannes Isaac Hollandus and his son Isaac were semi-legendary Dutch alchemists, likely writing in the 15th century, whose works were highly influential in the 17th century.</note> has written—noble Essences spiritually immigrate. Therefore, it is necessary that the sons of the **Art** know how they might, through a certain suitable saline Ferment <note>original: "Fermentum salinum"; a chemical agent used to trigger a transformation or "leaven" a metal.</note> pleasing to the Metallic nature, subdue, dissolve, separate, and concentrate not only the magnetic Virtue of Metallic dyeing, but also how they might be able to multiply the same in a philosophical manner within its own homogeneous Gold or Silver. For we see that the Bodies of all creatures are not only easily destroyed, but also immediately, as soon as the internal parts cease to live, they are snatched into Orcus <note>original: "Orcum"; a reference to the classical underworld, used here to represent a state of primal chaos or the "abyss" of unformed matter.</note> and ancient darkness, in which they lay hidden before they were brought into the light through the creation of God the Creator. But how few men are there who will demonstrate this **Art** to us in the Metallic Kingdom?

In almost the same way, a chick is produced from the white of an egg through natural heat. So also, from the seminal bond of life of some *Metal*, a new and more noble *Metal* is made, through the heat of a Saline fire suited to its nature; although very few *Chemists* know rightly and perfectly how the internal, ever-moving magnetic powers of *Metals* are described according to their own harmony or discrepancy; or why this *Metal* should have such a singular *Sympathy* or *Antipathy* with another *Metal*.
