### Marcellus Palingenius in *The Zodiac of Life*, Book 9.
<note>Marcellus Palingenius Stellatus was the pen name of a 16th-century Italian poet whose work *Zodiacus Vitae* combined scientific knowledge with moral philosophy and theology.</note>

Great Father of the Gods, Supreme Power of the World,
Than whom nothing can exist nor be imagined greater; standing
Far from all bodily mass, yet shaping all
Bodies—those entirely unknown to change, and those which,
Broken by the long circuit of time, fall into decay:
Beginning without beginning, the Fountain from which every kind
Of Good flows forth, Ruler and Author of Nature,
Comprehending all things, yet comprehended by none.
Immense Majesty, Goodness, Wisdom, Life,
Order, Beauty, End, Mind, Truth, Light, Way, Virtue:
Dwelling nowhere, yet dwelling everywhere: Immovable, yet giving
Constant motion to All: from whom all things, and into whom
All things, through whom also all things exist: remaining always 
In the same condition, unchangeable through any age:

The Greatest of Causes, who, revolving the starry mass
By a fixed law, governs the decrees of fate;
King of Kings, before whom a thousand stand, and a thousand
Hosts of joyful Gods <note>original: "Divorum," here referring to the angelic beings depicted in the diagram.</note> serve and sing hymns
In the fields of Infinite Light, beyond the outermost 
Walls of the World, where is the most fit seat for true things:
I worship You, I venerate You, I now reverently adore You
And pray as a suppliant that You might deign to look upon me
With a kindly Face, and hear the voice of one praying.
Send the rays of Your Light to me, drive away the darkness
Of a mind [alas] too much oppressed in a dying body,
Grant me to find the right path, lest harmful Error,
Vain belief, and blind Opinion drag me
Headlong into the rough places of things and the contagions of Life.

For without You, mortal talent and human virtue,
While it hopes to lift itself from the ground, just as Icarus once did, 
Falls with its frame pulled apart and its feathers loosened:
Nor is it able without You to see the inner chambers
Of hidden Truth, nor by what part or art salvation may be sought.
Bestow therefore upon me, O most worthy King of Kings,
That I may know You, and please You: then that I may know myself—
What I am, for what cause I was produced on Earth, and from where
I came here, and finally to where I shall go when life is finished:
What I must do while I live: and what must be avoided:
So that when Lachesis <note>One of the three Fates of mythology, the "allotter" who measured the thread of life.</note> has finished my threads, and the final 
Day has hidden these exhausted limbs in the tomb,
Death may become a welcome rest to me, and a harbor of salvation.

### Author of the *Handbook of Restored Physics*. Canon 1 and following.

> **§. 1.** God is the Eternal Being, Infinite Unity, and the Radical Principle of all things: Whose Essence is Immense Light; Whose Power is Omnipotence; Whose Will is Perfect Good; and Whose Command is an absolute Work. For those desiring more, there occur only wonder, silence, and the Abyss of the deepest Glory. **§. 2.** Many of the wise have held that the World was described from Eternity in its <term>Archetype</term> <note>The original divine 'blueprint' or idea of the world existing in the mind of God.</note>. However, the Archetype itself, which is entirely Light, was folded within itself before the Creation of the Universe; like a book, it shone for itself alone. But in the production of the World, it opened and unfolded itself as if in labor, and made manifest its Work—previously hidden in the Mind as if in a womb—by a certain extension of itself. Thus, it led out the Ideal World into an actual and material one, like a doubled Image of Divinity. *Trismegistus* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy.</note> confirms this when he relates that God changed His form, and the Universe was suddenly revealed and converted into Light: for the World is nothing else than the visible Image of the hidden Divinity. The Ancients seem to have understood this origin of the Universe through their **Pallas** <note>The goddess Athena.</note> emerging from the brain of **Jove** <note>Jupiter/Zeus.</note> by the help of **Vulcan**, namely, by the power of Fire or Divine Light. **§. 3.** The Eternal Parent of things, no less Wise in ordering than Powerful in creating, arranged the organic mass of the World into such a noble order that the highest things are intermingled with the lowest, and the lowest with the highest, without confusion, and are similar through a certain analogy. Whence the Extremes of the entire Workmanship, by a certain secret bond, cohere most strictly among themselves through invisible means, and all things spontaneously consent to the obedience of the supreme moderator. And for the benefit of lower Nature, they will allow themselves to be dissolved only by the command of Him who bound them. Rightly, therefore, did *Hermes* affirm that that which is below is similar to that which is above. **§. 4.** He who transfers the supreme right of the Universe to a Nature other than the Divine Nature denies God: for it is not lawful to acknowledge any other divine power in created Nature, either in producing or in preserving the individuals of this expanded Machine, except that Divine Spirit of the Creator which brooded over the first waters and led the confused seeds of things in Chaos from potentiality into Act. Once led out, He turns them through the constant wheel of alteration, treating these lower things geometrically by composing and resolving them.

->**George Ripley's Prologue to the Twelve Gates.**<-
<note>George Ripley (c. 1415–1490) was a famous English alchemist. His "Compound of Alchemy," also known as the "Twelve Gates," uses the metaphor of a castle with twelve gates to describe the chemical processes of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

**O** Incomprehensible Light! Glorious in Majesty, the brightness of whose rays dazzles our eyes. **O Unity in substance and Triple in Deity.** <note>A reference to the Christian Trinity—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—which alchemists often compared to the three principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury.</note> The joyful glorification of the heavenly jubilee. O merciful purification of souls and pure perpetuation, You who kindly snatch us from occurring dangers, and bring us from this turbulent valley of vanity into heaven. O power and wisdom, O unexplainable Kindness, sustain me daily, and be my Governor, so that my life may never displease You. O Excellent Casket, abounding in every Treasure, You are the one from whom all Goodness flows most generously to Men and to every creature, etc. *In the beginning* when You created all things out of Nothing—a spherical and dark work from confused <term>Chaos: the disorganized state of matter before the creation of the universe; in alchemy, it refers to the "First Matter" that the chemist must refine</term>—it was fashioned by Your authorship, not without a Miracle, containing within itself all things mixed together. This was separated over the space of Six days, as Genesis openly testifies. Then Heaven and Earth were made by Your Word, Your Will, and Your Power. From one confused mass were created all things that now exist. But Before that, You were in Glory as the Creator. Now also You Are, and You shall be without doubt. And purified souls shall come upward to Your Blessedness. 

This Beginning can be one and the same for the Declaration of our Blessed Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone.</note>. For just as all things were created from one mass, so in our <term>practice: the actual laboratory work of alchemy</term> this very thing must be; for all our secrets arise from One Image. In the Books of the philosophers, for anyone who wishes to see, our Stone is called the <term>Microcosm: the "little world," signifying that the Stone contains the same proportions and powers as the entire universe</term>, One and Three, <term>Magnesia: a symbolic name for the raw material of the Stone</term>, and also <term>Sulphur and Mercury: the active/fiery and passive/fluid principles of matter</term> proportioned by Nature.

### THE EMERALD TABLET OF HERMES.

**T**rue, without falsehood, certain and most true: That which is below is like that which is above, and that which is above is like that which is below, to accomplish the miracles of the One Thing. <note>This is the most famous axiom in alchemy, suggesting that the patterns of the stars and the heavens are mirrored in the laboratory and the human soul.</note> And just as all things were from One, by the mediation of the One: so all things were born from this One Thing by adaptation. Its father is the Sun, its mother the Moon. The Wind carried it in its belly. Its nurse is the Earth. The father of all the perfection <term>telesmi<gloss>derived from the Greek 'telesmos,' meaning completion, ritual, or perfection</gloss></term> of the whole world is here. Its power is complete if it be turned into earth. You shall separate the earth from the fire, the subtle from the gross, gently and with great ingenuity. It ascends from the Earth to Heaven, and again it descends to the Earth, and receives the power of the higher and the lower things. Thus you have the glory of the whole world. Therefore all obscurity shall flee from you. This is the strong fortitude of all fortitude, because it will overcome every subtle thing and penetrate every solid thing: THUS THE WORLD WAS CREATED. From this shall come wonderful adaptations, the method of which is this. Therefore I am called Hermes Trismegistus <note>Hermes "The Thrice-Greatest," the legendary founder of alchemy.</note>, having three parts of the philosophy of the whole world. What I have said concerning the operation of the Sun is complete.
